Name: Alkaline selection box
Description:
Are you an exotic fruit lover that likes to stay on an alkaline diet? Our alkaline selection is just the poduct for you.
Each of our alkaline selection boxes are unique, packed on a daily basis according to what's available and in season. The actual box you recieve will differ to the the ilustrative image used. We use the following produce in our alkaline selection boxes;
Avocado
Apples
Key limes, seeded
Dates
Sour oranges
Sweet oranges
Sweet tamarind
Sour tamarind
Drinking coconuts
Burro bananas
Apple bananas
Papaya
Pears
Mangoes
Melons
Cactus figs
Alkaline fruits have low acidity levels. Whilst most fruits are considered alkaline, there are some that have an especially high pH - the pH scale runs from 0-14, where foodstuffs with a pH level of 0-6 are classed as acidic (0 being the most), and those in the 8-14 range are classed as alkaline; 7 is neutral and considered the ideal pH level of the body. Indeed, navigating an alkaline diet can be difficult because even fruits that we consider acidic still have an alkaline effect on the body. For example, lemons and limes have a rather acidic pH, yet they actually have an alkalizing effect on the body. This is why we've made this bespoke selection box - you can buy this knowing you'll receive truly alkaline fruits and vegetables.
Alkaline diets have become very popular in recent years, gaining celebrity followers such as Victoria Beckham, Jennifer Aniston, and Gwyneth Paltrow, because eating alkaline foods is considered vital for maintaining pH balance in the body - in other words, it is believed that alkaline fruits can effectively neutralize the very high acid levels (scored at 2 on the pH scale) in the stomach.

Name: Dragon fruit selection box
Description:
Love dragon fruit? We have just the thing for you!
Our dragon fruit selection boxes are the best way to try all three different varieties of the hylocereus undatus family! A small dragon fruit box includes 1 of each variety, and a large dragon fruit box includes 3 of each!
Red dragon
The flesh of the red dragon fruit is sweeter than white flesh varieties and has a beautiful vibrant red to purple colour.
The texture and taste can be compared to kiwi and melon!
Red dragon fruit offers an array of health benefits. They are a good source of magnesium and contain beneficial plant compounds like polyphenols, carotenoids and betacyanins.
White dragon
Dragon fruit are spectacularly beautiful. The fuschia-pink peel is covered by sporadic green tipped scales and the striking white flesh inside is dotted with countless edible black seeds.
The flavour is slightly sweet and refreshing, somewhat like melon and kiwi, in texture and taste.
Dragon fruit are rich in vitamin c and dietary fibre.
Yellow pitahaya
Yellow pitahaya are ripe when the thick scaly skin is golden yellow. They grow on cactus plants and unusually, the flowers only bloom at night.
The juicy translucent flesh is dotted with countless black seeds and is deliciously sweet!
Due to their appearance, they are often known by the nickname, yellow dragonfruit.

Potatoes are a staple of many people's diet, and for good reason. Delicious, hearty, and nutritious, they are one of the most versatile ingredients and can please even the fussiest eaters!

Whether baking, boiling, mashing, chipping, or roasting, making crispy hasselback potato gratins or delectable gnocchi... the list is endless!

Whatever you choose, the result will be an appetizing and healthy delight!

Name: Apple - fuji
Description:
Fuji is one of the most attractive modern apple varieties!
The Fuji apple is an apple hybrid developed by growers at Tohoku Research Station in Fujisaki, Aomori, Japan in the late 1930s. It originated as a cross between two American apple varieties - the Red Delicious and old Virginia Ralls Genet apples.
Fuji apples are typically round and range from large to very large, averaging 75 mm in diameter.
They contain between 9-11% sugars by weight and have a dense flesh that is sweeter and crisper than many other apple cultivars, making them popular with consumers around the world.
In Japan, Fuji apples continue to be an unrivaled best-seller. Japanese consumers prefer the crispy texture and sweetness of Fuji apples almost to the exclusion of other varieties!

Name: Apple - meigetsu (luxury fruit for gifting)
Description:
Japanese apples arent like just any other apple, they are rare treats!
Meaning beautiful moon in Japanese, Meigetsu apples are a premium variety from the gunma prefecture in Japan traditionally given as gifts to friends and family or anyone who appreciated perfect fruit.
Beneath firm, matte, yellow-green skin is a crisp, fine-grained flesh bursting with sweetness. In fact, they are so renowned for their honey-like sweetness, juiciness and low acidity that, in Japan, they are viewed more as a candy-like treat or dessert than a fruit! Their sugar content is 15, which is almost the same as mangoes and the famous Yubari king melon.
Due to the high level of dedication and expertise require to grow Meigetsu apples, their low yield makes them extremely rare. This, paired with their popularity means that they are often sold out in harvest time every year and are rarely seen in the market. This could be your chance to one of the sweetest apples in the world, for yourself!

Name: Avocado - Caribbean or Ugandan
Description:
We sell two varieties of avocado - Caribbean and Ugandan - that, though slightly different, both taste divine!
If we had to pick a favourite, though, it would be Caribbean avocadoes. These avocadoes are generally considered to well surpass other types in terms of quality and taste, primarily because they are harvested when fully mature and then sent to the UK by air, unlike other varieties which are harvested early and held in refrigeration for extended periods whilst sent to the UK by sea.
Our Caribbean avocados grow abundantly on the tropical islands of St Lucia and Jamaica. They are round, plump and usually of medium to large size, with a fairly large round seed in the centre. They're harvested when glossy green but ripen to maroon red and eventually deep purple.
With a heavenly, melt-in-the-mouth texture, being supremely creamy and buttery, and a flavour that dazzles the tastebuds with its delightful sweetness, it's no wonder they are so adored by the locals! Make sure you leave them to ripen perfectly before eating so you enjoy the flesh at its finest.
Although most commonly eaten as they are, it has become very popular to make avocado toast, combine them in salads, and use them to make scrumptious baked goods - check out the 'Further information' tab below for some of our recommended recipes, including a unique avocado chocolate pudding!
As well as being delicious, avocadoes also boast many nutritional benefits: they are an excellent source of fibre, potassium, and folate, all of which support heart and cardiovascular health, and are rich in vitamin E. We also sell frozen avocado flesh! They have the same great flavour and nutritional benefits as fresh avocados we have simply removed the flesh from the skin and frozen it in our warehouse - no colourings, additives, or flavourings have been added.

Tab Content:Preparation:
Fresh: wash thoroughly before consumption. Slice in half, taking care to cut around the central seed. Once the seed is removed, use a spoon to scoop out the soft flesh.

Frozen: make sure it is fully defrosted before you consume it.
Tab Content:Usage: Eat straight out of hand or use with dishes, such as toast, eggs and salads.
Tab Content:Storage:
Allow to ripen at room temperature.

Once the avocado yields to gentle pressure, store it in refrigeration to prevent spoiling.
Tab Content:Average Weight:
Our avocados vary in size. They usually weigh between 350g to 550g each with an average size of about 450g. However, please note that there are natural variations in fresh fruit.

Our avocados from Saint Lucia vary in size quite significantly. They are between 300g to 500g in weight

Name: Banana - ambul kesel
Description:
Our ambul kesel bananas are a must-try!
Ambul kesel bananas immediately catch the eye due to their surprisingly miniature size: like our apple bananas, they are less than half the size of bananas you typically find in UK supermarkets! However, although they are small in size, these plump bananas are packed with flavour!
Beneath the smooth, yellow peel of these extremely aromatic fruits is soft, cream-coloured flesh that will astound your tastebuds: once the bananas are ripe, their flesh is wonderfully creamy and boasts a rich, sweet-sour savour. Indeed, although ambul kesel is commonly known as 'sour banana', you will be delighted by the perfect balance of sugary and tangy notes!
Their bite-sized stature means they are perfect to enjoy out of hand! However, as well as being refreshing, energising snacks, ambul kesel bananas have great culinary versatility - they can be utilised in any number of recipes! We'd recommend substituting standard supermarket-bought bananas for these brilliant bananas in all your favourite banana recipes, from banana bread and banoffee trifles and banana smoothies! Whilst unripe, they are commonly combined in curries. Check out the 'Further information' tab for some recipe inspiration, including an upside-down banana cake with maple-caramel sauce!
Alongside being delectable and making the ideal ingredients, ambul kesel bananas are extremely nutritionally valuable. In particular, they stand out among banana varieties in their outstandingly high vitamin C content, and are excellent sources of potassium and dietary fibre. We also sell frozen ambul kesel bananas! Fresh bananas have simply been peeled and then frozen, with no additives or preservatives added during the freezing process. As they're 100% pure, you can be confident that they are as healthy as the fresh fruits, and that they'll offer the same wonderful sweet-sour notes!

Name: Banana - apple
Description:
Apple bananas are a must-try for banana lovers!
Although small in size - they are less than half the size of bananas you typically find in UK supermarkets - these plump 'baby bananas' sourced from Uganda and India are far superior in texture and flavour to supermarket-bought bananas! Beneath their greenish-yellow skin is tender cream-coloured flesh that has a velvety smooth texture and a heavenly flavour: your tastebuds will be wowed with the sweet, yet tangy, taste, and the subtle hints of green apple.
Delectable when eaten fresh out of hand, they can also, like other banana varieties, be used in a range of recipes, from banana bread to smoothies. Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some recommended recipes, including a superb banana tiramisu, the ultimate dessert for fruit lovers!
As well as being delicious, apple bananas are extremely nutritious. Rich in potassium and fibre, and renowned for the rapid energy boost they provide eaters, they make the perfect healthy snack!

Name: Banana - bananito
Description:
Are you a banana lover looking for a different variety to try? Our bananitos are just the thing for you!
Bananitos are small, thin bananas - their delicate shape has earned them the name 'lady finger' bananas. Like many other banana varieties, bananitos ripen from green to yellow, however they differ in that they have softer and creamier flesh. This delightful texture is matched with a wonderful flavour, sweeter than standard supermarket-bought bananas and somewhat reminiscent of apple bananas.


Best eaten fresh out of hand, bananitos are also well suited for use in a range of sweet and savoury recipes. Simply use them how you would any other banana: from delicious banana bread and pancakes, to cocktails and refreshing smoothies, their culinary applications are endless!
Like other banana varieties, bananitos boast a range of nutritional benefits. In particular, they are excellent sources of potassium and vitamin C, and are great for boosting energy levels.

Name: Banana - burro
Description:
Are you a banana lover looking for a new variety to try? Our burro bananas are just the thing for you!
Burro bananas are primarily cultivated in Mexico and the Philippines, however we source ours from the Caribbean.
The name 'burro' comes from these bananas' short, plump shape, because their stubby stature is reminiscent of a 'burro', the Spanish word for 'donkey'! Indeed, burro bananas are occasionally sold under the name chunky banana as they are stubbier and more square-shaped than the common banana; some are even completely triangular!
The peel is a rich, vivid, dark green that turns deep yellow with characteristic black/brown spots when ripe. When young, the flesh of the burro banana is tart and tangy with notes of apple and lime. As the fruit matures, the yellow flesh is soft on the outside with a slightly crisp, textured centre. A ripe burro banana's flesh wows with its divine flavour: your tastebuds will be delighted by the creamy, sweet flesh with its wonderful lemon undertones!
Burro bananas are known as a dual-purpose variety because as well as enjoying them fresh out of hand when they're fully ripe, they can also be eaten green like a plantain! Burro bananas are also versatile in that they are ideal for use in both sweet and savoury preparations! When they're green, they're perfect for combining into curries and frying into banana chips. When they're ripe, they can be enjoyed in any way you'd consume regular bananas, from making smoothies and sorbets to making scrumptious banana bread! Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some more recipe inspiration, including amazing burro banana muffins!
As well as being supremely delicious, burro bananas boast numerous nutritional benefits. In particular, they are an excellent source of potassium and are rich in vitamins B and C, dietary fibre, and magnesium. They also contain good amounts of phosphorous, magnesium, calcium, iron, and zinc. Our frozen, peeled burro bananas are offered in 1kg vacuum packs. They contain on average 11 to 12 bananas per packet. The bananas are frozen ripe so will be soft when defrosted, best used in smoothies.

Tab Content:Usage: Ripe burro bananas are delicious eaten straight out of hand, however they may also be cooked. They are prepared using similar cooking methods to that of plantains, e.g. boiling and baking (if ripe), to make either savoury or sweet dishes. When green, burro bananas are delicious simply fried in butter with a little salt and pepper.

To ripen, leave at room temperature or warmer. To hasten ripening, place in a paper bag and keep in a warm place.

Frozen burro bananas should be re-frozen immediately upon arrival or stored in the fridge and used within 3 days.

Name: Banana - red (whole racks available)
Description:
Red bananas are a must-try for exotic fruit lovers!
We sell both rath kessel red bananas from Sri Lanka and red dacca bananas from Ecuador. Both are similar in shape to (although slightly smaller than) standard yellow bananas, but immediately catch the eye with their dazzling red/maroon rind. You'll notice that rath kessel bananas are more rounded, whereas red dacca bananas have more noticeable ridges.
When you peel back the smooth, thick skin, a fruity scent is released - rath kessel bananas are the more aromatic of the two. When fully ripe, the deep yellow to orange coloured flesh (sometimes with subtle pink hues) is delicately soft and creamy, and it delights the tastebuds with its notes of berry and mango.
Rath kessel bananas are especially delicious. The flesh is softer and smoother than that of most bananas, and the richness of their exotic sweetness is particularly notable. If you're a first-time buyer of red bananas, we'd recommend starting with rath kessel (also known as rath kehel) bananas - we know you won't be disappointed!
Although the mouthwatering tropical sweetness of red bananas means they are best enjoyed when simply eaten fresh out of hand, they are also perfect for use in a range of recipes! Whether you use them to top pancakes or cereal, blend them into smoothies or ice cream, make banana bread, or mellow the spiciness of curries, you'll love these amazing fruits! In fact, you can use red bananas in pretty much any way you'd use yellow ones! Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some of our favourite red banana recipes, including a scrumptious custard and banana pudding!
As well as being delectable, red bananas provide many health benefits. Indeed, they are more nutritious than the popular yellow cavendish bananas commonly found here in the UK, notably containing significantly more vitamin C! In particular, they are rich in vitamin B6, potassium, and dietary fibre, and the rapid energy boost given by their high sugar levels means that they're a great, healthy snack.

Name: Banana - sugar
Description:
Seeni bananas, better known in the English-speaking world as sugar bananas, are a must-try for banana lovers!
Although our sugar bananas from Sri Lanka are small in size - they are not much larger than apple bananas, which are less than half the size of bananas you typically find in UK supermarkets! - these plump bananas are far superior in texture and flavour to supermarket-bought bananas! Beneath their smooth, visually appealing golden-yellow skin is tender, cream-coloured flesh that has a velvety smooth texture and a heavenly flavour: one bite of these bananas and your tastebuds will be wowed by their sweet taste! Indeed, so renowned are these bananas that in Cambodia they are considered the national fruit, a title bestowed on them by royal decree!
Although they are the perfect size for eating fresh out of hand, they are also, like other bananas, ideal for use in a range of culinary applications. We'd particularly recommend using them to make scrumptious banana bread, refreshing banana sorbet, and gloriously fruity smoothies! Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some recommended recipes, including a superb banana tiramisu, the ultimate dessert for fruit lovers!
As well as being delicious, sugar bananas are extremely nutritious. Rich in potassium and fibre, and renowned for the rapid energy boost they provide eaters, they make the perfect healthy snack! In fact, these nutrient-rich fruits are so highly regarded for their health benefits in Sri Lanka that they are often recommended for the sick. We also sell frozen sugar bananas! Fresh bananas have simply been peeled and then frozen, with no additives or preservatives added during the freezing process. As they're 100% pure, you can be confident that they are as healthy as the fresh fruits, and that they'll offer the same wonderful sweet notes!
Whole racks of sugar bananas are available. Find more information here.

Name: Breadfruit
Description:
Often referred to as a 'tropical potato', breadfruit is certainly one of the most unusual fruits we sell!
Related to mulberry, fig, and jackfruit, breadfruit is native to many regions across the tropics, and is known for requiring minimal care and bearing fruit much quicker than other plants - its yield can be up to 200kg per year! Breadfruit trees are also drought resistant and can survive tropical storms. It is for this reason that breadfruit is such a staple part of the diet of millions of people!
Large in size and round to oval in shape, breadfruit's pebbled skin matures from green to yellowish-brown and its cream-yellow flesh has, when eaten raw, a custard-like texture and is sweet to taste, with a flavour similar to jackfruit, corn, and durian. Breadfruits are usually, however, cooked before consumption to enjoy a richer flavour and softer consistency - during cooking, they release a sweet and fragrant aroma reminiscent of freshly baked bread, and once cooked, they have a bread-like texture and a taste that resembles potato, artichoke, and chestnut.
Breadfruit can be enjoyed in a number of ways. The flesh can be boiled or steamed and added to pasta salads, mashed with coconut milk or garlic and oil as a side dish, incorporated into pancake batter, or stirred into dips. It can also be added to curries, soups, and stews, or incorporated into casseroles, burritos, rice-based dishes, and falafel.
As well as being delicious, breadfruit is packed full of nutrients. In particular, it is a good source of antioxidants, calcium, dietary fibre, iron, magnesium, omega 3 and omega 6 - you can be confident in knowing that the fruit that's delighting your tastebuds is supremely healthy too!

Tab Content:Preparation:
Always wash first.

Sometimes you may notice small amounts of latex on the skin which is normal.

Unripe breadfruit are firm and evenly green and it's these which are used for cooking. To cook unripe breadfruit either boil, fry, bake, roast or steam. They can be cooked whole or cut into slices. Breadfruit slices can be marinated or pickled.

To ripen breadfruit leave them for a few days in a warm environment. Wrap in a tea towel to speed up the ripening process but each day remove from the towel and wipe with kitchen towel then re-wrap.The purpose of wiping the breadfruit is to prevent moisture building up on the skin which can cause the fruit to spoil. Ripe breadfruit are ready to eat once very soft all over.
Tab Content:Usage: Breadfruit can be eaten raw when the fruit becomes soft all over and the skin turns to yellow-brown. At this stage, as well as being eaten out of hand, the fruit is often used in baked goods, beverages and desserts. Once the unripe fruit is cooked, it will often accompany savoury meals much the same as a potato would be used.
Tab Content:Storage:
If cooking, keep in a cool dark place or in the refrigerator wrapped in a thick bag to maintain freshness.

Our dried breadfruit should be kept in a cool dry place and consumed by the best before date.
Tab Content:Average Weight:
Our smaller breadfruit usually weigh around 1kg to 1.5kg each.

Our larger breadfruit usually weigh around 1.5kg to 2.5kg each.

Name: Cactus fig - 'prickly pear'
Description:
Cactus figs are a must-try for exotic fruit lovers!
Cactus figs are the fruit of the cactus plant. They are small fruits covered in spines, hence their nickname 'prickly pear'. The juicy flesh inside is full of small seeds and is flavoured like watermelon and strawberry! The Colombian cactus figs are our recommended variety. They are the plumpest fruits with firm, sweet flesh and have a longer shelf life.
The colour of the fruit varies naturally, from deep purple to orange to green. There are subtle differences in the flavour.
Due to the high proportion of seeds, some people find it more convenient to put the cactus figs through a juicer to then enjoy the resulting sweet liquid.

Fresh: usually eaten out of hand but also made into juice and jams.

Frozen: defrost fully and then eat as a snack or use in drinks and smoothies.

Fresh: keep refrigerated.

Name: Cacao fruit
Description:
As the source of chocolate, cacao is an absolute must-try for exotic fruit lovers and chocoholics alike!
Cacao pods are medium to large in size and oblong in shape. When you open the pod, you will immediately be struck by the astringent, faintly floral aroma of the fruit and see that beneath the dense, textured outer shell are 20-60 compact, elongated seeds (also known as beans) enveloped in a fleshy, white pulp. The delicious pulp surrounding each bean is soft and slippery, whereas the beans tend to be drier and chewier. If you are looking for optimal juiciness, our St Lucian cacao is the best choice, because whilst it has less flesh than the Ecuadorian variety, the pulp is notably more succulent and less dense.
The flavour of cacao pulp and seeds varies depending on the variety and where and how the pods were cultivated, with some notably sweeter than others. However, the pulp typically has a sweet-sour taste, combining fruitiness, tanginess, acidity, and subtle sweetness, with divine notes of pineapple, citrus, lychee, and mango. Some people liken the flavour to 'passionfruit lemonade'! If we were to compare it to other exotic fruits, we'd say that cacao is a unique combination of soursop and mangosteen in texture and taste.
Although most commonly enjoyed by sucking on the glorious white pulp, there are many other ways to make the most of these fruits! For example, you can ferment, dry, and roast the fruit's seeds to turn them into cacao nibs, which are perfect for sprinkling over granola, yoghurt, and ice cream, and can be ground into cocoa powder. Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some recipe inspiration, including an article on how to make cacao nibs!
Cacao fruit boasts a host of health benefits. As well as being an excellent source of dietary fibre and vitamins and minerals such as magnesium and potassium, it is the highest plant-based source of iron known to man and has over 40 times the antioxidants of blueberries!

Name: Custard apple - cherimoya
Description:
The cherimoya is the fruit of the species Annona cherimola, which is thought to be native to Ecuador, Colombia, Peru and Bolivia. Today, cherimoya is grown throughout the world. The creamy texture of the flesh and its delicious sweet flavour gives the fruit its secondary name, custard apple.
A single, medium-sized cherimoya fruit contains 30 milligrams of vitamin C, providing about 35% of the daily recommended intake. Furthermore, one medium cherimoya provides a whopping 5 grams of dietary fibre, amounting to about 90% of the recommended amount!
We also sell frozen cherimoya! We offer vacuum-packed frozen halves, whereby we simply wash our ripe soft cherimoya fruits, slice them in half, seal them in vacuum bags, and freeze them.

Name: Citrus - Beni Madonna jelly orange (luxury fruit for gifting)
Description:
Ehime prefecture in Japan is well known for growing mandarins, but the star of the show is without a doubt the Beni Madonna jelly orange.
Prized for their sweetness and jelly-like softness, Beni Madonna oranges are a sought-after delicacy often given as a gift in the Winter. Their name, Madonna, is believed to be inspired by the nickname for a beautiful character in the famous Japanese novel, Botchan.
Beneath their thin, deep red skin is a flesh that is supremely soft and succulent. As you bite into a jelly orange, the flesh melts in your mouth and explodes with sweetness and a second-to-none juiciness.
First brought to market in 2005, it took farmers over 17 years to first produce them. Much care, dedication and expertise goes into growing a Beni Madonna orange, including control over moisture, covers to protect the soft skin from harsh rainfall and sunlight, and a rigorous selection process where only those passing a high level of sweetness, low levels of acidity and the correct colour are ready for market.
Beni Madonna oranges are a true treat, and unlike any other citrus youll try!

Name: Citrus - calamansi
Description:
Love citrus fruit but getting bored of the typical supermarket varieties? Calamansi is just the thing for you!
Calamansi (also known as calamondin) is a small citrus fruit with bumpy green rind and juicy golden-yellow flesh. They are divinely aromatic, with a floral fragrance that fills the room, and their flesh (which contains numerous cream-coloured seeds) has a tart, acidic-citrus flavour that will wow your tastebuds. One thing many people don't know about calamansi is that both the flesh and the rind are edible! The peel has a slightly sweeter taste than the flesh, with satisfyingly tangy undertones.
Calamansi is a versatile citrus that's used in many food and drink preparations. Here in the UK, chefs often use calamansi in dipping sauces and marinades, whilst bartenders use the fruit to make juice, cocktails, and alcohol infusions. It's very commonly used as a condiment in Filipino cuisine like pancit or lugaw, or in the basic sawsawan (dip) of calamansi juice with soy sauce/fish sauce, for fish, spring rolls, dumplings and various meats.
The fruit is used in local recipes in northern Indonesia. Fish are spritzed with the juice prior to cooking to eliminate the "fishy" smell. Kuah asam ("sour soup") is a regional clear fish broth made with calamansi juice. In bars in Asia, it's common for the calamansi to be frozen and used as ice cubes in beverages such as tea, soft drinks, water, and cocktails. A popular liqueur in the Philippines is made from calamansi. Calamansi can also be used to make marmalade and confectionery. As you can see, there are almost endless ways you can use your calamansi - as a place to start, check out the 'Further information' tab below for some of our favourite recipes!
As well as being amazingly versatile, calamansi boasts a range of nutritional benefits. In particular, they are an excellent source of vitamin C and have a high content of potassium, vitamin A, fibre, calcium, and limonene, a constituent part of the oil found in the rind that acts like an antioxidant in the way it benefits general health.

Tab Content:Also Known As: Calamonding, Calamondin, Calamandarin, Golden Lime, Kalamunding, Kalamansi, Philippine Lime, Panama orange, Musk Orange, limau kasturi.
Tab Content:Preparation:
Wash the calamansi then slice in half if being used as a condiment with food dishes.

The calamansi can also be eaten fresh out of hand after being peeled, although the tangy sour flavour lends them to more commonly being used in food and drinks applications.
Tab Content:Usage:
In Asian cuisine, calamansi juice is used to flavour fish, fowl and pork dishes during the cooking process or mixed with other sauces, herbs and spices to making dipping sauces.

Calamansi is also often used to make juice, served hot or cold, usually with honey to sweeten. Extracts of calamansi are used in cheaper bottled soft drinks found commonly across Southeast Asia.

It can also be used to make concentrate, confectionery and jams/marmalades.
Tab Content:Storage:
Kept in the refrigerator, fresh calamansi will last for a week or two.

When left to ripen at room temperature, they will turn tangerine orange.

Frozen calamansi should be placed in the freezer immediately upon arrival, or kept in the refrigerator and consumed within one week.

Name: Citrus - cedro diamante, frozen
Description:
Cedro Diamante is a unique citron fruit mostly cultivated in Santa Maria del Cedro, a town named in their honour.
Citron (known in its native Italy as 'cedro') are possibly the first citrus cultivated in Europe, possibly arriving from Persia, and have been cultivated for thousands of years in civilizations around the globe as a culinary ingredient, medicinal remedy, and religious symbol. They are one of the four 'original' citrus fruits, meaning that all other citrus varieties that are in existence today originate from citron. Cedro diamante are particularly important in Jewish culture as the purest and most perfect of all citrus and growing them is a labour of love.
Cedro diamante are one of the largest varieties of citrus, measuring up to three times the size of a supermarket lemon. These immensely aromatic fruits have wrinkled skin that ripens from green to bright yellow, and is enveloped in prominent oil glands, giving the surface a pebbled, glossy appearance. Beneath the skin is a layer of thick, white pith (which constitutes approximately 70% of the entire fruit), encasing a small amount of flesh.
Unlike other citrus fruits, citron has very little juice and flesh, so are most commonly used for their spongy pith and oil-infused zest. The pith is surprisingly sweet and is commonly sliced into small pieces and tossed with sugar and herbs to add some bright citrus notes to salads or combined with balsamic vinaigrette to create a lively salad dressing. The rind has a flavour and fragrance reminiscent of lemons, and In Italy, the peel is customarily candied and enjoyed as a sweet delicacy. The juice of the citron fruit is used as a drink and often as a syrup too. Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some of our favourite recipes, including a citron risotto!
As well as being versatile and divinely perfumed, citron boast many nutritional benefits. In particular, they are an excellent source of dietary fibre, potassium, and magnesium, and also provide good amounts of vitamin C, iron, and vitamin B6.

Name: Citrus - key limes, seeded
Description:
Key limes are a must-try for citrus lovers!
These citrus fruits are spherical in shape and small in size, ranging from 2.5 to 5cm in diameter. They have glossy, textured skin that ripens from yellow to an eye-catching deep green with a yellow blush. Beneath their leathery peel is a thin layer of spongy white rind attached to yellowish-green flesh that is tender and incredibly succulent. Key limes have become renowned not only for their intense citrus aroma, but also for the fact that boast a higher acidity than most other lime varieties, which gives them a strong tangy flavour with floral undertones. The flesh contains numerous small white seeds which are inedible and should be discarded.
Although, like other members of the citrus family, key limes are not eaten fresh out of hand, they have many culinary applications suitable for both raw and cooked recipes! With their name derived from their association with the Florida Keys, key limes have become best known as the flavouring ingredient in key lime pie, and we'd recommend using them in other sweet recipes too, such as cakes and ice cream. Their zest and juice are both highly regarded by bartenders and chefs for flavouring cocktails (and mocktails!), jams, marinades, and sauces - indeed, they have become so popular in this sphere that they are sometimes called 'the bartender's lime'! Our dried slices are similarly perfect for flavouring drinks, and make attractive cake decorations and cocktail garnishes too!
As well as being versatile and packed full of flavour, they are nutritionally beneficial too. In particular, they are an excellent source of vitamin C and potassium, and are rich in iron and calcium.

Name: Citrus - kumquat
Description:
One of the most overlooked citrus fruits, kumquats are a must-try for exotic fruit lovers!
In appearance, kumquats are comparable to small, oval oranges - indeed, their name comes from the Cantonese term 'kam kwat', which translates to 'golden orange'!
The skin of these olive-sized fruits is thin, glossy, and taut. Beneath the textured, bright orange-coloured peel are 3-6 segments of tender orange flesh, which contain a few small creamish/white seeds. The juicy flesh will wow your tastebuds with its sharp flavour.
However, kumquats stand out amongst other citrus varieties in that the entire fruit is edible, including the peel and the seeds! In fact, the peel boasts a divinely sweet and almost floral flavour, so you experience a fantastic taste sensation of zesty sweetness when you eat kumquats whole!
Although they are often simply eaten fresh out of hand, kumquats' combination of sweet and sour notes means they are perfect for use in both sweet and savoury dishes. Kumquats are popularly utilised in preserves, sauces, and salsas, and we'd especially recommend using them to make scrumptious cakes, pies, and even ice cream! Kumquats are also favoured by bartenders as aromatic edible garnishes and as a bright, fruity flavouring for cocktails and mocktails. Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some of our favourite recipes, including delicious kumquat marmalade!
As well as being supremely delectable and versatile, kumquats are nutritionally valuable. In particular, they are an excellent source of dietary fibre and are rich in vitamin C.

Tab Content:Preparation: Wash, pull off the stem, then chop or slice as required. The thin skin is very tricky to peel and as it provides a pleasant contrast to the slightly more sour flesh, it's generally left on.
Tab Content:Usage: If ripe, eat whole or slice to use in salads. Less ripe fruit can be simmered in sugar syrup (30 minutes) before being added to fruit salads, or served with ice cream. You can also use it to make marmalade.
Tab Content:Storage: Kept in the fridge in a perforated bag, kumquats can last for up to two weeks.
Tab Content:Average Weight: One kumquat usually weighs approximately 5-10g.
Tab Content:Further Info:
Wondering how best to enjoy your kumquats? We'd recommend using them to make this scrumptious kumquat cake with an orange glaze, and this refreshing kumquat ice cream, the perfect dessert for summer!

We'd also recommend making kumquat marmalade - the recipe is below!

Ingredients

  • 2 cups of kumquats, chopped
  • 1/2 cup sugar
  • 1/2 water
  • Spices such as vanilla bean or cinammon

Method

  1. Place the kumquats, sugar, and spices in a saucepan. Let it sit for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
  2. Add water and bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce heat to medium-low and simmer for 15-20 minutes or until the liquid has reduced and thickened.
  3. Place in an airtight container and store in a refrigerator. Use within 2 weeks.

Name: Citrus - lemon, organic
Description:
These lemons from Spain not only taste better than the standard supermarket variety, but they're better for the enviornment!
They are organically certified and grown in accordance with biodynamics, an agricultural practice that promotes soil fertility, crop diversity and respect for nature's cycles. Originating from family farms in Spain, they are sourced based on pure organic excellence, ensuring you get only the best-in look and taste!
As well as being large in size - they are significantly bigger than supermarket-bought lemons! - these organic also have a distinctive shape, being much more elongated and tapered than the rounder lemons commonly cultivated in Italy.
These organic lemons are refreshing and their juice makes the perfect flavouring, whether you are marinading meat or fish, making jams or marmalades, creating cocktails, or anything else that you desire. It will provide the ideal citrus kick!
Did you know that lemon peel can be eaten too, and that it is delicious and healthy? Lemon peel is very aromatic, tart, and is rich in essential oils, and as such is the ideal flavouring for creams, liqueurs, cocktails and mocktails, desserts, and more! It is also a great source of fibre and vitamin C.
Enjoy a delicious lemon with the comfort of knowing it was grown with care.

Name: Citrus - lemon, snack lemon
Description:
Lemon lovers, we have just the thing for you - snack lemons!
Sweeter than a traditional lemon, these juicy lemons can be eaten fresh out of hand. In fact, as their name suggests, they have been specially cultivated for snacking!
Unlike most lemon varieties, snack lemons have a low level of sourness, instead offering a delightful sweet-tangy flavour with each bite. When combined with their small size, it's no surprise that these lemons are creating a buzz as the ideal fruity snack!
Snack lemons have an edible peel too, so you can eat the whole fruit! If you do want to remove the peel though, you're in luck, as the rind is very easy to peel.
Their combination of sugary sweetness and tanginess makes these delicious lemons super versatile! We'd particularly recommend using them to add a kick of zesty fruitiness to desserts. In addition to being packed full of flavour, snack lemons are a great source of vitamin C and antioxidants. Who knew that snacking could be so healthy?

Name: Citrus - lime, kaffir lime
Description:
Kaffir limes are citrus delicacies that all exotic fruit lovers need to try!
The kaffir lime is a wonderfully aromatic citrus fruit native to various Asian countries. They are small in size - slightly smaller than regular limes - and round in shape, with a slightly protruded nozzle at the top. They immediately attract the eye with their bumpy, dark green rind. Beneath their appealing skin is a thin layer of spongy white pith, attached to segmented light green flesh. This tender flesh boasts a much richer, more complex flavour than supermarket-bought limes, wowing with its combination of tangy and floral notes.
Although, like other citrus fruits, kaffir limes are not eaten fresh out of hand, their outstanding savour and aroma have led chefs and bartenders around the world to prize them as superior culinary ingredients! Their aroma is so renowned that their essential oil is used in perfumery! They are particularly popular in Southeast Asian cuisine, with the juice, peel, and leaves all utilised in cooking - indeed, in Cambodia, the entire fruit is crystallised/candied for eating! The peel is commonly utilised in marinades and incorporated in Lao and Thai curry dishes to add a fresh, astringent flavour. The zest of the kaffir lime, referred to as combava, is also used in creole cuisine to impart flavour in infused rums and rougails in Martinique, Réunion and Madagascar, and slices of kaffir lime make the perfect cocktail garnishes! We'd particularly recommend using these tantalisingly tart fruits in stir-fries and soups, as well as adding a squeeze of lime juice into a glass of spring water to create an invigorating beverage!
Alongside being supremely versatile and ideal for adding a sharp, zesty kick to your mealtimes, kaffir limes are also nutritionally valuable. In particular, they are excellent sources of vitamin C - one lime provides 32% of your daily vitamin C needs! - and are rich in dietary fibre.

Name: Citrus - lime, kaffir lime
Description:
Kaffir limes are citrus delicacies that all exotic fruit lovers need to try!
The kaffir lime is a wonderfully aromatic citrus fruit native to various Asian countries. They are small in size - slightly smaller than regular limes - and round in shape, with a slightly protruded nozzle at the top. They immediately attract the eye with their bumpy, dark green rind. Beneath their appealing skin is a thin layer of spongy white pith, attached to segmented light green flesh. This tender flesh boasts a much richer, more complex flavour than supermarket-bought limes, wowing with its combination of tangy and floral notes.
Although, like other citrus fruits, kaffir limes are not eaten fresh out of hand, their outstanding savour and aroma have led chefs and bartenders around the world to prize them as superior culinary ingredients! Their aroma is so renowned that their essential oil is used in perfumery! They are particularly popular in Southeast Asian cuisine, with the juice, peel, and leaves all utilised in cooking - indeed, in Cambodia, the entire fruit is crystallised/candied for eating! The peel is commonly utilised in marinades and incorporated in Lao and Thai curry dishes to add a fresh, astringent flavour. The zest of the kaffir lime, referred to as combava, is also used in creole cuisine to impart flavour in infused rums and rougails in Martinique, Réunion and Madagascar, and slices of kaffir lime make the perfect cocktail garnishes! We'd particularly recommend using these tantalisingly tart fruits in stir-fries and soups, as well as adding a squeeze of lime juice into a glass of spring water to create an invigorating beverage!

Name: Citrus - orange sweet, navelina seeded unwaxed
Description:
Are you an orange lover looking for a new variety to try? Our navelina oranges are just the thing for you. The fruits grown in Italy are by farmers who use organic growing methods, they are not touched by pesticides and also aren't waxed after harvest!
Like our chocolate oranges, navelina oranges are a variety of navel orange. They are medium to large in size and are round to slightly pear-shaped, with a distinctive dip (also known as a navel) at the stem end.
Beneath their pebbled, reddish-orange rind is a thin layer of white pith that is easily removed from the tender orange-yellow flesh. The soft, segmented flesh emits a floral and fresh citrus fragrance and is sure to refresh and satisfy your tastebuds. The flesh is juicy and sweet.
Navelina oranges are ideal for eating fresh out of hand, they are easy peelers and contain very little acidity.
Of course eating straight out of hand is not the only use for these citrus goodies, we'd particularly recommend blending them into a tangy and bitter marmalade or for juicing at home.
Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some more recipe inspiration, including a navel orange souffle!
Remember to include oranges in your diet, they are nutritionally valuable. In particular, they are excellent sources of vitamin C and potassium and are also rich in dietary fibre, vitamin A, and magnesium.

Name: Citrus - pomelo red
Description:
Not only do pomelos wow with their size - they are the biggest citrus fruit in the world! - but their wonderful aroma and flavour delight exotic fruit fans too!
Although pomelo (also known as shaddocks, after the sea captain who brought them from Polynesia to the West Indies) closely resemble grapefruit, they are a species in their own right.
Round to oval in shape and, as aforementioned, large in size - pomelo can weigh up to 5kgs, however most export quality fruits are around 1-2kgs - red pomelos are less common than other pomelo varieties. They have green/dark green skin and firm red or pink flesh which has a dazzling citrus flavour, with both sweet and sour notes. Less juicy than other pomelo types, the flesh of red pomelo is nevertheless favoured for its crunchiness and aromatic savour.
For a short time each year, we source fresh red pomelo from Tân Lc, which is in the Northern province of Hoà Bình in Vietnam. These pomelo have yellow peel and rich red flesh which has a perfectly balanced sweet and bitter flavour. They are a juicy variety, favoured over other varieties in Vietnam which have drier flesh.
As pomelos are the least acidic of all citrus fruits, they are usually eaten out of hand (though the pith around the segments is bitter and therefore not usually eaten). Yet, they are also well-suited to a number of sweet and savoury recipes! We'd particularly recommend using them to add some exotic flavour to your salads, chopping them into salsas, blending them into smoothies and pressing them for their richly flavoured fruit juice that will liven up your cocktails (or mocktails!) They can also withstand heat, so they are ideal for simmering into jams and compotes, incorporating into baked goods recipes, and roasting in the oven topped with unsalted butter. The list is endless! Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some more recipe inspiration.
As well as being delectable, pink-flesh pomelos are nutritionally valuable. In particular, they boast a high concentration of vitamins A and C, and are a good source of potassium and copper.
As well as being delectable, pomelo are nutritionally valuable, boasting in particular a high concentration of vitamin C. They are also believed to help alleviate the condition acid reflux.

Name: Citrus - sudachi (luxury fruit for gifting)
Description:
Do you want to try one of Japans most famous citrus?
Sudachi is one of Tokushimas most famous products. Exclusively farmed in its hilly and mountainous areas, Sudachi grow in the winter when the colder makes them the most sour. These prime conditions give Tokushima Sudachi their characteristic fresh aroma and tartness that make them so beloved. They are then harvested in their dark green immature state when theyre at their most refreshing and vibrant. In its native Tokushima, youll see Sudachi everywhere, seasoning native dishes, garnishing cocktails and even incorporated into sweets!
But what makes them so special? Beloved as they are in Japan, they are rapidly becoming popular overseas too as a unique and delicious citrus set apart from lemons and limes. Theyre not usually eaten out of hand. Instead, they are used primarily for their juice, squeezed over grilled chicken, seafood, noodles, and any dish that needs a zesty kick or a refreshing revival.
The pulp is finer than citron and more acidic with a uniquely refreshing and spicy scent. They are also much zestier than lime or lemon juice, with a distinctly peppery flavour. Their limited availability due to their growing season, as well as their tricky harvesting process (their trees are not guaranteed to produce fruit every year!) make Sudachi from Tokushima even more revered. You cant get these from the supermarket!
As well as being versatile and packed full of flavour, they are nutritionally beneficial too. In particular, they are an excellent source of vitamin C, potassium, and calcium.
We sell our sudachi in 200g or 1kg boxes.

Name: Citrus - tangelo
Description:
Love oranges but getting bored of the same supermarket varieties? Tangelo may be just the fruit for you!
Tangelos are the result of a hybridisation between a tangerine and a pomelo. Medium to large in size - they are usually about the size of an adult's fist - tangelos' shape catches the eye, owing to the distinctive protrusion at the top of each fruit. Their thick, pebbled, dark orange skin is loose and easier to peel than standard oranges, and their seedless flesh (in 10-12 sections) is incredibly succulent and refreshing, with a delectable flavour that is tangy and tart, complemented by a medium sweetness.
Although most often eaten fresh out of hand, tangelos' sweet yet tart flavour means they are incredibly versatile, being ideal for use in a variety of sweet and savoury food and drink recipes. You can use tangelos for any recipe that calls for oranges or tangerines, but we'd especially recommend: using them to make invigorating juice, to be drunk by itself or put in cocktails, smoothies, and sauces to give them a tangy citrus kick; adding segments to salads to infuse them with some exotic fruit flavour; making salsas to accompany seafood dishes, and zesting them to bring some freshness to sweet desserts. Even tangelos' peel can be used, most often simmered in a sugar syrup to make candied peel! Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some of our favourite recipes.
Our dried tangelo - dried fruit and dried peel - is perfect for cocktail garnishing or infusing hot and cold water to create the ideal, aromatic drink! Meanwhile, our 1kg vacuum bags of frozen peeled tangelo are perfect for making your own tangelo juice!
As well as being delicious, tangelos boast a number of nutritional benefits. In particular, they are an excellent source of vitamin C, providing almost 60% of the required daily amount! They are also rich in dietary fibre, folate, and calcium.

Name: Coconut - jelly nuts
Description:
Certain varieties of green coconut, or young coconut, are also known as 'jelly nuts' because of the thin layer of jelly-like coconut flesh, which is present when they are harvested. The flesh is usually a light grey colour and translucent, resembling jelly.
The green coconuts are harvested when they are young whilst the coconut water is still crisp and refreshing and the coconut flesh is still thin and soft. It has a large amount of coconut water and a small layer of jelly-like coconut meat.
The coconut water in jelly nuts is crisp with a slight sweetness - perfect healthy hydration.
Our green coconuts are either from Costa Rica or farms in Sri Lanka (the farms in Sri Lanka follow organic farming practices however they do not hold organic certification).
The green coconuts from Costa Rica travel by sea, whilst the green coconuts from Sri Lanka travel by air. Please note, you should expect around one week between ordering and dispatch if you are purchasing the Sri Lankan because we only receive a limited shipment of these once per week.

Name: Coconut - mature
Description:
The image that appears in most people's minds when they think of coconuts, round, brown, hairy, and with bright white flesh - these are mature coconuts (so-called to distinguish them from the distinctive young coconut variety).
Coconuts, the fruit of coconut palms - coconut palm trees are native to southeast Asia and islands between the Pacific and Indian oceans, but are believed to be the most widespread fruit trees in the world! - have a variety of culinary uses. For instance, they provide two delicious beverages to enjoy: coconut water and coconut milk.
Once you've punctured the 'eyes' of the coconut using a hammer or corkscrew (see the 'Further information' tab below for more detailed instructions), you can pour the water straight out of the fruit: fresh coconut water has a unique, crisp flavour, incorporating sweet, salty, and nutty notes, and is the perfect beverage to refresh yourself. Coconut milk on the other hand is extracted by pressing the raw, grated meat of the fruit, and because of this it has a similar taste to the meat itself, and a texture someway between the water and thick coconut cream.
Coconut oil is also extracted from the meat of the fruit, and is often used in cooking as a substitute for other vegetable oils. The meat itself is also consumed: the firm white flesh is slightly sweet and is popularly eaten both fresh and dried, as well as grated and shaved, and then incorporating the shavings in a number of recipes, from baked goods and ice creams, to garnishing fruit salads and drinks.
The fresh and dried meat, milk, and water of the coconut can too be used in a variety of food and drink recipes, especially as their unique blend of flavours allows them to work in both sweet and savoury dishes. Description:
When a coconut falls from the palm it will eventually germinate and the coconut water inside the shell transforms to an almost unbelievable sponge-like consistency. The sponge is at maximum size at around 20 to 24 weeks after germination.

Name: Coconut - young coconut
Description:
Love coconuts? Young coconuts are just the thing for you!
Young coconuts are about 6 to 9 months old when they are harvested. The size of the coconuts varies, but all of these immature coconuts have an eye-catching appearance, encased as they are in their aesthetically appealing ivory shell.
Inside this uniquely shaped casing is a 1/2cm layer of soft, pinkish brown meat - it is occasionally soft enough to be eaten with a spoon but, being firmer than the meat found in jelly nuts, it can have a bit of a bite. Young coconuts are however primarily harvested for their supremely refreshing juice. There can be anywhere between 350ml to 600ml of nutritious young coconut water inside a single coconut. The coconut water is cloudy or yellow in colour and boasts a rich, malty taste. If you prefer lighter flavours you should try our jelly nuts which have fresh, refreshing and crisp water with a light to medium sweetness.
We usually source the nam-hom variety from Thailand which is renowned for its sweet, aromatic water and soft, tender flesh.
As well as offering delicious meat and a thirst-quenching beverage, young coconuts boast a number of nutritional benefits. In particular, they are a good source of calcium, iron, and dietary fibre, and young coconut water is rich in beneficial electrolytes. Image for illustrative purposes only. Water from a young coconut is not clear. It is often a beige colour with a malty taste.

Name: Dates - barhi
Description:
Barhi dates are smaller and more spherical than other date varieties. They have a lower-than-average astringency, meaning that they are edible during all three stages of ripeness. These dates are often still attached to the vine when sold in their unripe, yellow stage. The yellow Barhi date has a golden matte finish and a crunchy apple-like texture with a slight sweetness and mild astringency. If left at room temperature, it will eventually turn a brownish color as it ripens, becoming soft and chewy with a thin crisp outer skin.
They provide a varying degree of sweetness depending upon their ripeness level, ranging from fresh sugar cane to coconut and butterscotch - once fully ripe, Barhi dates are considered the sweetest and creamiest of all dates!
Although best enjoyed when simply eaten out of hand, Barhi dates are also ideal for a number of culinary applications, especially as they mature into softer, sweeter fruits. Once they reach this creamy sweetness, they are perfect for pureeing or using as a natural sweetener by chopping them and adding them to smoothies, cereals, and baked goods recipes. Their rich butterscotch flavour means they are particularly popular as ingredients in cake and sweet treat recipes! Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some recipe inspiration!
As well as being delicious and versatile, Barhi dates boast a number of nutritional benefits. In particular, they are an excellent source of dietary fibre and are rich in potassium.

Name: Dates - medjool (Jordan and Palestine)
Description:
Our premium Medjool dates from Palestine and Jordan are a must-try! They are some of the best quality Medjool dates you can buy.
The Medjool date is believed to be one of the worlds oldest cultivated fruits, with cultivation dating (pardon the pun) as far back as 4000 BC! They have been extremely popular in the Middle East and North Africa for thousands of years - the Ancient Egyptians are known to have used them to make an early form of wine!
Medjool dates are plump and oval in shape and slightly larger in size than other date varieties. They have wrinkled, glossy - their natural sugar crystals give rise to a distinctive shimmer - dark brown skin, underneath which is chewy, juicy, amber-coloured flesh that wows the tastebuds with its sweetness and undertones of caramel, honey, and cinnamon. Within the meaty flesh is a single elongated pit, which you need to remove before consumption.
Thanks to their succulence, softness - they have a softer texture than other dates - intense natural sweetness, and richly aromatic flavour, there are very few date varieties that can compare to the Medjool. Indeed, they are often called the Cadillac of Dates and the "King of Dates" due to their superior taste, size, and consistency!
Our Medjool dates from Palestine and Jordan are both Class 1, medium-sized fruits. They are both 100% pure, containing nothing but fruity goodness (with no added co and will delight you with their softness and complex flavour.
Whichever dates you choose, you will enjoy supremely delicious fruits that are perfect for snacking and a range of culinary uses! Although most commonly eaten fresh out of hand, they are also an ideal natural sweetener and sugar alternative. They are often chopped into pasta or rice dishes, and their sweetness makes them perfect for complementing savoury notes in vegetable and meat dishes, like lamb, pork, or poultry. You can blend dates into smoothies, press them into a syrup, or use them in baked goods like cakes, pies, and bread. We would particularly recommend honouring their Middle Eastern origins by making maamoul, scrumptious cookies filled with date pudding that melt in the mouth! Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some of our favourite recipes!
As well as being divinely delectable, Medjool dates boast many nutritional benefits. In particular, they are an excellent source of fibre, calcium, and vitamin B, and contain more potassium than bananas!

Name: Dragon fruit - red flesh
Description:
Widely regarded as one of the most eye-catching and delicious tropical fruits, it's no surprise that dragon fruits are a firm favourite among our customers!
Red dragon fruits are small to medium fruits which wow with their reddish-pink skin adorned with many green-tipped scales. Beneath the waxy, semi-smooth skin of these round to oval-shaped fruits is vibrant red to purple-coloured flesh containing hundreds of tiny, edible, black seeds. The combination of the tender, aqueous flesh and the crunchy, chewy seeds means eating a dragon fruit is similar to eating a kiwi! Red dragon fruit particularly stands out because their crisp flesh boasts a more intense sweetness than white flesh varieties, and this sweetness is perfectly complemented by slightly acidic undertones and hints of nuttiness from the seeds.
The brilliant flavour profile of red dragon fruits means they are most commonly eaten simply fresh out of hand - try chilling them beforehand as this enhances their spectacular taste! However, these mouthwatering fruits are also ideal for use in any number of recipes! They are perfect for incorporating into raw dishes such as fruit salads, cooking into sauces and syrups, and chopping into salsas. They are also well-suited for making smoothies and sorbets, and for flavouring and garnishing cocktails. Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some recipe inspiration, including dragon fruit macarons and dragon fruit jam!
As well as being divinely delectable and extremely versatile, red dragon fruits offer an array of nutritional benefits. In particular, they are an excellent source of betacyanins and lycopene (healthful compounds that give the fruits their red hue) and are rich in vitamin C, dietary fibre, and potassium.

Name: Dragon fruit - yellow
Description:
Yellow dragon fruit is one of the most visually pleasing fruits we sell!
Hailing from Central and South America, yellow dragon fruit is like its sister fruits of different colours in having very distinctive skin and bright flesh containing an abundance of small black seeds.
Yellow dragon fruit's somewhat crunchy, juicy white flesh has a texture similar to that of white dragon fruit and boasts a delicious, but mild, flavour which is satisfyingly sweet and delights the tastebuds with subtle undertones of citrus and floral notes. As much as we enjoy all varieties of dragon fruit, we think yellow dragon fruit outshines its counterparts in both succulence and sweetness, so we'd recommend it to those looking for a real fruity treat!
Delectable when eaten fresh out of hand, yellow dragon fruit can also be used in a variety of food and drink recipes. They are commonly used in smoothies and fruit salads, as well as mixed with yoghurt and ice cream, but we would also recommend making yellow dragon fruit salsa and macarons - check out the 'Further information' tab below for the recipes!
As well as being wonderfully refreshing and extremely appetizing, yellow dragon fruit is also nutritionally beneficial: they are rich in vitamins B and C and various antioxidants, and are also a good source of a plethora of minerals, including calcium and phosphorus.

Name: Dragon fruit - yellow pitahaya
Description:
Yellow pitahaya are a must-try for all exotic fruit lovers!
First recorded in 1494, pitahaya - the Spanish word for 'scaly fruit' - have been enjoyed for centuries!
Small to medium in size and oval to elliptical in shape, yellow pitahaya are in appearance very similar to other dragon fruit varieties, although they are usually slightly smaller than red and pink dragon fruits. Beneath their thick, rubbery, scaly skin - which ripens to an eye-catching golden yellow - is crisp translucent flesh that delights the tastebuds! Not only do eaters rejoice in their crunchy seeded flesh but they are also astounded by the flesh's divine sweetness, which is gloriously complemented by subtly floral and fruity notes!
Although best enjoyed when simply eaten fresh out of hand, yellow pitahaya are excellent culinary ingredients too! From adding slices of pitahaya to fruit salads and fruit kebabs, to chopping pitahaya into tangy salsas, simmering it into compotes and jams, and blending into sorbets, the opportunities are almost endless! Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some more recipe inspiration, including a pitahaya, mango, and arugula salad and a brilliant yellow dragon fruit lemonade, the ideal thirst-quencher!
As well as being supremely delectable, pitahaya have been staples of traditional medicines for at least 500 years, and continue to be highly regarded for their nutritional value. In particular, they are rich in magnesium, potassium, and calcium.

Name: Durian - frozen
Description:
Keeping well in the freezer for up to 3 months after delivery, our frozen durian flesh is perfect for those who want to have a ready supply of the 'king of fruits' all year round!
Durians are distinctive for their large size, strong odour, and formidable thorn-covered husk. The fruits can grow as large as 50cm long and 30cm in diameter, and they typically weigh two to four kilograms!
Their thick, golden-yellow flesh (containing small, flat seeds) has a soft, almost melt-in-the-mouth texture. This creamy smoothness is coupled with a balanced flavour: your tastebuds will be delighted by its combination of both sweet and bitter notes!
Like the fresh flesh, our 100% pure frozen durian flesh boasts a wonderful savour. Indeed, our frozen durian flesh will actually be preferable to those new to durian, as the fruit's unique taste - which has been compared to everything from custard to onions! - is somewhat mellowed during the freezing process.
You can choose from either monthong or Ri6 durian. Monthong is the more well-known variety: it accounts for over 50% of durian production within Thailand and is the top exported cultivar of the fruit! It's great reputation stems from its wonderful flesh. Its name means 'golden pillow' in English, an indication of the distinctive softness and thickness of monthong's flesh! The variety has also become renowned for how well it keeps - it can be stored for approximately twenty days without spoiling.
Although not as well-known, Ri6 has become extremely popular in Vietnam, with locals considering it a premium variety. Its flesh boasts a brighter golden-yellow colour and a stronger, more tropical aroma than other durians, and some think it has a more sugary sweetness too!
The frozen, peeled flesh can be enjoyed in many different forms. Alongside consuming the fully defrosted flesh neat like you would that of a fresh durian, you can blend the flesh into smoothies to create the perfect healthy drink and we'd also recommend combining the flesh with desserts such as ice cream to add some tropical flavour to your sweet treats. Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some recipe inspiration, including durian cheesecake!
As well as being flavoursome and versatile, our frozen durian flesh boasts a number of nutritional benefits. It is an excellent source of dietary fibre and vitamin C, and with no colours, preservatives, or flavourings added, you can be confident in knowing that you're only consuming fruity goodness!

Name: Feijoa
Description:
The feijoa takes its name from the Portuguese botanist, Dom da Silva Feijoa, who discovered the fruit in Brazil. They are a distant member of the guava family - this is evident through the fruits' similar taste and aroma.
They can be up to the size of a small egg, however they are usually smaller than this and have tough dark green skin. The outer part of the flesh is grainy and firm but the central portion of the fruit is a sweet and creamy, clear jelly-like pulp.
The sweet aromatic flavour of this fruit is comparable to pineapple and guava, hence the nickname 'pineapple guava'.
The tiny edible seeds in the centre are not noticeable.
Feijoa are rich in Iodine and a great source of vitamin C.

Name: Feijoa
Description:
The feijoa takes its name from the Portuguese botanist, Dom da Silva Feijoa, who discovered the fruit in Brazil. They are a distant member of the guava family - this is evident through the fruits' similar taste and aroma.
They can be up to the size of a small egg, however they are usually smaller than this and have tough dark green skin. The outer part of the flesh is grainy and firm but the central portion of the fruit is a sweet and creamy, clear jelly-like pulp.
The sweet aromatic flavour of this fruit is comparable to pineapple and guava, hence the nickname 'pineapple guava'.
The tiny edible seeds in the centre are not noticeable.
Feijoa are rich in Iodine and a great source of vitamin C.

Name: Grapes - Queen Rouge (luxury fruit for gifting)
Description:
Introducing Queen Rouge grapes, a new variety developed in the Nagano prefecture as a hybrid of the dark purple unicorn and the supremely popular shine muscat.
Only debuting in 2021, this special variety still has a limited harvest, meaning its extremely exclusive! Cultivation is currently only permitted within Nagano prefecture where conditions are perfect for creating juicy sweet grapes.
With a glowing red hue and an elongated shape, Queen rouge are completely seedless (Seedless red grapes are notoriously difficult to cultivate!) and can be eaten without first removing the skin. Beneath their thin skin is a seedless translucent flesh with a rich, sweet honeyed flavour. They have a bQueerix level of 20/22 and very little acidity, making for a balanced flavour that is not overwhelmingly sweet.
It take a lot of time, patience and dedication to grow queen rouge grapes. Farmers shield each bunch from pests and elements with individually wrapped bags. When the grapes are fully grown, it takes the honed skills of farmers to prune into neat, uniformed bunches. Final checks are then undertaken for sugar content and taste, to ensure only the finest tasting grapes make it to market.

Name: Jackfruit - whole jackfruit
Description:
Jackfruit is an exotic fruit grown in tropical regions of the world. It is native to South India.
It is part of the Moraceae plant family, which also includes fig, mulberry and breadfruit. Jackfruit has a spiky outer skin and is green or yellow in colour.
One unique aspect of jackfruit is its unusually large size. It is the largest tree fruit in the world and can reach up to 80 pounds (35 kg) in weight.
Jackfruit has a subtle sweet and fruity flavour. It has been said to taste similar to a combination of fruits, including apples, pineapples, mangoes and bananas.
Since jackfruit is able to withstand tropical climates, it can be a major source of calories and carbs for people in developing countries who are at risk of starvation.
It contains a moderate amount of calories, providing 155 in a one-cup (165-gram) serving. Approximately 92% of the calories come from carbs, while the rest come from protein and a small amount of fat.
Furthermore, jackfruit contains some of almost every vitamin and mineral that you need, as well as a decent amount of fibre.
Our honey jackfruit are sourced from India and Bangladesh.

One unique aspect of jackfruit is its unusually large size. It is the largest tree fruit in the world and can reach up to 80 pounds (35 kg) in weight.
Jackfruit has a subtle sweet and fruity flavour. It has been said to taste similar to a combination of fruits, including apples, pineapples, mangoes and bananas.
Since jackfruit is able to withstand tropical climates, it can be a major source of calories and carbs for people in developing countries who are at risk of starvation.
It contains a moderate amount of calories, providing 155 in a one-cup (165-gram) serving. Approximately 92% of the calories come from carbs, while the rest come from protein and a small amount of fat.
Furthermore, jackfruit contains some of almost every vitamin and mineral that you need, as well as a decent amount of fibre.
Our honey jackfruit are sourced from India and Bangladesh.

Name: Kiwi - red
Description:
Are you a kiwi lover in need of a new variety to try? Our red kiwis are just the thing for you!
At first glance, red kiwis seem unassuming: like supermarket-bought varieties, they are small in size, ovoid in shape, and have smooth, brown, paper-thin skin. However, when you look inside, you'll understand one reason why these delicious fruits are so highly regarded. Their golden-yellow flesh boasts an eye-catching burst of bright red streaks emanating from the centre, hence the 'red' part of their name!
The flesh also stands out in flavour too. As well as having a slightly different texture to other varieties, red kiwis also wow the tastebuds with their savour: they are significantly sweeter and much more aromatic in flavour than the more commonly found green kiwi! Indeed, red kiwis are considered to be one of the best varieties of kiwi due to their divine sweetness (and excellent shelf life) and as such fetch a much higher market price than most other varieties!
Red kiwis are perfect for eating fresh out of hand. In fact, as they are less 'hairy' than green kiwis, they are more palatable for consumption without peeling! However, they are also ideal for slicing and adding to your breakfast cereals or porridge, mixing into yoghurt, creating colourful fruit salads, making cocktails and mocktails, and much more! Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some more recipe inspiration, including scrumptious kiwi bread!
Alongside being delectable and versatile, red kiwis are nutritionally beneficial too. In particular, they are excellent sources of vitamin C and dietary fibre.

Description:
One of the most highly-regarded items that we sell, leaf of life is a must-try for all!
The leaf of life plant, also known as 'miracle leaf' and 'life plant', is native to Madagascar but can be found all over the world.
The plant owes its name to its purported medical properties. The thick, curved leaves of this succulent, perennial plant have long been used in traditional medicine, with the juice of the leaves being a staple part of Jamaican medicine for centuries.
In culinary use, the leaves are usually consumed as tea, blended in juices, or eaten raw.

Lucuma can be cooked too - we'd particularly recommend simmering them into jams, syrups, and preserves! Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some more recipe inspiration!

Name: Lychee
Description:
Lychee are a must-try for all exotic fruit lovers!
These fruits native to China are small in size and round to oval in shape. They have thin, bumpy skin that delights the sight with its appealing reddish-pink hue (although some varieties are still green in colour even when fully mature).
Beneath the easily peelable skin of these plump, delightfully aromatic fruits is glistening translucent to opaque white flesh that has a delectably sweet, floral flavour, with musky, citrus undertones. We've noted hints of rose water, watermelon, strawberry, and melon, making each bite of these fruits a real taste sensation! The thick, juicy flesh is somewhat firm, and has a slight, soft crunch - the texture can be compared to that of a chewy, crisp grape. The flesh easily detaches from the medium/large, dark brown central seed which is inedible. We'd particularly recommend our new 'kway may pink' (also known as 'kwai mai pink') variety of lychee. Although these Chinese lychee are harvested later in the season than other types, they still have the spiked, reddish-pink shell and the delicious, sweet and juicy flesh that lychee are known for.
To best enjoy their amazing aroma (with notes of sweet fruits and roses) and flavour, simply consume them fresh out of hand, making sure to remove the skin and seed. However, they are well-suited to a number of culinary applications. They are commonly mixed into green and fruit salads and taste sublime when halved and served over desserts, ice cream, or shaved ice, or incorporated in recipes for puddings, custards, crumbles, cupcakes, and cakes. Lychees can additionally be simmered into sauces and spooned over seafood dishes, cooked into jams, or infused into syrups. Why not follow Haitian custom by stuffing lychees with cream cheese and topping them with macadamia nuts? Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some of our favourite recipes, including a nectarine and lychee cobbler!
As well as being delicious, lychee have been used in traditional Chinese medicine for centuries, and still today are valued for boasting many nutritional benefits. In particular, they are an excellent source of vitamin C and provide good amounts of potassium, dietary fibre, copper, and B vitamins.

Name: Mango - alphonso
Description:
Alphonso mangoes are known as the 'king of mangoes', and for good reason!
These small, somewhat egg-shaped mangoes from India first gained popularity in the UK after they were shipped to London for Queen Elizabeths coronation in 1953. They have smooth, golden-yellow skin, which, when the fruits are fully ripe, develops an eye-catching saffron hue and a red blush. Their aroma is second to none, filling the room with their intense tropical fragrance, and their flavour is similarly divine. One bite of their soft, immensely succulent flesh will leave you hungry for more, as your tastebuds are wowed by its creamy texture and rich sweetness. The flesh is also notably non-fibrous, which means alphonso mangoes are an easier - and infinitely less messy! - variety to devour.
Although best enjoyed fresh out of hand, mangoes are very versatile and are therefore well-suited to a number of culinary applications. They are ideal for adding a natural sweetness to your food and drink creation: they are especially perfect for creating smoothies and cocktails (or mocktails), and also make spectacular salsas, sorbets, and fruit salads! Why not respect their Indian roots by pureeing and mixing the mangoes with milk or cream and then using it as a delicious dipping sauce? Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some of our favourite recipes, including an amazing mango panna cotta!
As well as being mouthwateringly delectable, alphonso mangoes boast a number of nutritional benefits. In particular, they are an excellent source of potassium and magnesium.

Why not respect their Indian roots by pureeing and mixing the mangoes with milk or cream and then using it as a delicious dipping sauce? As well as being mouthwateringly delectable, alphonso mangoes boast a number of nutritional benefits. In particular, they are an excellent source of potassium and magnesium.

Name: Mango - ataulfo
Description:
Love mangoes but in need of a new variety to try? Our ataulfo mangoes from Mexico are just the thing for you!
Although they are slightly smaller than other mango varieties, ataulfo mangoes immediately catch the eye with their distinctive oblong shape and golden yellow skin. Beneath this smooth, delicate, aesthetically appealing skin is tender, velvety soft orange pulp (encasing a thin central seed) that emits a spectacular floral fragrance and is sure to wow your tastebuds with its divine sweetness and mouthwatering succulence. As well as being supremely aromatic, refreshing, and delectable, ataulfo mangoes are almost entirely fibreless, meaning that they are an easier - and infinitely less messy! - fruit to enjoy.
Whilst their nectar-sweet, melt-in-the-mouth flesh means they are best enjoyed when simply eaten fresh out of hand, ataulfo mangoes are also a superior culinary ingredient. Indeed, ataulfo mangoes are celebrated by many as the perfect all-round mango, and as a result have acquired the nickname 'champagne mango'! Whilst their sweetness makes them perfect for dessert recipes, they are very versatile and therefore can be used in a range of savoury applications too! We'd particularly recommend using them to make delicious jams and chutneys, blending them into smoothies, capitalising on their rich tropical savour to liven up your cocktails (and mocktails!), and stirring some into curries to balance out their spiciness. Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some of our favourite mango-based recipes, including an amazing mango sorbet!
As well as being brilliantly appetizing, ataulfo mangoes boast a range of nutritional benefits too. In particular, they are an excellent source of dietary fibre, are rich in vitamins A, B, and C, and provide a good amount of magnesium and potassium.
