Not only is the flesh of this wonderful fruit refreshing and supremely appetizing, but it is also not at all fibrous, which means that they are a much easier - and infinitely less messy! - ,mango variety to eat. Alongside being delectable when simply eaten fresh out of hand as a snack, badami mangoes' enchanting tropical flavour makes them ideal for use in a range of food and drink recipes too, from smoothies and cocktails (and mocktails!) to ice cream, cakes, and even curries! Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some of our favourite mango-based recipes.
As well as being delicious, badami mangoes also boast a wealth of nutritional benefits: like other mango varieties, they are an excellent source of dietary fibre, have a high content of vitamins A and C, and also include a good amount of magnesium and potassium.

Ready to eat once the mango yields to gentle pressure.

Quite simply, one can peel back the skin and eat the mango flesh directly from the central seed.

Alongside being ideal for making dipping sauces, sweet preserves, and pickles, they are also well-suited for combining in fruit and green salads, and for adding some exotic flavour to desserts, from sorbets and mousses to tarts and pies! As well as being versatile and imbued with a spectacular flavour, East Indian mangoes also possess many nutritional benefits. In particular, they are an excellent source of dietary fibre, are rich in calcium, and contain good amounts of potassium.

Name: Mango - kartha kolamban
Description:
Looking for a new mango variety to enjoy? Kartha kolamban mangoes are just the thing for you!
Our Sri Lankan kartha kolamban mangoes are medium to large in size and oblong in shape. They dazzle the eyes with their bright green peel, which is smooth, thin, and glossy. Beneath this aesthetically appealing skin is particularly dark orange flesh (kartha kolamban loosely translates to 'dark' or 'black') that has a wonderfully floral aroma and a sublime flavour similar to that of many other South Asian mango varieties found in India and Pakistan: one bite of these magnificent fruits is enough to wow your tastebuds, with a divine sweetness and intense tropical notes sure to please all mango lovers! They also have only minimal fibre, meaning they are an easier - and infinitely less messy! - mango variety to eat,
Like other mangoes, succulent kartha kolamban mangoes are best enjoyed when simply eaten fresh out of hand. However, they are also well-suited to any number of culinary applications. They are ideal for adding some natural sweetness to your food and drink creations, being perfect for creating smoothies and cocktails (or mocktails), salsas, sorbets, fruit salads, and more! Sour, unripe kartha kolamban mangoes can be utilised too - they make brilliant chutneys. Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some more recipe inspiration!
As well as being delectable and versatile, these mangoes also boast many nutritional benefits. In particular, they are an excellent source of vitamin C and dietary fibre, and are also rich in potassium and magnesium.

Name: Mango - kent
Description:
Kent mangoes are a must-try for all mango lovers!
We source our kent mangoes from Brazil and Peru. They are oval-shaped, plump mangoes, weighing around 400g-500g, and have delicate, smooth, yellow skin with a red blush. They have eye-catching bright orange flesh that is succulent (they are highly regarded for their juice content) and not at all fibrous, meaning they are a much easier - and infinitely less messy - mango to eat! The flavour of this firm flesh is divinely sweet, with a mild tropical flavour. There is a medium-sized seed encased within the flesh.
Our Brazilian kent mangoes have been hand-selected as first-class specimens. They are tree-ripened and should be almost ready to eat when they arrive at your address. The golden orange firm flesh is very sweet, juicy and fibreless. The skin ripens from green to orange-red. Our Peruvian kent mangoes are harvested a little earlier by the grower and will usually arrive with you less ripe than the Brazilian variety.
Although most commonly eaten simply fresh out of hand, they are also ideal for adding a natural sweetness to your food and drink creations. They are especially perfect for creating smoothies and cocktails (or mocktails), but are also well-suited for making salsas, sorbets, and spectacular fruit salads! Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some of our favourite recipes, including delightful mango and coconut trifles!
Our frozen kent mango pulp and frozen halves are just as delicious and almost as nutritious as the fresh mangoes themselves. For the pulp, we simply separate the juicy flesh from the skin and central seed, whereas the halves consist simply of mangoes split in two, with only the stone removed. Neither of them have added flavourings or additives, so you can be comfortable in knowing you're only consuming pure fruit. Once fully defrosted, they can be used in the same way as the fresh mangoes.
Both the fresh and frozen kent mangoes boast a number of nutritional benefits. In particular, they are rich in fibre, magnesium and potassium, and are an excellent source of vitamin C.

Name: Mango - kesar
Description:
Kesar mangoes are a must-try for mango lovers!
These mangoes, also known as 'gir kesar' mangoes, are one of the most popular mangoes in their native India - they're so renowned that they have earned the nickname the 'queen of mangoes', and for good reason!
Large in size and elongated in shape, kesar mangoes have thin, smooth skin that ripens from green to an eye-catching golden yellow (they are named after their colour, as kesar is the Hindi word for saffron!), often with a slight red blush. These mangoes have the divine floral aroma that is characteristic of mangoes from this part of South Asia, and their flavour is similarly superb. Their soft, tender, golden flesh is sublimely succulent - they truly melt in the mouth! - and delight the tastebuds with a delectably sweet and tropical flavour, with subtly tangy undertones due to their slight acidity.
Although kesar mangoes are best enjoyed fresh out of hand, they are also perfect for use in any number of food and drink recipes. Indeed, they are like other mangoes in being well-suited to both sweet and savoury culinary applications! Why not respect their Indian roots by pureeing and mixing the mangoes with milk or cream and then using it as a delicious dipping sauce? We'd recommend using them to make desserts such as sorbets, wonderful marmalades and chutneys, healthy smoothies or energising cocktails, or utilising them to add some fruity notes to your curries! Check out the 'Further information' tab below for recipe inspiration.
As well as being flavoursome and versatile, kesar mangoes boast a range of nutritional benefits. In particular, they are an excellent source of dietary fibre, have a high content of vitamins A and C, and also provide a good amount of magnesium and potassium.

Tab Content:Preparation:
Ready to eat once the mango yields to gentle pressure. 

Wash the mango first.

Quite simply, one can peel back the skin and eat the mango flesh directly from the central seed.

Alternatively, cut long ways along each side of the seed to separate the mango into 3 pieces. With a spoon, scoop the flesh from the two outer pieces. The flesh surrounding the seed shouldn't be wasted! Scrape off with a spoon or eat the mango flesh directly from the central seed. 

You may also use the 'hedgehog' method to prepare honey mangoes - score longways and crossways on the outer pieces and turn inside out to reveal many cubes of mango which can be easily removed from the skin.

Farmers then wait for the fruit to naturally fall from the tree, a sign that they are perfectly ripe. Even then, each fruit is rigorously tested for weight, sugar content, shape and appearance, meaning that only the best are chosen.
Such efforts mean you can be assured that each Miyasaki mango you receive is the best it could possibly be, offering an unrivalled taste experience.

Name: Mango - nam doc mai
Description:
One of the most popular mango cultivars and arguably the best dessert mango, Nam Doc Mai mangoes are an absolute must-try.
With an exceptional appearance and taste, it is unsurprising that these Thai mangoes are the most sought-after of the vast variety of Asian mangoes.
The fruits are long, slender and sigmoid, weighing from 12 to 16 ounces. When they are ripe, their smooth skin ranges from a greenish- to canary-yellow, sometimes boasting a reddish blush on the sun-exposed shoulder. Beneath their appealing skin is eye-catching, golden-orange flesh that will instantly fill the room with its intense tropical aroma, and will delight your tastebuds with its heavenly flavour: the firm flesh is completely fiberless, sublimely succulent, and wonderfully sweet.
Although unbelievably delicious when eaten fresh out of hand - the fact that their velvety smooth flesh is fibreless means they are an infinitely easier and less messy mango variety to eat too! - Nam Doc Mai mangoes are also extremely versatile, perfect for use in a number of sweet and savoury recipes. In Thailand and throughout much of Asia, they are commonly used while immature to make dipping sauces, sweet preserves, and pickles. They are also ideal for combining in fruit and green salads, and for adding some exotic flavour to desserts, from sorbets and mousses to tarts and pies! Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some recipe inspirations, including brilliant mango jam and Thai mango sticky rice!
As well as being versatile and imbued with a spectacular flavour, Nam Doc Mai mangoes also possess many nutritional benefits. In particular, they are an excellent source of dietary fibre, are rich in calcium, and contain good amounts of potassium.

Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some of our favourite mango-based recipes.
As well as being delicious, TJC mangoes also boast a wealth of nutritional benefits. Like other mango varieties, they are an excellent source of dietary fibre, have a high content of vitamins A and C, and additionally provide a good amount of magnesium and potassium.

Name: Mangosteen
Description:
Mangosteen are without a doubt one of the most exquisite fruits of the tropics - you're missing out if you don't try some!
In the late 19th century, it was rumoured Queen Victoria would grant a knighthood to anyone who brought her mangosteen. This, as well as its superb flavour, was enough to earn the mangosteen a new name, "the queen of fruits".
Still today, these small purple-skinned fruits are very highly regarded, and for good reason. Beneath their hard skin is fibrous, white, segmented flesh that is refreshingly juicy and has a delightful flavour: one bite of mangosteen's delicate flesh will dazzle your tongue with a distinctive combination of both sweet and citrus notes, and the succulent flesh will create an explosion of flavours in your mouth. We'd say the taste is most comparable to a mouthwatering mix of lychee, peach, grape and pineapple, although some people liken mangosteen to sherbet!
Mangosteen are most often eaten fresh out of hand, but they are also ideal for use in a variety of food and drink recipes. We'd particularly recommend using them to make scrumptious jams (perfect for adding some exotic flavour to your toast!), blending them to create creamy smoothies, and serving them with ice cream, a spectacularly flavoursome dessert. Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some of our favourite mangosteen recipes, including a heavenly panna cotta!
As well as being delicious, mangosteen also boast a myriad of nutritional benefits. For instance, they are an excellent source of fibre, are rich in vitamins C and B9, and contain many beneficial anti-oxidants, including xanthones, a unique plant compound believed to have strong antioxidant properties.

Still today, these small purple-skinned fruits are very highly regarded, and for good reason. Beneath their hard skin is fibrous, white, segmented flesh that is refreshingly juicy and has a delightful flavour: one bite of mangosteen's delicate flesh will dazzle your tongue with a distinctive combination of both sweet and citrus notes, and the succulent flesh will create an explosion of flavours in your mouth. We'd say the taste is most comparable to a mouthwatering mix of lychee, peach, grape and pineapple, although some people liken mangosteen to sherbet!
Mangosteen are most often eaten fresh out of hand, but they are also ideal for use in a variety of food and drink recipes. We'd particularly recommend using them to make scrumptious jams (perfect for adding some exotic flavour to your toast!), blending them to create creamy smoothies, and serving them with ice cream, a spectacularly flavoursome dessert. Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some of our favourite mangosteen recipes, including a heavenly panna cotta!
As well as being delicious, mangosteen also boast a myriad of nutritional benefits. For instance, they are an excellent source of fibre, are rich in vitamins C and B9, and contain many beneficial anti-oxidants, including xanthones, a unique plant compound believed to have strong antioxidant properties.

Name: Medlar
Description:
Cultivated since the Roman period, medlars' delicious flavour makes them a popular choice among fruit lovers even today!
Medlar are a small fruit that looks like a cross-between of a small apple and a rosehip. When ripe and ready to harvest, medlar are hard and acidic, but become edible after being 'bletted'. Bletting is a process whereby the fruits soften through exposure to frost or being kept in cold storage. The process can take a long time but the delicious taste makes them worth the wait!
Once softening begins, the skin rapidly takes on a wrinkled texture and turns dark brown. As such, a softened fruit can look as if it has spoiled, but don't worry, this actually means that they are at the perfect stage for consumption! Once fully ripe, the flesh gains an almost liquid consistency and has a multi-layered flavour that is rich and complex: some people compare the sweet taste to dates, whilst others say the flavour is reminiscent of toffee apples or apple sauce. Either way, this unique flavour is sure to wow your tastebuds!
Although, once fully bletted, they are most often eaten raw - they are scrumptious with creme fraiche or yoghurt or as an accompaniment to cheese - medlars can be used for a variety of culinary applications. As medlars are high in pectin, they are ideal for making jelly, and it is also popular to turn these fruits into medlar cheese, a type of curd made with sugar, butter, and eggs.
As well as being delectable, medlars boast a range of nutritional benefits: they are rich in vitamins C and B and are a good source of protein, calcium, and iron.
Our frozen perfectly-ripe whole medlar fruits are just as healthy and delectable as the fresh fruit themselves, and they keep for up to a month in the freezer, so they are perfect for those who want their medlar to last for longer.

Tab Content:Preparation:
Fresh: always wash first. Once the medlar are ripe (very-soft all over), the skin should be peeled, or slice in half and scoop the thick pulp out. The seeds are not eaten.

Frozen: defrost fully.
Tab Content:Usage:
Fresh: eat raw, after bletting, or use to make medlar jelly and medlar cheese.

Frozen: defrost fully and then use to make jelly or cheese.
Tab Content:Storage:
Fresh: keep in a cool, dry area. Check regularly and turn to encourage even ripening. Eventually the medlar will ripen but it can take weeks!

Frozen: refrigerate and use within 3-5 days or re-freeze immediately upon delivery and use within a month.

Name: Melon - raiden melon (luxury fruit for gifting)
Description:
The Raiden melon, named after the coast in Hokkaido, Japan, is a premium melon, beloved for its succulent flesh that melts in the mouth. You wont taste another like it!
Juicy, mellow and richly sweet, the Raiden melon Is the result of a labour of love and meticulous care. They are grown with green onions as companion plants, a cultivation method recognised by the Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries. This gives them a natural pesticide, ensuring that they are grown with a reduced dependency on chemicals. Once grown, each melon must pass a rigorous screening process that checks for visual impact and a minimum sugar content of 16 brix.
The result is a finely netted melon that is unlike any you will have tried before. Uniquely tender and sweet, Reward yourself with the exceptional taste of Japan with every bite.

Name: Melon - snowball
Description:
Looking for a new melon to try? We have just the thing for you!
Snowball melons - also known as 'dino melons' due to their apparent resemblance to dinosaur eggs! - are small- to medium-sized melons from Brazil that will wow your tastebuds with their incredibly refreshing, crisp taste!
Beneath their dazzling speckled white skin is white flesh that is extremely succulent and sweet. Although the sweetest and juiciest flesh is at the centre of the melon, all of the flesh is supremely delectable, and an added bonus is that the rind is very thin, so there's more flesh for your money!
Snowball melons are best enjoyed when simply eaten fresh out of hand - they make the perfect refreshing snack! However, they can also be in sweet and savoury recipes like other melon varieties: you incorporate slices into fruit and green salads, yoghurts, and cereals, make thirst-quenching fruity juices and smoothies, create delectable sorbet, and much more! Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some more recipe inspiration, including strawberry, melon, and ginger sundaes!
As well as being delicious, snowball melons boast many nutritional benefits. In particular, they are rich in potassium and are an excellent source of vitamin C.

Name: Melon - yubari king melon (luxury fruit for gifting)
Description:
Meet the worlds most luxury melon, the Yubari King melon.
As one of the most expensive fruits in Japan, the Yubari King melon is highly regarded and sought after. So much so, that each year their harvesting peak is celebrated at the Yubari melon festival with an auction. Theyre so renowned, that one year, a pair of Yubari king melons sold for an incredible 5 million yen! (Thats £25,000!).
It takes incredible patience and dedication to grow a Yubari king melon, as well as perfect conditions. Its so aligned with its environment that attempts to grow it elsewhere consistently fail to match the same extraordinary quality.
Their journey begins in the winter in heated greenhouses. In Spring, farmers lay mats underneath to help them grow into perfect spheres with just the right amount of sunlight. At harvest, Yubari king melons are rigorously inspected for sugar content, net pattern, shape and size and only the best are sold.
Such strict measures make for a melon with a extremely soft and juicy flesh, a strong tropical aroma and a wonderful sweetness. In fact, some people find the Yubari so sweet that they prefer to enjoy with a glass of water.
Such a premium melon makes for an extremely prestigious gift. In fact, they are frequently exchanged in Japan during formal ceremonies, celebrations or to express gratitude in a gesture of respect and goodwill.
They are a variety that ripen quicker than others. Therefore, it's exceptionally unsuual to see them outside of Japan.
Gift the Yubari king melon to someone truly special or indulge in the luxury yourself.

Name: Papaya (Brazil)
Description:
Papayas are mouthwatering and incredibly nutritious fruits that all exotic fruit lovers need to try!
Papayas are elongated to spherical shape and can be as long as 50cm (although the fruits we receive from our farmers are usually 20cm to 30cm in length). Their smooth, glossy skin is deep green in colour when the fruits are immature, however the skin develops orange-yellow hues as the fruits ripen.
Beneath their appealing skin is bright orange flesh encasing a cavity filled with many black seeds, each seed surrounded by a bubble of flavourless jelly. Both the flesh and seeds are edible! Once the papaya is fully ripe, the eye-catching flesh becomes so soft that it boasts a butter-like consistency, and this wonderfully creamy flesh wows with its combination of sweet notes - hints of mango, peach, and banana can be detected! - and distinctively musky undertones. The crunchy seeds contribute to the unique flavour profile of papaya, as they taste just like pepper!
As well as simply eating the flesh and seeds out of hand, papayas are also perfect for use in any number of sweet and savoury recipes! Passion Fruit acquired its name from Spanish missionaries who saw the plant's distinctly shaped flower as a symbol of Christ's crucifixion.

Name: Hakuto premium peaches (luxury fruit for gifting)
Description:
Introducing the Hakuto peach from Yamanashi.
Yamanshi sits at the heart of Japans reputation for world-renowned fruit cultivation. As the peach capital, Yamanshi is the perfect environment for growing high sugar low acid peaches, and there is no peach more delicious than the Hakuto.
The Hakuto peach is a highly popular variety of Japanese white peach, a cross between Hakuto (white peach) and Kishu Hayase. Known for its fragrant sweetness, juiciness and fine-textured flesh, Hakuto are almost buttery when perfectly ripe. The fruit has a plump white skin, which blushes red on the side exposed to sunlight.
Beneath their delicate skin is a fine-textured, juicy and deliciously aromatic flesh with a high sugar content, typically ranging from 12 to 14 on the Brix scale and ideal for those who prefer sweet fruits.
Each peach is meticulously hand-grown in controlled conditions. They are convered with small paper bags while they are green to encourage them to grow pale and sweet. Harvesting is a delicate process, plucked by hand.
During summer gift-giving season, chugen, these peaches are a prized gift to give loved ones or important clients.
Treat yourself or someone special to the sweetest, softest peach youll ever taste! Truly a one of a kind taste experience.

Tab Content:Origin: The Yamanshi prefecture is the main production area, renowned for its high-quality peaches and often referred to as the ‘Peach Capital’ of Japan.
Tab Content:Preparation: Yamanashi peaches are best enjoyed slightly cooled. Store your peaches in the fridge for 2-3 hours before you’re ready to eat them. Once chilled gently peel the skin with fingers and slice into wedges.
Tab Content:Usage: Eat fresh out of hand or pair with ice cream or mascarpone.
Tab Content:Storage:
Store at room temperature and refrigerate before eating.

Japanese peaches are fragile like tofu and have a special way of handling them to ensure they are not damaged.

When picking up the peaches, do not rely on your fingers alone. Instead, gently hold the foam net around the peach to pick it up. Place the peach in your other hand and wrap it in your palms, then hold it securely.

To temporarily remove the foam net around the peach and check for any flaws, use your palms to handle the fruit. Ensure that only your palms touch the peach throughout the process, avoiding the use of your fingers.

If you want to remove the foam net, hold the peach in one palm and gently place it upside down onto the other palm.

Description:
Experience the taste of autumn in Japan with Fuyu persimmon.
Widely regarded as a traditional autumn treat (persimmon is the national fruit of Japan!), Fuyu persimmon is an ancient delicacy. Of the 1000 varieties in Japan, Fuyu stands out as one of the most popular persimmons in the world.
Beneath glossy orange and satisfyingly crisp skin is a melt-in-the-mouth sweet flesh that will keep you hooked. Their taste is very sweet with hints of cinnamon, honey and brown sugar.
They are non astringent and offer different flavours at different stages of ripeness. As the fruit ripens, it becomes softer and juicier with a gloriously intensified sweetness.
Our black sesame persimmons are just as sweet and juicy, while being even more unique. An uncommon black-flesh variety, these persimmons get their colour from a specific growing method. The fruits are exposed to sunlight for a longer period of time and picked only when completely mature, creating a deeper sweetness and a non-astringent texture.
Although best enjoyed simply eaten fresh out of hand, Japanese persimmons are very versatile, being suited to a range of culinary applications whether they are firm and dense or have the softness and squishiness of full maturity. We'd especially recommend cooking them into jams and chutneys, adding slices to fruit salads, chopping them into salsas, and incorporating them into sweet baked goods such as tarts and pies!
As well as being versatile, Japanese persimmons are a good source of vitamin A and C, as well as dietary fibre and antioxidants.

How to make physalis jam;

Ingredients: 100g physalis without husk, 330ml water, 1 lime, 40g sugar jelly, half an orange

Name: Pineapple - baby pineapple
Description:
Love pineapples? Our two varieties of baby pineapples - phulae pineapples (also known as 'Phu Lae') from the Nang Lae district of Thailand and Queen Victoria pineapples from Bangladesh and Mauritius - are just the thing for you!
In appearance, baby pineapples are almost identical to regular pineapples, varying only in their slightly more rounded shape and miniature size. Called 'baby' pineapples, it's no surprise that they are much smaller than pineapples you can find in supermarkets - they typically measure approximately 5 inches long and 3 inches wide.
Like their larger sister fruits, they have an intense fragrance that fills the room, with many regarding them as more aromatic than regular pineapples. Beneath their eye-catching, golden outer casing is yellow flesh which delights the tastebuds with its sugar-sweet taste, containing little to no acidity. As well as being favoured for their succulence and sweetness, baby pineapples are also loved by exotic fruit fans due to the fact that they have a much softer core than regular pineapples - unlike supermarket-bought pineapples, you can easily eat the core, and do not need to discard it! Our phulae pineapples are especially juicy and sweet, and are accordingly one of the most popular pineapples in Thailand, which is impressive considering the country cultivates at least 27 different varieties of the fruit! Indeed, phulae pineapples are a rare and expensive delicacy in their native Thailand, where they are sold at 10 times the price of other pineapples due to their superior flavour!
The best way to enjoy this wonderful fruit is to simply devour the flesh. For instance, on the streets of Southeast Asian countries, pieces of baby pineapple are sold as refreshing snacks to provide much-needed coolness and hydration in the scorching summer months. However, there are innumerable culinary applications for baby pineapple, with these versatile fruits suiting both sweet and savoury recipes! They are perfect for adding some tropical flavour to fruit salads and creating stunning smoothies, and taste divine when served grilled with chicken. From barbecuing to blending, the list of opportunities is endless! Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some recipe inspiration, including a pineapple and rambutan fruit salad!
As well as being extremely delectable, baby pineapples boast many nutritional benefits. In particular, they are an excellent source of dietary fibre, and are packed with vitamins and minerals, including vitamin B, iron, calcium, and zinc.

Name: Pineapple - golden 'MD2'
Description:
Our MD2 pineapples are one of the most popular pineapple varieties in the world, and for good reason!
This hybrid pineapple variety was first developed in the 1970s. MD2 was originally known as 73-114 but it was later renamed MD2, in honour of Millie Dillard, the wife of the then General Manager of the Maui Pineapple Company (which oversaw the initial cultivation of the variety).
Before MD2 pineapples, most people outside of the tropics only ate canned pineapple. MD2 pineapples were therefore grown to satisfy the growing demand for fresh pineapples and they succeeded! Since the inception of commercial production in the 1980s, MD2 pineapples have been highly praised not only for their exceptional sweetness, but also for their consistency in size and ripeness.
After being wowed by beholding the uniformly bright gold colour of these appealing pineapples, your tastebuds will be delighted by the supreme succulence and richly sweet savour of their crunchy golden flesh! It's no wonder then that these glorious pineapples are regarded by many as the superior variety. Indeed, so renowned are these brilliant fruits that they command around three times the price of other more commonly found pineapple varieties!
These divinely delectable fruits are best enjoyed when simply eaten fresh out of hand, particularly because they are less acidic and less fibrous than other varieties. However, we'd also recommend substituting standard, supermarket-bought pineapples for these spectacular MD2 pineapples in your favourite sweet and savoury pineapple recipes. From refreshing juices and fiery cocktails to cooling sorbets and scrumptious cakes, the list is almost endless! Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some more recipe inspiration, including a delectable pineapple and prawn curry.
As well as being delicious and versatile, pineapples are also nutritionally valuable. In particular, they are an excellent source of vitamin C - they boast four times the amount of vitamin C as other varieties! - and are rich in dietary fibre.

Name: Pineapple - snack pineapple (luxury fruit for gifting)
Description:
Also known as Bogor pineapples, these Japanese snack pineapples boast a unique feature that sets them apart: they can be pulled-apart using just your hands!
The bright yellow flesh is so soft and tender that it breaks apart easily from the core, making it great for a snack. The core is edible, too, with a delicious crispness and soft texture so unlike the hard cores of supermarket pineapples. Their sweetness is so pronounced that it exceeds 20 brix during peak harvest season, making snack pineapples truly deserving of all their high praise.
The process of growing snack pineapples is a labour-intensive one, beginning two years before harvest, and involving a strict regimen of mowing, shading and fertiliser management. Pineapples do not ripen, so it is down to the expertise of the farmer to know when the optimal time for harvest is. An incorrectly times harvest can ruin the balance of sweetness, so it is only through years of experience that they are perfect every time.
With such a high sugar content and a low acidity, these snack pineapples are almost candy-like in their natural sweetness, and would make the perfect gift to a fruit-loving loved one, or even a special treat for yourself! Treat yourself to a unique and delicious summer time treat.

Name: Potato - beni haruka sweet potato (luxury fruit for gifting)
Description:
Out of the 40-60 varieties of sweet potato grown in Japan, Beni Haruka are one of the most popular. Some go as far as to suggest that they sparked the baked sweet potato boom in Japan!
Though this variety is relatively new, they have quickly gained popularity for their soft, almost chewy texture, and their outstanding natural sweetness often compared to honey. They also have a high water content which makes for a moist, buttery texture.
In shape, Beni Haruka potatoes are much like other sweet potatoes, thin and perfect for slicing and mashing. Their moist texture make them ideal for baking. In fact, baking on a lower heat for longer unlocks Beni Harukas natural sweetness. Just add butter for a sweet, buttery treat.
As well as being divinely soft and sweet, Beni Haruki are rich in B vitamins and dietary fibre, making them not only the tasty choice, but the healthy one too.
Treat yourself to one of the sweetest, softest Japanese sweet potato and bake, roast, mash or fry for a luxurious snack or as part of a meal. Gift to someone who enjoys trying new things or treat yourself to one of the best sweet potatoes money can buy.

Name: Potato - purple, sweet
Description:
Not only are sweet potatoes one of the oldest-cultivated foods in the world - remnants of sweet potatoes have been found that date back over 8000 years! - but they are also one of the healthiest, with purple sweet potatoes in particular being hailed as a 'superfood' due to their supposed ability to extend life expectancy!
In shape, purple sweet potatoes resemble other sweet potato varieties. However, they excel in flavour. Although their deep purple flesh is denser and drier than most sweet potato varieties, it wows the tastebuds with its intensely rich flavour that combines both sweet and savoury notes and boasts an almost wine-like savour! Once boiled and coated with a tad of melted butter, these potatoes gain a delightfully creamy texture, making them simply divine!
Purple sweet potatoes' starchy texture means they are best suited to cooked applications such as boiling, mashing, frying, or baking, although please note that their crumbly flesh takes longer to cook than that of regular potatoes. They are also ideal for adding some subtle sweetness to salads, curries, and soups, and are perfect for bringing eye-catching colour to your mealtimes, such as dazzling purple jacket potatoes and chips! Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some of our favourite recipes, including a scrumptious purple sweet potato pie!
As well as being supremely delectable, purple sweet potatoes are renowned for being far more nutritious than supermarket-bought potatoes, boasting a higher content of dietary fibre and being lower in both carbohydrates and calories! Purple sweet potatoes also contain anthocyanin (the natural compound that gives the potatoes their striking purple hue!), a powerful antioxidant linked to numerous health benefits, and they are additionally rich in potassium, iron, folate, and vitamins A and C.

Name: Plum mango
Description:
Love plums and mangoes? Our plum mangoes are just the things for you!
Plum mangoes, also known as 'Maprong mangoes' and 'Marian plums', are closely related to the mango.
They are small fruits and have a size and shape roughly comparable to an egg. They have thin, smooth skin that ripens from green to a dazzlingly bright orange-yellow hue.
Although in appearance plum mangoes do not resemble their namesakes, once you cut into the flesh you will realise how they gained their title. The first hint is given by their aroma: the fruits emit a divine mango-like fragrance that wows your senses.
It is the flesh's flavour and texture though that really give plum mangoes their name. In texture, the fruits are often said to be comparable to plums: the orange flesh (encasing a bitter but edible central seed) offers an initial crispy bite, but then reveals its soft, jelly-like (and slightly fibrous) texture. In flavour, however, the fruits are regularly likened to mangoes, as they delight the tastebuds with a sweet taste and subtle notes of tartness.
Whilst plum mangoes are most commonly eaten fresh out of hand, they are ideal for a number of culinary uses. We'd recommend adding them to fruit salads and using them to make mouthwatering pickles, chutneys, and compotes. Check out the 'Further information' tab below for more recipe inspiration.
As well as being delicious, plum mangoes boast a number of nutritional benefits. In particular, they are an excellent source of dietary fibre and vitamin C.

As well as being delicious, plum mangoes boast a number of nutritional benefits. In particular, they are an excellent source of dietary fibre and vitamin C.

Name: Rose apple
Description:
Rose apples are a refreshing fruit from South Asia with a delicate flavour and crisp texture.
An aesthetically appealing fruit, rose apples have a distinctively elongated, bell-like shape and their skin boasts a glossy shine. The smooth, delicate skin has a wax like texture, which is the reason why the fruit is often referred to as 'wax apple'.
Beneath their attractive exterior is white or pink flesh which is fragrant, crisp, and extremely juicy. In fact, rose apples are one of the most succulent fruits we've ever tried: they consist of over 90% water, so it's not surprising that these 'water apples' are considered ideal for quenching thirst! The usually seedless flesh is subtly sweet, offering hints of watermelon and apple flavour.
Whilst immature green rose apples are perfect for making delicious pickles and chutneys and combining into salads, the riper red-skinned fruits are usually eaten fresh out of hand (especially because you don't need to peel them!)

RECIPE
Rojak Buahan (Spicy Tropical Fruit Salad)

Recipe courtesy of Raffles Hotel, Singapore.

Serves 4

Salad - 8 Red Rose Apple - ripe, 200g baby Pineapple, 200g half-ripe Papaya, 200g half-ripe Mango, 1 Thai Guava

Sambal Rojak - 80ml Tamarind Juice, 12g Sugar, 15ml Lime juice, 30g Sambal Chilli, 60g black Shrimp paste

Sauce - 160g Sambal Rojak, 60g lukewarm water

Garnish - 16 Lettuce leaves, 10g toasted Sesame seeds, 4 Wanton skins (sliced into 1-2cm strips), 60g cooking oil

Peel and cut each fruit into cubes of about 1cm. Set aside. Heat oil in a wok and deep fry the wanton skins until golden brown. Remove and place on an absorbent paper towel to drain off the excess oil. Set aside. Arrange lettuce leaves on a plate. Place the diced fruit on the leaves and pour the sauce over the fruit. Name: Sapodilla - 'the brown sugar fruit'
Description:
Sapodillas are a must-try for exotic fruit lovers!
Popular across the world, particularly South and Southeast Asia, South America and the Caribbean, these small, round-to-oval fruits are sure to wow your tastebuds with their delicious flavour! Beneath their smooth, thin, brownish-orange skin is soft, pulpy flesh - similar in texture to pears - that is sublimely sweet, with divine notes of brown sugar, caramel and molasses. Indeed, the fruits are so well-known for their sweetness that they have gained the nickname 'brown sugar fruits'! Within the flesh, there are inedible black seeds that need to be removed before consumption.
Although commonly enjoyed fresh out of hand, sapodillas' malty flavour means they are also well-suited for use in a number of sweet and savoury recipes. Whether blending the flesh into milkshakes and smoothies, mixing it into green and fruit salads, simmering it into jams and chutneys, or incorporating it into desserts such as tarts and custards, you will not be disappointed! Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some recipe inspiration, including a chocolate milkshake that, intriguingly, doesn't include chocolate!
As well as being supremely delectable, sapodillas also boast many nutritional benefits. In particular, they are an excellent source of dietary fibre, provide good amounts of vitamins A and C, and are rich in tannins, compounds that have anti-inflammatory properties.

Name: Sapodilla 'caramel'
Description:
The caramel sapodilla is a superior variety from Vietnam which are around 3 to 4 times larger than the sapodilla we sell that come from Thailand and India. The texture of the Vietnamese sapodilla is perfectly smooth, one of the softest and smoothest fruits you will ever try.
The flavour is divine, reminiscent of caramel and brown sugar and the reason we put the caramel sapodilla in our list of top 10 fruits! Simply wait to ripen then eat out of hand or mix in a blender with almond milk and cinammon for the ultimate smoothie.
Sapodilla was imported to Vietnam a long time ago. In the last 20 years, sapodilla has been widely planted in the north, where it grew for the first time in Xuan Dinh, Tu Liem district, Hanoi.
Sapodilla fruit is shaped like an egg and weighs from 10 to 200 grams. Its peel is brown with tiny cracks near the stalk. The pulp, which is brown and yellow, is very juicy and smells very sweet. When it is not ripe, it is not edible because it contains a lot of sticky resin.
There are two popular species of sapodilla grown in Vietnam: orange pulp and white-yellow pulp sapodilla. The orange pulp sapodilla is planted in the north on the highlands. The pulp of the white-yellow sapodilla is light yellow or yellow and the peel is green or yellow. The peel is thin; the pulp is soft and has taste of peach, banana, and apple.
Sapodilla flower consecutively bloom in bunches so that it has fruits to offer throughout the year.

Description:
Have you heard of the sour berries with exceptional antioxidant properties?
Seabuck thorn is a thicket-forming shrub with dense thorny twigs. In the autumn, the shrub transforms as it fills with bright glossy orange berries. Name: Sea moss (Barbados)
Description:
Sea Moss is a species of red algae which grows abundantly along the rocky parts of the Atlantic coast of Europe and North America.
Our sea moss is from the Caribbean islands and sold in 100g packets (unprocessed) and 50g packets (natural debris removed, cleaned and separated into small pieces). You'll notice that the price for the 50g packets is almost the same as the 100g packets as it's particularly time-consuming to clean and sort the sea moss once it's been removed from the ocean.
It's an industrial source of carrageenan, which is the main reason for cultivation however due to a high nutrient density, it's also grown and dried then exported around the world to be used as a healthy supplement to a balanced diet.
Culinary uses of sea moss vary across the world. In Ireland and parts of Scotland, it's boiled in milk and strained, before sugar and other flavourings such as vanilla, cinnamon, brandy, or whiskey are added. The end product is a kind of jelly similar to pannacotta.
Similarly, in Jamaica and Trinidad and Tobago, it's boiled with cinnamon and milk to make a thick drink called Irish moss that is believed to be an aphrodisiac.
In Venezuela it has been used for generations as a home remedy for sore throat and chest congestion, boiled in milk and served with honey before bed.

Wash the sea moss first and remove any debris which may remain after it was harvested from the ocean. Our 50g packets of 'cleaned' sea moss have a majority of the natural debris removed before being packaged.

There are multiple ways to prepare sea moss - here is a suggestion: Pour 3 litres of water into a pot, bring to the boil then add sea moss and linseed. After 30 minutes add nutmeg and a further 500ml of water. Stir constantly. Boil for a further 30 minutes, strain off the liquid and place the contents into a clean container and allow to cool then stir in milk of your choice and vanilla essence. Add brown sugar or honey to taste. Blend to make a healthy smoothie. Keep refrigerated.

Name: Sea moss (St Lucia and Jamaica)
Description:
Our sea moss from St Lucia and Jamaica is wild grown and hand harvested from the warm waters of the Caribbean sea that surround the island. It's dried in the sun after harvest.

Name: Sea spaghetti
Description:
Why not replace spaghetti with seaweed in your next pasta dish? Our sea spaghetti is a must try for any foodie!
Named for its spaghetti shape, sea spaghetti is a brown seaweed commonly found in the northeast Atlantic ocean but is most common around the British isles. It can grow up to 2-3m tall!
Though sea spaghetti is saltier than other seaweeds, the taste can be altered through preparation. Soak the seaweed for 3-4 minutes in clean water or vinegar and repeat if seaweed still appears salty.
After preparation, they are perfect for incorporating into a variety of dishes. Sea spaghetti adds a beefy flavour to soup, stews and casseroles and tastes deliciously nutty-like when used in salads. But perhaps their best usage is alongside a pasta sauce, where they can offer a great low carb pasta or noodle alternative. They could even be cooked alongside regular spaghetti for an interesting combination.
However you use them, they will definitely bring freshness and a striking visual contrast to your meals!
As well as this, they are rich in fibre and contain an array of other healthy nutrients and minerals too, including magnesium, iron and calcium.

Description:
Soursop, also known as graviola, guanabana, and guyabano is a delicious fruit in high demand because of the health benefits it's believed to have.

Name: Coquito nut - the World's smallest coconut!
Description:
Introducing the world's smallest coconuts! Coquito nuts are the full-size fruits of the Chilean wine palm. Though they taste and look like coconuts, they differ on two points. One is that they contain no liquid and the other is that they are tiny!
After discarding the tough shell (see the Further information tab below for more detailed instructions), you can eat these small nuts whole. Their white flesh is firm and crunchy with a rich coconut flavour and a nutty sweetness reminiscent of almonds.
Though wonderful eaten fresh out of hand, coquito nuts are very versatile. Locals enjoy them raw and cooked. Chop and add to salads, dip in chocolate as a sweet snack or incorporate into cookies and cakes.
As well as being versatile, coquito coconuts also boast a range of nutritional benefits including being a good source of fibre and vitamin C.

Name: Soursop - dried soursop 'soft, sweet and chewy'
Description:
Our dried soursop from Sri Lanka is a must-try for all exotic fruit lovers!
These delicious dried soursop pieces are made by dehydrating the flesh of ripe soursop fruits. The soft, fully matured fruits are harvested from the tree, cleaned, and then the skin and seeds are separated from the flesh. The flesh is dehydrated until only around 10% of the moisture remains.
The result is a flavourful delight! The texture is soft and chewy - in texture, dried soursop is similar to other dried fruits like dried banana and dried mango - and your tastebuds will be wowed by the delectable combination of both sweet and tangy notes! Being made of 100% pure fruit, it's not surprising that our dried soursop captures the sweet-sour flavour of fresh soursop!
Dried soursop makes the perfect on-the-go snack: conveniently packed in small packets, they are ideal for stashing in your bag and munching as you travel! To make it even tastier, why not mix the dried soursop with other dried fruits and nuts to make a healthy snacking mixture?
As well as being supremely appetizing, our dried soursop is nutritionally beneficial too! Being made from 100% soursop, dried soursop contains many of the healthful benefits of fresh soursop fruit; with no nasty chemicals, preservatives, flavourings, or sweeteners added, you can be confident in knowing that you're consuming only natural goodness!

Name: Soursop leaves dried
Description:
While the fresh soursop fruit is widely used for tasty desserts and juices, the leaves have long been used to make tea to be used in traditional medicine in various cultures.
Our air-dried soursop leaves are currently sourced from various suppliers in Mauritius, Sri Lanka, Vietnam and St Lucia. Some of the leaves are air-dried at source whilst others are transported to us fresh then we air-dry, hand sort and pack them here in the UK.
Our St Lucian dried soursop leaves are organically grown leaves which are harvested by hand in small batches and washed in spring water. They are harvested at the last possible opportunity before being packed for export meaning they are the freshest leaves we can source. In order to maintain a good crop of soursop fruits, there are limits on how many leaves can be cut from the tree each week so we only receive them in small quantities.
The soursop leaves are sold in 10g packets which usually contain 20 to 30 leaves, and larger 50g packets which usually contain between 100 to 150 leaves.

Description:
Here in the UK, most people use dried soursop leaves for making soursop tea however we're now seeing an increased demand for fresh leaves as some people consider these to be nutritionally optimal. From our experience, we find that both the fresh and dried leaves produce a good quality and pleasant-tasting tea.

Due to the need to sell the fresh soursop leaves quickly and a risk of wastage, most companies only handle the dried leaves. We receive fresh soursop leaves by air from the tropics just a day or two after harvest and ship them to customers usually within 48 hours of arrival in the UK.

As far as we are aware, we are one of only a few companies in the UK to provide both fresh and dried soursop leaves.

We usually supply the fresh soursop leaves on the branches as this means they will stay fresher for longer.

We can accept wholesale orders for soursop leaves and can offer a discounted rate. Please email us for further information.

Please order by 8pm Sunday to ensure delivery the following week.

Name: Sugarcane
Description:
Sugarcane - the origin of sugar!
Fresh sugarcane can be used to make juice by passing through a manual or electric press. More simply, one can remove the outer layer with a sharp knife and chew the remaining internal part of the cane to extract the sweet delicious juice.
The canes are not only used for their juice. but also in culinary preparations. They can be divided into thin sections and used as a natural skewer to impart a natural flavour onto the meat, fish and vegetables added to the skewer.
Some bartenders split the cane into thin narrow pieces and add them to cocktails to be used as a stirrer.
Our sugarcane can't be re-grown.
CategoryManagement: Home > Shop Online > Sweet Fruits:Home > Shop Online
MetaDescription: Buy fresh sugarcane online - naturally sweet, juicy, and perfect for juicing, snacking or using in culinary preparations such as making a stirrer for cocktails.
Related Products: Mango - sugar,Sapodilla - 'the brown sugar fruit',Tamarillo - red,Sea moss (Barbados)
Tab Content:Preparation:
Wash the outer layer well first before removing with a sharp knife - taking care to not cut your fingers!

To extract the juice either chew directly on the internal part of the sugar cane or pass through a manual / electric press. When chewing on the cane directly it's preferable to cut into smaller bite-size pieces.

The pure sugar cane juise is sometimes mixed with water and more commonly, various types of fresh citrus juice to balance the sweetness.
Tab Content:Usage:
Sugarcane has a multitude of uses. The primary use of fresh sugar cane is to make juice however around the world it's used in the following ways;

- to make soup (Sayur nganten, Indonesia)

- to make molasses and syrup.

- to make Jaggery, which is a solidified molasses. It's produced by evaporating the sugarcane juice to make a thick sludge, and then cooling until it sets.

- to make various alcoholic beverages including falernum, cachaça, basi and rum.

- to make flour (rapadura, Latin America and the Caribbean)
Tab Content:Storage: Keep refrigerated at all times to prevent the sugar cane from drying out.

Name: Snake fruit - salak pondoh, Indonesia
Description:
Salak is the fruit of a species of palm tree, native to Java and Sumatra in Indonesia. Snake fruit, as it's also called, thanks to its brown scaly skin, has a good keep quality. Peeling the thin skin will reveal 3 lobes, cream to yellow in colour containing 2 or 3 inedibe seeds. They are about the size and shape of a mature fig. The taste can be compared to that of an apple and pineapple.
The texture varies between cultivars, salak pondoh having a crisp and crunchy feel in the mouth.
Salak pondoh is grown in abundance in the Yogyakarta province on the island of Java, Indonesia. It's popularity in Indonesia, compared to other cultivars, is mainly due to the intensity of its aroma the well balanced sweet flavour and low cost.
There are three commonly found cultivars of salak which are pondoh, bali and gula pasir. Typically, pondoh are the largest in size.

Description:
Salak is a species of palm tree native to Java and Sumatra in Indonesia.
The taste is usually sweet and acidic at the same time, but its apple-like texture can vary from very dry and crumbly (salak pondoh from Yogyakarta) to moist and crunchy (salak Bali). The taste is often compared to a rich pineapple flavour with a hint of fizziness.
The fruits grow in clusters at the base of the palm, and are also known as snake fruit due to the reddish-brown scaly skin.
They are about the size and shape of a ripe fig, with a distinct tip. The pulp is edible. The fruit can be peeled by pinching the tip, which should cause the skin to slough off so it can be pulled away.
The fruit inside consists of two or three lobes with the two larger ones, or even all three, containing a large inedible seed. The lobes resemble, and have the consistency of, large peeled garlic cloves.
As well as being delicious, salacca boasts numerous health benefits. In particular, it is extremely rich in iron, providing 30% of your daily required amount, and provides a good amount of vitamin C.

Name: Star apple - fresh and frozen
Description:
Star apples are a must-try for exotic fruit lovers!
Star apples are small to medium in size - they usually measure about 5-10cm in diameter - and perfectly round in shape. They have delicate, glossy skin that ripens to either a vibrant green or a dazzling purple hue.
Beneath their smooth, attractive skin is a thin layer of rind: the rind is dark purple in purple star apples, whereas in green star apples it is white. Whilst the rind of purple star apples is typically much thicker, please note that in both varieties the rind contains a sticky latex that is inedible.
At the core of these aromatic fruits is tender, white or purple pulp that wows with its radiating star pattern (hence the nickname 'star apple'!) The soft pulp excites the tastebuds too with its delicious flavour: once you've discarded the inedible seeds, you can enjoy the sweet, juicy jelly-like flesh and be delighted by its combination of notes of lychee, persimmons, and rambutans! For those with a sweet tooth, we'd particularly recommend the purple star apples, as these are usually packed with more sweetness, however some fruit fans prefer green star apples due to their thinner skin and slightly greater density of pulp.
Star apples are best enjoyed when simply eaten fresh out of hand, especially because this is the optimal way to savour the fruits' sweet milky juice! Yet they are also perfect for use in any number of sweet and savoury recipes. They are particularly ideal for combining in fruit salads, incorporating into ceviche, blending into smoothies, and making sorbet! They are also well-suited for baking, making a wonderful pastry filling, and can even be used to flavour teas and cocktails! Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some more recipe inspiration, including the famous Jamaican fruit salad known as 'matrimony' that combines condensed milk and flavourful tart fruits including grapefruits, star apples, and oranges!
As well as being supremely delectable, star apples boast many nutritional benefits. In particular, they are an excellent source of vitamin C and calcium and provide a good amount of phosphorous.

Name: Starfruit
Description:
Starfruit (also known as 'carambola') is a must-try for exotic fruit lovers!
As you have probably guessed, these fruits are best known for their distinctive appearance. These medium-sized, waxy-skinned fruits have 5 ridged edges, so when they are sliced crossways, the slices are shaped like stars (hence their name)!
However, it is not only their eye-catching appearance that delights the senses - starfruit's flavour is similarly spectacular!
When they are picked before they've reached full maturity, starfruits are firm and green with a crisp, citrus-like flavour. At this stage, they primarily impart sour notes, so they are ideal for salads and stir-fries. Yet, if left to ripen fully, starfruits turn a dazzling bright yellow in colour and they soften significantly. Once completely mature, starfruits are succulent and crisp, and boast a divine sweet-tart savour, with delectable notes of grape and plum!
Ripe starfruits are best enjoyed when simply eaten fresh out of hand, especially because the entire fruit is edible, including the small, brown seeds! Slices are also popularly combined in fruit salads. The fruits are also perfect for juicing - indeed, in Brazil, starfruit juice is renowned as an excellent thirst quencher! Starfruit juice is also an excellent addition to cocktails and slices of starfruit make brilliant cocktail garnishes! Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some more recipe inspiration, including a scrumptious starfruit bruschetta!
Furthermore, starfruits are nutritionally beneficial. In particular, they are extremely rich in vitamin C - one starfruit provides half your daily required vitamin C content! - provide great amounts of vitamin K, and are a good source of dietary fibre.

Name: Starfruit
Description:
Starfruit (also known as 'carambola') is a must-try for exotic fruit lovers!
As you have probably guessed, these fruits are best known for their distinctive appearance. These medium-sized, waxy-skinned fruits have 5 ridged edges, so when they are sliced crossways, the slices are shaped like stars (hence their name)!
However, it is not only their eye-catching appearance that delights the senses - starfruit's flavour is similarly spectacular!
When they are picked before they've reached full maturity, starfruits are firm and green with a crisp, citrus-like flavour. At this stage, they primarily impart sour notes, so they are ideal for salads and stir-fries. Yet, if left to ripen fully, starfruits turn a dazzling bright yellow in colour and they soften significantly. Once completely mature, starfruits are succulent and crisp, and boast a divine sweet-tart savour, with delectable notes of grape and plum!
Ripe starfruits are best enjoyed when simply eaten fresh out of hand, especially because the entire fruit is edible, including the small, brown seeds! Slices are also popularly combined in fruit salads. The fruits are also perfect for juicing - indeed, in Brazil, starfruit juice is renowned as an excellent thirst quencher! Starfruit juice is also an excellent addition to cocktails and slices of starfruit make brilliant cocktail garnishes! Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some more recipe inspiration, including a scrumptious starfruit bruschetta!
Furthermore, starfruits are nutritionally beneficial. In particular, they are extremely rich in vitamin C - one starfruit provides half your daily required vitamin C content! - provide great amounts of vitamin K, and are a good source of dietary fibre.

Name: Tamarind sweet
Description:
One of the most unusual-looking fruits we sell, sweet tamarinds are a must-try for lovers of unusual fruit!
Tamarinds are bean-like pods with a light to dark brown exterior shell. Beneath their hard, smooth, outer casing is soft flesh that surrounds shiny black seeds - as the fruits mature, the flesh dehydrates and takes the form of a paste.
It is at this stage of advanced maturity that the flesh acquires the best flavour: the fully ripened flesh mellows in sourness and instead becomes sweeter, wowing the tastebuds with its wonderful mixture of notes of dates and raisins. Some people even compare their flavour to that of Coca-Cola!
The small size and sweet flavour of tamarinds means they are perfect for snacking. However, they are more commonly used in recipes - indeed, they are a staple ingredient in Thai cuisine! The pasty flesh is perfect for complementing the spicy notes of curries and is used in Pad Thai, one of Thailand's most famous dishes! Sweet tamarinds are ideal for making drinks too: simply soak the flesh in a small amount of warm water for 10 minutes and then remove the seeds and fibre. After that, blend the flesh with cold water and sugar until smooth and then strain! Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some more recipe inspiration, including a scrumptious beef stew in tamarind sauce!
As well as being delicious, sweet tamarinds boast numerous nutritional benefits. In particular, they are an excellent source of vitamin B and are rich in calcium.

Name: Ume green plums (luxury fruit for gifting)
Description:
Japanese Ume, also known as umeboshi when pickled, are small sour stone fruits that are associated with Spring in Japan.
When ripe, ume have a lovely beige-pink flush. Under their skin is an incredibly tart and bitter flavour, which is why Ume are typically pickled to make Umeboshi, one of the most iconic flavours in Japan, Umeshu ( a Japanese plum wine) and ume miso, rather than eaten fresh out of hand.
When pickled, ume transforms into a superfood, high in citric acid, and used to treat a range of ailments such as fatigue, infections, colds and high blood pressure.
Experience a real taste of Japan with fresh ume.

Description:
Bored of your standard supermarket fruit juices? If so, we have just the thing for you!
Acerola cherries are bite-sized, bright red fruits that are both wonderfully delectable and supremely healthy!
Although small in size, these cherries from Brazil pack a punch in their flavour: their delightful juicy texture and sweet, fragrant, tangy taste will dazzle your tastebuds!
Nutritionally acerola cherries stand out too. They not only contain up to 65 times as much vitamin C as oranges, making them one of the best naturally occurring sources of the vitamin, but they are also rich in vitamins A, B1, B2, and B3, as well as carotenoids and bioflavonoids, which provide important health benefits.
Made from 100% pure fruit, our frozen acerola cherry pulp is just as delicious and nutritious as the fresh fruits themselves! All you have to do to turn our organic pulp into a wonderful beverage is add water or milk (and sweetener if you desire) - within minutes you will have a deliciously sweet fruity drink to enjoy! Indeed, you can even consume it neat!
There are many other ways you can enjoy our frozen acerola cherry pulp, however: you can stir it into creamy smoothies to give them a kick of tropical flavour; combine it with desserts such as ice cream to add a unique spin to your favourite sweet treats, or use it to make up to 0.5L of thirst-quenching juice. Whatever you choose, the result will be an appetizing and healthy delight! Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some of our favourite recipes, including one for an incredibly refreshing juice that is popular in the Dominican Republic (simply substitute the fresh cherries for the same quantity of the pulp)
As well as being full of flavour, the pulp contains no added colours, preservatives, or flavourings, so you can feel confident that you're consuming only pure fruit.

Name: Achacha
Description:
The achacha is a highly prized tropical fruit. With its sweet, tangy, refreshing taste it adds a new flavour to the fruit bowl! The achachas firm orange skin peels away easily to reveal a subtly sweet-then-tart white interior. The fruits can contain one or two large seeds. Achachas originated in the Bolivian Amazon Rainforest, and are now cultivated largely in Australia.
Achachas are a valuable source of vitamin C and folate, as well as potassium, riboflavin and antioxidants. The sugar levels of the achacha are relatively low compared to other fruits.

Name: African cherry (agbalumo)
Description:
The African cherry, mainly cultivated in West Africa, is an underrated fruit that dazzles people's tastebuds with its unique array of flavours - the skin, flesh, and seeds all have a different taste, making for an unforgettable eating experience!
Also known as African star apples, so-called because inside each fruit is a cluster of large seeds stuck together in the shape of a star, these tangerine-sized fruits have tough, almost leather-like skin, which changes from green to dark orange in colour as it ripens. When ripe, the fruits have tender, fibrous dark red/orange flesh that offers eaters a delightful flavour combination, intriguingly containing notes of both sweetness and tartness, with subtle acidic, citrus hints.
Embedded within the flesh are seeds with shiny brown casings (which feel like plastic), covered with a cream-ish white, fibrous, sweet membrane.
Not only are African cherries incredibly delicious, but they are also extremely nutritious: they are an excellent source of calcium and fibre, are rich in iron, and also contain good amounts of vitamins A and C, boasting higher levels of vitamin C than oranges!
Although most commonly eaten fresh out of hand, African cherries can be used in food and drink recipes too, from smoothies and mocktails to desserts! Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some of our favourites, including an amazing African cherry ice cream!
Don't forget our frozen African cherries too. They are a real treat to be enjoyed when the fresh fruit is out of season.

Name: Aloe vera leaf and plant
Description:
Aloe vera, a succulent plant species originating from the Arabian Peninsula - it grows wild in tropical, semi-tropical, and arid climates around the world - is globally renowned for its medicinal and cosmetic uses. Indeed, thanks to the multitude of beneficial ways it can be put to use, particularly its health and skin care benefits, aloe vera is often described as the 'wonder plant'!
The aloe vera leaf is green and firm on the outside, creating a shield from its soft jelly-like flesh. Both the skin and the gel inside aloe vera leaves can be eaten, but make sure to wash the skin or gel thoroughly before consumption to remove all traces of latex, which can have unpleasant and potentially harmful side effects.
It has become popular to mix aloe vera flesh with a variety of different ingredients to make refreshing, invigorating juices and smoothies - check out the 'Further information' tab below for our recommended recipes! As aloe vera is rich in many antioxidants, has anti-inflammatory properties, and may aid digestion, you can be happy knowing that these drinks are nutritionally beneficial as well as rejuvenating. Caution: Aloin, present in the outer layer (green skin) is toxic. Remove the outer layer (green skin) and rinse the flesh before use. Not recommended for pregnant and lactating women and children under 12 years.

Name: Amla
Description:
Amla, also known as Indian gooseberry, are small, round - they are roughly the size of a marble - berries perfect for a variety of culinary uses!
Native to the subtropical South Asian countries of India, Pakistan, and Bangladesh, these berries have tough, yet thin, light-green skin, and flesh that is crisp and juicy, and contains an interesting hexagonal-shaped stone with 6 small seeds. The taste of the flesh is intriguing: it has a mix of flavours unlike any other fruits we've tried, ranging in one bite from a rich earthiness to a sour bitterness.
The grape-like berries can be eaten fresh, though the bitter taste is better offset with a sprinkle of salt, so traditionally they're used for making delicious pickles and chutneys. However, their unique, multi-dimensional flavour means they are ideal for use in a variety of recipes, suiting both sweet and savoury applications. We'd recommend using these fruits to make amla murabba, a delightful sweet preserve served with Indian flatbread, bake them into tarts and other sweet treats, or juice them to create delectable flavourings for vinegars and marinades. Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some recipes!
As well as being extremely versatile, amla are also believed to have excellent nutritional value, and indeed are highly revered in Ayurvedic medicine. In particular, they are rich in vitamin C and many antioxidants, and are regarded as being beneficial in supporting healthy digestion.

Name: Apple - butter fuji
Description:
Butter Fuji apples are one of the most attractive modern apple varieties!
Also known as golden Fuji or cream fuji apples due to their glossy pale yellow skin, these eye-catching fruits from China are the same variety as Fuji apples, but have been covered in bags while growing so their peel gains this distinctively soft colouring instead of the red of their more well-known counterpart.
Round in shape and around 3 inches in diameter, butter Fuji apples have smooth, delicate skin and flesh that is firm, yet softer than conventional apple varieties and wonderfully succulent. Like regular Fujis, they contain between 9-11% sugars by weight and have a dense flesh that is sweeter and lighter than many other apple cultivars, making them popular with consumers around the world. Indeed, many people think butter Fujis have an even more delicious taste than the red variety - the fact that they stay on their trees for at least a month longer than red Fujis, butter Fujis are commonly praised for boasting an even sweeter flavour, with especially pronounced notes of honey.
Although best enjoyed simply eaten fresh out of hand, cream Fujis are also perfect for adding some colour to your fruit and green salads - they combine particularly well with walnuts, almonds, cranberries, and pears - and are well suited to pairing with cheeses such as cheddar. You can also use Fuji apples in any recipe that calls for apples - check out the 'Further information' tab below for some of our recommended recipes, including one for a quick and easy apple crisp, the perfect dessert!
As well as being delicious, cream Fujis are packed full of beneficial nutrients. As well as a high sugar content, they are an excellent source of fibre and are rich in vitamin C and omega-3.
Fuji apples are an apple hybrid developed by growers at Tohoku Research Station in Fujisaki, Aomori, Japan in the late 1930s. It originated as a cross between two American apple varieties - the Red Delicious and old Virginia Ralls Genet apples.

Name: Apple - red flesh 'redlove', 'kissabel' and 'rosetta'
Description:
Are you a lover of apples? Well, red flesh apples will be just the thing for you!
We source two varieties of red flesh apples: kissabel and redlove.
Our kissabel apples, grown in England, have aesthetically pleasing golden yellow/orange skin, with a slight red blush that matches the appealing rosy-coloured flesh. One bite of these fruits and you will fall in love: your tastebuds will be in heaven when you bite into the crisp, crunchy, sweet flesh, especially when you experience the wonderfully tangy aftertaste! Many people describe the flavour as being comparable to a mix of apple and pear.
Redlove apples are similarly brilliant. These hybrid fruits developed in Switzerland are red both on the outside and inside, making these glossy, smooth apples a real treat for the eyes. They have a strong, fruity-sweet aroma and, like kissabel apples, their flesh is firm, crunchy, and superbly succulent. Redlove apples are slightly less tart than kissabel apples, with their tartness offset by sweet undertones and tangy notes similar to cherries and berries.
Rosetta apples, grown in England, are a rare early season variety that get their name for the rosette pattern that emerges when you cut them open. Beneath their thick smooth skin is a pink marbled flesh that has a light delicate sweet flavour with notes of berry. As a dessert apple, they are best consumed straight out of hand.
Delectable when eaten out of hand as a regular apple, they are also perfect for brightening up and adding some crispness to fruit salads - especially because the highly oxidized flesh doesn't turn brown when sliced, unlike regular apples! - making apple juice or cider, and are well-suited to baking applications. Indeed, redlove apples are particularly valued not only for their bright red hue but due to the fact that they are equally capable of being used as an eating and a cooking apple. Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some fantastic recipes!
Additionally, red flesh apples boast numerous health benefits. As well as being full of antioxidants - redlove apples have an antioxidant content that is 30-40% higher than regular apples! - they are rich in anthocyanins, which can help protect the immune system, and are an excellent source of fibre, potassium, and vitamins A and C.

Name: Apple - sun fuji (luxury fruit for gifting)
Description:
Discover the exquisite sun fuji apple from Aomori Prefecture in Japan. The perfect luxury fruit for gifting to an apple or fruit connoisseur. For someone who appreciates the finest food.
Renowned for its vibrant red skin that mirrors the sun, this apple not only captivates the eye but also boasts a unique 'honey core.' This natural feature is the sugars in the apples moving to the centre to provide a remarkable defense against the extreme temperature fluctuations typical of the Fuji Mountain region. The apples can be exposed to temperatures between -20 to +10 in the same day! Apples from trees with the most prominent honey-core attract the highest market rate. Please note though, once the sun fuji apples are exposed to stable warmer temperatures the honey core gradually dicipates as the sugars evenly distributes across the whole flesh. It's for this reason that we can't guarantee your sun fuji will have the honey core characteristic.
Each bite reveals a rich flavour, an elevated apple experience.
Its delightful sweetness and hint of acidity make the sun fuji apple a cherished treat in Japan, and increasingly more here at one as luxury fruit is being discovered in the UK.
For a special occasion, or as an elegant addition to any gift basket. Indulge yourself, or someone special, with this exceptional fruit.

Name: Asian Mango Variety Box
Description:
Indulge in the exquisite flavors of Asia with our Asian Mango Variety Box, an exclusive collection of the regions most beloved and sought-after mangoes!
Mangoes from India and Pakistan are regarded by many as the best mangoes in the world, with a delectable sweet tropical flavour and floral undertones only found in mangoes from South Asia.
From the velvety, honey-sweet Alphonso mangoes of India to the floral, golden Nam Doc Mai from Thailand, this box is perfect for any mango lover that wants to sample some of the tastiest.
Whether you're discovering new favorites or indulging in nostalgic flavors from your homeland, the Asian Mango Variety Box is a luxurious, sensory adventure that brings the best of Asian fruit culture straight to your door.
As the contents of the mango variety box is always changing, depending on what's in season and available, we can't provide a definitive list of what will be included in your box but we will always aim to include between 5 to 10 different varieties and also ensure that you will receive a little more for your money when compared to ordering the mangoes individually. You may receive more than one of some varieties.
Some of the varieties of mango stated below are only available to us for a few weeks of the year. If you would like to get a better idea of the current contents of our Asian mango variety box, please message us using our contact page.
We source the following varieties of Asian mangoes throughout the year;
alphonso, amrapali, anwar rettol, badami, banana, banganapalli, bari-4, dasheri, fazli, himsagar, honey, kartha kolomban, kesar, langra, nam dok mai, neelam, rajapuri, TJC, totapuri, vilad. May also include the exclusive himayat mango!

Name: Avocado - long neck
Description:
Long Neck avocados are one of the most visually distinctive fruits we sell!
As the name suggests, Long Neck avocados are best known for their shape, which is an entirely natural characteristic. They gained worldwide fame for their unusual shape n 2019 when a photo of these extremely long fruits, which can grow up to 45cm in length, went viral on social media - a chef subsequently revealed that they are so large, you can make 12 avocado toasts from a single Long Neck avocado!
However, these large avocados are also favoured for the wonderful taste of their thick yellow-green flesh, encased by thin, shiny, and smooth green skin. One bite of this creamy and buttery flesh, with its unique salty and sweet flavour, will leave you eager for more!
Like smaller avocados, these fruits too have their cavity filled with a brown seed, but rest assured that the pit is small in comparison to the amount of edible flesh!
Long Neck avocados are best enjoyed when eaten fresh out of hand, but the moisture-dense flesh is also well suited to other raw applications, working well in both sweet and savoury recipes. We'd recommend removing the flesh from the skin, slicing or cubing it, and then adding it to salads, sandwiches, or tacos; layering the flesh over sushi; chopping it into salsa, or mashing it into guacamole. In short, you can use Long Avocados in any of the ways you'd use traditional avocados.
As well as being delectable, Long Neck avocados are an excellent source of fibre and vitamin K, and are rich in potassium, folate, and vitamin C.
The Long Neck avocado has a short season so they are not the avocado of choice for large-scale avocado farmers, so we usually source ours from rare fruit growers who specialise in unusual varieties.

Tab Content:Preparation:
Long Neck avocados should be washed before consumption.

Cut along the fruit from top to bottom and all the way around. Then separate the two halves, remove the seed, and eat!
Tab Content:Usage:
Long Neck avocados can be used as an impressive garnish in salads due to their distinct shape. Cut in half and leave it in the peel, then rest on top of a colourful plant-based salad.

Aside from garnishing, Long Neck avocados are perfect for simply eating out of hand, or why not make your own guacamole with the creamy, buttery flesh?
Tab Content:Storage:
If they arrive before they are fully mature, store Long Neck avocados in a warmer place, or at least at room temperature, to allow them to ripen. Do not leave them in a cold draft or cooler place. 

Once ripe, Long Neck avocados should be stored in the fridge for up to 3 days.
