Name: Citrus - lemon, Persian sweet lemon
Description:
Our sweet lemons are a must-try for citrus lovers with a sweet tooth!
In appearance, sweet lemons do not immediately stand out from the crowd: these medium to large-sized fruits are round or oval in shape (they tend to be more circular than other types of lemon) and have glossy, pebbled peel that ripens from green to golden yellow.
Yet, once you taste these wonderful lemons, you'll understand why they are a unique variety. Beneath their thin, taut, and supremely aromatic skin is 9-10 segments of pale yellow flesh that is tender, pulpy, and simply mouthwatering. Unlike other lemons, this often seedless variety possesses little acidity, so the flesh has an exquisitely sweet taste! In fact, demand for the sweet flavour of these fruits has led them to be cultivated in Asia for centuries.
The bright, floral, and slightly tangy flavour of sweet lemons means they are ideal for use in any number of sweet and savoury dishes. Indeed, sweet lemons can be used anywhere you want to add pure lemon flavour with none of the characteristic lemon bitterness! We'd recommend juicing them to make brilliant marinades and vinaigrettes and candying the peels to create delectable treats. In sweet foods such as marmalade, lemonade, or desserts, the lower acid level of sweet lemons means less sugar may be required. Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some more recipe inspiration, including the ultimate lemon meringue pie!
Sweet lemons have been used in traditional medicine for hundreds of years (particularly medicinal beverages for cold and flu) and are still today noted for their nutritional benefits. In particular, they are an excellent source of vitamin C and are rich in vitamin A, dietary fibre, and potassium.

Name: Citrus - lemon, primo fiore
Description:
Grown naturally without any chemical treatment, waxes, or preservatives, our primo fiore lemons stand out in their abundant juice, intense flavour, and high acidity levels.
This citrus comes from the first flowering and has an elliptical shape and a medium size. Its skin is a very light yellow colour.
Our lemons are refreshing and their juice makes the perfect flavouring, whether you are marinading meat or fish, making jams or marmalades, creating cocktails, or anything else that you desire. It will provide the ideal citrus kick!
The ripening of the fruit begins at the end of October and lasts until the first days of April.
Did you know that lemon peel can be eaten too, and that it is delicious and healthy? Lemon peel is very aromatic, tart, and is rich in essential oils, and as such is the ideal flavouring for creams, liqueurs, cocktails and mocktails, desserts, and more! It is also a great source of fibre and vitamin C.
If you're lucky enough to receive some lemon leaves too remember that they can be used to flavour meats and cheeses!

Description:
Grown naturally without any chemical treatment, waxes, or preservatives, our primo fiore lemons stand out in their abundant juice, intense flavour, and high acidity levels.

Name: Citrus  - lemon, sylheti jara
Description:
Sylheti jara are delicious, aromatic fruits exclusively cultivated in the Sylhet region of Bangladesh.

Although they somewhat resemble both limes and lemons, these fruits are in fact neither, although they are part of the citrus family.

Fully grown, sylheti jara are quite large, usually boasting a much bigger size than a lemon we see in UK supermarkets. It's not uncommon for this specialty citrus to weigh as much as 1kg each!

However, it is the flavour of these citrus fruits that makes them so sought after. Whereas its sister fruit, the jara lemon, is often completely sour, sylheti jara have a delightfully unique taste that is both sweet and sour.

Although sylheti jara have more pith than the jara lemons, which have a higher proportion of flesh and juice, the floral aroma and delectable taste of the former are considered superior.

Sylheti jara are used in similar ways to jara lemons - to add a citrus kick to mealtimes! For instance, it is common in Bangladesh to pair both of these fruits with spicy dishes, especially in order to impart a sour, citrusy note to curries, and it is also popular to eat the flesh alongside seafood. Some people use it in drinks making too, in particular the creation of liqueurs.

Name: Citrus - lime, dried black lime
Description:
Dried black limes are a must-try!
Dried black limes are limes which have lost all water content, usually after having spent the majority of their drying time in the sun.
Strongly flavoured, they taste sour and citrusy like a lime but they also taste earthy and somewhat smoky and lack the sweetness of fresh limes. As they are preserved, they also have a slightly bitter, fermented flavour, but the bitter accents are mainly concentrated in the lime's outer skin and seeds.
Given their unique flavour, they are primarily used to add a sour flavour to dishes, through a process known as souring. However, dried black limes have proven to be very versatile, suiting a number of culinary applications, whether you slice, crush or ground them into a powder. For example, in Persian cuisine, dried black limes are used to add this earthy, sour flavour to stews and soups. Across the Persian Gulf they are paired with fish, whereas in Iraq they are added to almost all dishes and stuffing. They are also commonly made into a warm drink called hamidh. Powdered dried lime is also used as an ingredient in Persian Gulf-style baharat (a spice mixture which is also called kabsa or kebsa). Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some of our recommended recipes, including one for a dark chocolate and Persian lime tart!
As well as being full of flavour, dried black limes also boast a range of nutritional benefits. In particular, they are good sources of vitamin C, potassium and iron.

Name: Citrus - limequat
Description:
Love citrus fruits but looking for a new variety to try? Limequats are just the thing!
The limequat is the delicious result of a cross between the key lime and the kumquat. They are very small in size, measuring only 2-3cm in diameter, and are globular to oblong in shape. They look somewhat like a baby lime. They have bright green, thin, shiny peel that is edible and emits a wonderfully floral fragrance.
As they are very sour they are not usually eaten raw but are rather cooked or preserved in the same way as kumquats. They are commonly used in the preparation of beverages, pastries, sauces, jams, and juices. Limequats can also be used in cocktails in place of larger more commonly found lime varieties. Why not try limequats dipped in caramel? It pairs perfectly with the citrus flavour. Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some more recipe inspiration, including limequat cupcakes!
As well as being delicious and versatile, they also boast a number of nutritional benefits. In particular, they are an excellent source of vitamin C and folic acid.

Name: Citrus - limón sutil
Description:
Peru has wonderful limes, known as Limón Sutil - they are small and tart, but not as bitter as other lime varieties, and have a more balanced flavour than the Persian or Tahitian Limes which are usually found in the UK. The rind isn't as thick and they vary from green to yellowish in external colour.
They are favoured in Peru mainly for use in ceviche, pisco sour and are also used to marinate red meats.
Limón sutil fulfils most of the demand for limes in Peru. They're grown in the northern Peruvian region of Piura.
Due to a shorter shelf life than other lime varieties which can be sent to the UK by sea (which takes around 1 month or more), Limón Sutil have to be picked efficiently and quickly exported to the destination.

Name: Citrus - mandarin, gold nugget
Description:
One of the rarest citrus fruits we sell, gold nugget mandarins are a must-try for exotic fruit lovers!
Gold nugget mandarins were developed at the University of California during the 1950s. The hybrid fruit was created from two non-commercial breeding varieties, kincy and wilking mandarins.
They are a medium-sized variety, with a flattened, round appearance. They have textured, deep orange skin that is supremely aromatic and easy to peel. Beneath their bumpy skin is juicy, bright orange flesh. Their tender, usually seedless flesh is highly favoured by citrus fans due to its spectacular flavour: their high sugar content means the flesh boasts a divine sweetness to perfectly balance the mild acidity.
The flesh's succulence and combination of sweet and tangy notes means gold nugget mandarins are best enjoyed when simply eaten fresh out of hand. However, they are also perfect for use in a range of sweet and savoury recipes. Popularly utilised in fruit salads and cereal bowls to smoothies, juices, and cocktails, we'd also recommend using them as a wonderfully zesty flavouring for cakes, tarts, and other desserts! Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some more recipe inspiration, including mandarin margaritas!
As well as being delicious and versatile, gold nugget mandarins are nutritionally valuable. In particular, they are an excellent source of dietary fibre and vitamin C. The image used in this product listing is with credit to www.specialtyproduce.com

Name: Citrus - melogold
Description:
Do you love pomelos and grapefruits? If so, we have just the thing for you!
Melogold grapefruits, known in botanical terms as Citrus grandis × Citrus paradisi, are hybrid fruits, developed in the 1980s by crossing a pomelo with a white grapefruit. They are large in size, typically being about 13cm in diameter, and physically resemble their parent fruits: they are round with a somewhat flattened base, with smooth, thin, glossy peel that matures from green to a dazzling bright yellow (although even when they are fully ripe they might still bear some green patches).
The intense, fragrant aroma of melogold grapefruits entices you in, and the taste does not disappoint! Peeling back the skin, you will find a thick white rind encasing 12-14 segments of golden-hued translucent flesh. One bite of the juicy, soft, and tender flesh is enough to wow your tastebuds: a wonderful sweetness perfectly balances the tartness, making them appealing to both lovers of traditional citrus fruits, with their strong tangy flavour, and those who prefer fruits with a more mild taste (indeed, the 'melo' part of their name comes from the fact that they have a 'mellow' flavour when compared to their parent fruits).
Much less bitter and acidic than grapefruits, they are best eaten fresh out of hand so you can enjoy their succulent, sweet-sour flesh. However, melogold grapefruits are also well suited to a number of culinary applications. We'd recommend adding segments to your fruit salads or using them as a brilliant fruity topping for icecream, muesli, and yoghurt; stirring melogold peel zest into your sauces, soups, and stir-fries to impart the fruit's subtle citrus flavour to these savoury items; simmering the flesh into marmalades and jams; chopping the segments to make a unique salsa, or pressing the fruit to make refreshing juice. The opportunities are endless! Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some of our favourite recipes, including one for an amazing grapefruit brûlée, a fruity twist on that classic after-dinner treat!
As well as being supremely delectable, melogold grapefruits boast a number of health benefits. In particular, they are an excellent source of vitamin C and are rich in dietary fibre, potassium, iron, and zinc.

Name: Citrus - mikan orange (Spain)
Description:
Mikan oranges are citrus delicacies that all exotic fruit lovers need to try!
Mikan oranges are most closely associated with Japan, where they are highly regarded as speciality fruits. Indeed, they were once so valuable in Japan that they were used as a form of currency there!
They are small to medium in size - typically measuring only 6-8cm in diameter - and round in shape. They have pebbled, reddish-orange rind that is delicate and easy to peel. Beneath their textured skin is very thin, white, spongy pith, attached to tender orange flesh that emits a glorious fragrance and a flavour that is sure to wow your tastebuds. The soft flesh - which is usually seedless but can sometimes contain a few ivory seeds - is exceptionally juicy, and astounds eaters not only with its almost melt-in-the-mouth consistency, but also with its rich savour which combines both sweet and tangy notes!
Unlike other citrus fruits, these supremely refreshing, succulent oranges are best enjoyed when eaten fresh out of hand. Yet, they are also extremely versatile, perfect for use in both sweet and savoury recipes! They are particularly ideal for making delectable marmalades, syrups, and jellies, and are often dipped in chocolate and used as a garnish for desserts! They can also be chopped into salsa and made into sorbet, and their juice is favoured by bartenders as a superior flavouring ingredient for cocktails! In Japan, Mikan peels are dried and ground into a powder which is used in a variety of ways: most commonly, the powder is infused in hot water and honey to create a comforting herbal tea. Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some more recipe inspiration, including delicious mikan orange jam!
As well as being versatile, mikan oranges have been utilised in traditional medicines for centuries, and are still today valued for their nutritional benefits. In particular, they are good sources of vitamin A, dietary fibre, and potassium.

Miyagawa mandarins are native to and primarily cultivated in Japan - today, they account for over 50% of the mandarins produced for Japanese commercial markets!
They are medium in size - typically measuring 6-7cm in diameter - and round to oblate in shape. They have a pebbled, glossy green rind that often develops a yellow blush as it ripens and is supremely easy to peel. Beneath their wonderfully aromatic skin is a very thin layer of white, spongy pith, attached to tender, orange flesh that is often seedless (although sometimes containing a few small seeds) and is sure to wow your tastebuds with its glorious flavour: the soft flesh is exceptionally juicy and boasts a delightfully balanced savour, with brilliantly sweet notes complemented by intense tartness.
The combination of high sugar levels and rich acidity means miyagawa mandarins offer a simultaneously zesty and bright savour and fragrance which makes them heavenly when eaten fresh out of hand! However, these impressive qualities mean they are a firm favourite among chefs and bartenders too. Their sweet-tart flavour means they are ideal for use in both fruit and green salads and they are perfect for simmering into delectable jams and marmalades, blending into smoothies and sorbets, using the juice to flavour baked goods, and more! The peels can be zested like lemons and limes to flavour and garnish cocktails (and mocktails!), and they create a flavourful seasoning powder when dried and ground. Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some more recipe inspiration, including a scrumptious mandarin and almond cake!
As well as being divinely delicious and incredibly versatile, miyagawa mandarins are nutritionally valuable. In particular, they are excellent sources of vitamin C and are rich in vitamin A, potassium, and dietary fibre.

Looking for a new way to add a kick of flavour to your diet? Our mosambi from Pakistan are just the thing for you!
Mosambi, also known as 'Persian limes' and 'meethay fruits', are wonderfully aromatic citrus fruits popular throughout Asia.
In appearance, they resemble other green limes: small in size and round in shape, mosambi fruits have thin, textured green skin that imparts a glorious fragrance. Beneath the surface, they have pale greenish yellow-orange, segmented flesh (with small white seeds) that is certain to wow your tastebuds with its tangy flavour! Whilst they have the nickname 'sweet limes', these fruits are actually intensely bitter and astringent, with their taste compared to a unique combination of grapefruit and lemon.
This zesty taste makes mosambi ideal ingredients for juicing, which is the fruit's most common culinary usage - whilst the juice is sometimes drunk neat for its perceived health benefits, we'd recommend incorporating the juice into cocktails (and mocktails!) to give them a twist that will impress your friends! The succulent flesh is also a perfect addition to fruit salads and the fruits are commonly turned into chutneys and seasoning sauces. Check out the 'Further information' tab below for recipe inspiration, including how to make mosambi sherbet!
As well as boasting culinary versatility, mosambi also possess numerous medicinal properties. Staples of Ayurvedic medicine for centuries, these fruits are an excellent source of vitamins C and B6, contain a good amount of potassium and iron, and are rich in flavonoids, which have an important antioxidant effect.

Wondering how best to enjoy your mosambi fruits? We'd recommend using them to make this refreshing juice, the perfect thirst-quencher, and a delectable mosambi sherbet - the full recipe is below (and also found here)!

Ingredients: 

  • 2 cups of chilled mosambi juice
  •  ½ cup of sugar
  •  ½ cup of salt
  • 1 tablespoon of fresh lemon juice
  • 1 tablespoon of cumin powder
  • 1 cup of chilled water
  • 2-3 mint leaves

  • Finally, garnish the drink with some fresh mint leaves.

Name: Citrus - mosambi 'sweet lime'
Description:
Looking for a new way to add a kick of flavour to your diet? Our mosambi from Pakistan are just the thing for you!
Mosambi, also known as 'Persian limes' and 'meethay fruits', are wonderfully aromatic citrus fruits popular throughout Asia.
In appearance, they resemble other green limes: small in size and round in shape, mosambi fruits have thin, textured green skin that imparts a glorious fragrance. Beneath the surface, they have pale greenish yellow-orange, segmented flesh (with small white seeds) that is certain to wow your tastebuds with its tangy flavour! Whilst they have the nickname 'sweet limes', these fruits are actually intensely bitter and astringent, with their taste compared to a unique combination of grapefruit and lemon.
This zesty taste makes mosambi ideal ingredients for juicing, which is the fruit's most common culinary usage - whilst the juice is sometimes drunk neat for its perceived health benefits, we'd recommend incorporating the juice into cocktails (and mocktails!) to give them a twist that will impress your friends! The succulent flesh is also a perfect addition to fruit salads and the fruits are commonly turned into chutneys and seasoning sauces. Check out the 'Further information' tab below for recipe inspiration, including how to make mosambi sherbet!
As well as boasting culinary versatility, mosambi also possess numerous medicinal properties. Staples of Ayurvedic medicine for centuries, these fruits are an excellent source of vitamins C and B6, contain a good amount of potassium and iron, and are rich in flavonoids, which have an important antioxidant effect.

Sour oranges are perfect for juicing, cocktails and marmalades and are actually well suited to add flavour to many sweet and savoury recipes. 

The juice is used in various alcoholic products including triple sec, cointreau, curacao and grand marnier.

Wondering how to best enjoy your Seville oranges? We'd recommend following the recipe below to make 2.1kg of scrumptious Seville orange marmalade!

Ingredients
- 675g Seville Orange
- 1 large lemon
- 1.75 litres water
- 1.4kg granulated, cane sugar
 
Method
  1. Halve and juice the oranges and lemon.
  2. Pour the juice with the water into a large lidded pan, 6-9 litres.
  3. Using a small sharp knife. remove the inner membranes from the oranges and chop them finely with the remains of the lemon. Do not remove the pith from the oranges.
  4. Put the chopped membranes, lemon remains and any pips into a 36cm x 36cm piece of thin cotton muslin. Tie this up with string and add to the pan. Make sure the bag is roomy, not tightly compact with plenty of space for the water to penetrate and cook the contents.
  5. Shred the orange peel finely and add to the pan with 1.75 litres cold water. Leave the pan overnight.
  6. Next day, bring the lidded pan to boil, turn down the heat and simmer very gently for two hours. Remove the lid from the pan and set aside. Warm the sugar in an ovenproof bowl in a low oven, 140°C /275°F/ Gas 1 for 20 minutes.
  7. Remove the muslin bag and squeeze the liquid from the bag back into the pan through a sieve, using a large spoon. Check the volume in the pan has reduced by a third.
  8. Remove the sugar from the oven and place clean jars in the oven. Add the sugar to the pan and stir to dissolve. Bring the pan to a rolling boil and test for a set after 8 minutes. Dip a large spoon into the pan and scoop out a spoonful. Lift the spoon above the pan and turn it horizontally. The marmalade should drip then hang on the side of the spoon. This is known as the flake test. Alternatively, check the temperature with a digital thermometer and look for a reading of 104.5C. Turn off the heat and remove the jars from the oven.
  9. Leave the marmalade to cool for 10 minutes. Remove any scum from the surface with a large metal spoon. Gently stir the marmalade to distribute the peel. Pour the marmalade into the jars up to the brim of each jar and seal with new twist top lids. Leave the jars upright and undisturbed to set completely.

Name: Citrus - orange sweet, ruby orange
Description:
Although ruby oranges look like a typical orange on the outside, once you peel back the orange skin, you will find eye-catching ruby-red pulp! The ruby oranges are juicier and sweeter than conventional oranges, meaning they are well-appreciated by fruit lovers.
Ruby oranges are considered to be a healthy choice too because of the high concentration of antioxidants, namely lycopene. Cara cara and kirkwood red (varieties of ruby orange) contain very little limonin, a substance that makes the juice bitter. This makes them popular for juicing.
Kirkwood red is a chance mutation that developed from a palmer navel tree planted at Kirkwood Red Trust in South Africa. They are a high-quality citrus variety that are differentiated by an external blush, ruby flesh and exceptional taste. They are firm, medium-sized oranges that peel well. When grown in warmer climates, the internal flesh is a darker colour. This variety with higher acids and being firmer, can hang on the tree for up to four weeks longer than other ruby oranges, extending the season by an extra month. Name: Citrus - orange sweet, seeded
Description:
Love oranges but tired of the standard supermarket varieties? Our St Lucian and Vietnamese sweet oranges are just the thing for you!
Whilst their round shape and bright orange peel mean that, in appearance, they are very similar to regular oranges, sweet oranges stand out, as their name suggests, in their heavenly sweetness!
You will be wowed by how their wonderfully intense, rich aroma fills the room, and, once you peel back the delicate, semi-smooth skin and bite into a segment, your tastebuds will be supremely satisfied by the tender, extremely succulent, and refreshing flesh. Both the St Lucian and the Vietnamese sweet oranges provide an astounding flavour: the former are one of the Caribbean's favourite citrus fruits, and the latter are especially favoured for boasting a much sweeter flesh than their European counterparts, and for having a particularly distinctive taste owing to their growth in fertile soil in the mountainous region of Cao Phong (they are only harvested once a year, so spend 12 months benefitting from their absorption of all the soil's nutrients!) So either way you will be tasting something special!
Although these divinely aromatic fruits are best enjoyed eaten simply fresh out of hand, they are also very well suited to a number of culinary applications. We'd recommend using them to create a scrumptious marmalade to add a fruity kick to your toast; make invigorating juice, perfect for drinking by itself or adding to cocktails, syrups, and marinades, and adding the zest into your favourite baking recipes. Name: Citrus - orange sweet, navel chocolate orange
Description:
A few years ago, a grower in a citrus orchard in Valencia discovered brown-coloured oranges on a navel tree whilst the fruit on his other trees had the usual orange colour. He decided to have the brown oranges analysed and the result was surprising! The brown-coloured oranges turned out to be better in quality and flavour than the other oranges.
The grower was excited to propagate this new variety through grafting and developed a new viable variety that was named "navel chocolate"
The Navel Chocolate oranges have a sweeter taste, a lower acidity, and are also juicier than regular navel oranges. They have a brix (sugar content level) of 12, making them one of the sweetest oranges on the market!
In addition, they also have a longer shelf life, which makes this variety a particularly top-quality product!

Name: Citrus - ortanique
Description:
Ortanique is an overlooked citrus fruit that all exotic fruit lovers need to try!
First discovered in Jamaica, the fruit's name derives from a combination of or for orange, tan for tangerine, and ique for unique. Ortanique (also known as 'tangor') is thought to be a natural hybrid of a sweet orange and a tangerine, first produced in 1920.
The fruit is small to medium in size, round to oval in shape (with no discernible neck) and has a pebbled, dark orange rind. The orange flesh is tender, exceptionally juicy, and emits a glorious citrus fragrance that fills the room. The succulent pulp wows the tastebuds with its rich flavour that combines both sweet and tangy notes.

Name: Citrus - pomelo 'madou'
Description:
One of the most highly-prized pomelo varieties, our madou pomelos from Taiwan are a must-try!
These pomelos get their name from the primary place where they're cultivated - the Madou region of Taiwan. Taiwan is said to pride itself on the quality of its pomelos: in fact, the Madou Farmer's Association holds a pomelo beauty contest every year! It's perhaps unsurprising then that Madou alone accounts for nearly 30% of Taiwan's annual exports of pomelos.
Like other pomelo varieties, madou pomelos are large in size - pomelos are, after all, the biggest citrus fruit in the world, with a single fruit sometimes weighing up to 5kgs (however most export-quality fruits are around 1-2kgs). Although their rounded shape means that at first glance they resemble grapefruits, pomelos (also known as shaddocks, after the sea captain who brought them from Polynesia to the West Indies) are actually a species in their own right.
These aromatic, hefty fruits are one of the most popular citrus fruits in the world, and for good reason! Beneath their textured, glossy, easy-to-peel skin (which ripens to a yellowish-green) is firm golden-coloured flesh that will dazzle your tastebuds: one bite of the supremely juicy, segmented flesh, with its notable sweetness (and subtly sour undertones) is enough to make you a fan! Indeed, madou pomelos' delicate flesh is sweeter than that of other varieties, so people with a sweet tooth will enjoy these too! Although the pith around the segments is bitter and therefore not usually eaten, the fact that the flesh is almost seedless means you have more mouthwatering fruit to enjoy.
Whilst pomelos are usually eaten raw to enjoy the explosion of sweet-sour succulence that their flesh offers, because they are the least acidic of all citrus fruits, they are well-suited to a number of recipes! We'd particularly recommend using them to add some exotic flavour to your salads, chopping them into salsas, blending them into smoothies and pressing them for their richly flavoured fruit juice that will liven up your cocktails (or mocktails!) They can also withstand heat, so they are ideal for simmering into jams and compotes, incorporating into baked goods recipes, and roasting in the oven topped with unsalted butter. The list is endless! Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some more recipe inspiration.
As well as being delectable, madou pomelos are nutritionally valuable too. In particular, they boast a high concentration of vitamins A and C, and are a good source of potassium and copper.

Unlike other citrus fruits, these supremely refreshing, succulent mandarins are best enjoyed when eaten fresh out of hand. Yet, ponkan mandarins are also extremely versatile, perfect for use in both sweet and savoury recipes! They are particularly ideal for combining in fruit salads, making delectable marmalades, syrups, and jellies, and garnishing desserts. They can also be chopped into salsa and made into sorbet, and their juice is favoured by bartenders as a superior flavouring ingredient for cocktails! Indeed, we'd recommend substituting supermarket-bought oranges for ponkan mandarins in any recipe calling for oranges. Name: Citrus - shikuwasa
Description:
Shikuwasa is a citrus delicacy that all exotic fruit lovers need to try!
Shikuwasa limes are native to Japan and still today the fruits are mainly cultivated there. They are small in size - typically measuring only 3-4cm in diameter! - and round in shape. These plump fruits have thin, pebbled, green rind that sometimes gains an attractive yellow/orange blush when the fruits are fully ripe. Beneath their textured, wonderfully aromatic skin is segmented, tender, yellowish-orange flesh that is sure to wow your tastebuds: the soft, usually seeded (although sometimes seedless) flesh is exceptionally juicy, bright, and tart. As the fruits mature, they become sweeter, so the taste profile of a ripe shikuwasa satisfies both those with a sweet tooth and those looking to add a tangy kick to their mealtimes!
Although ripe, refreshing shikuwasa limes can be eaten fresh out of hand, these speciality fruits are usually used as a brilliant flavouring ingredient, perfect for imparting sour, tropical notes to your diet! The acidic juice is ideal for flavouring sauces, noodles, meats, and fish dishes, and also works well in alcoholic drinks and desserts such as baked goods and ice cream! In Okinawa, for instance, shikuwasa juice is combined with awamori, a local alcohol, to create a powerfully pungent drink which astounds with its sweet and sour hues. We'd recommend simply squeezing a splash of juice into a glass of spring water to create an invigorating morning beverage! The peels can additionally be zested like lemons and limes to flavour everything from cakes to cocktails and they are popularly used as garnishes too. You can also create a perfect seasoning powder by drying and grinding the peel. Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some recipe inspiration, including a shikuwasa gingerade!
As well as being versatile, shikuwasa limes are nutritionally valuable. In particular, they are excellent sources of vitamin C and are rich in vitamin A, potassium, and calcium.

Name: Citrus - sudachi
Description:
Looking for a new citrus fruit to try? Sudachi is just the thing for you!
Cultivated primarily on the Japanese island of Shikoku, sudachi are extremely popular and highly prized in their native Japan - they are beginning to become globally renowned too, as chefs and bartenders seeking gourmet delicacies are starting to recognise sudachi's potential to enliven a range of food and drink recipes!
These premier culinary ingredients are small in size - measuring only 3-4cm in diameter! - round in shape. Harvested when dark green, their thin, leathery, textured skin becomes a delightful golden-yellow upon ripening. Although supremely visually attractive, sudachi are primarily renowned for what's beneath their peel: their succulent, orange-yellow flesh. Their tender, seeded flesh emits an intense citrus aroma and is highly regarded for its high juice content.
Like other citrus fruits, sudachi are not usually eaten out of hand. Instead, they are principally used for their juice - the juice's fragrant perfume and delightfully sour, peppery taste, offering distinctly herbal undertones and a much zestier flavour than lime or lemon juice, makes it the perfect flavouring! Similar to yuzu juice, sudachi juice works well in both sweet and savoury recipes, adding a tart, tangy kick to drinks (especially cocktails!) and desserts but also pairing well with meats, fish, sushi, ceviche, salads, and much more! Sudachi juice is famously considered essential when eating matsutake mushrooms and is commonly used to make ponzu sauce, a delicious Japanese dipping sauce. Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some recipe inspiration, including chunky sudachi cookies and a brilliant sudachi margarita!
A great source of calcium, iron, and dietary fibre, and with a higher vitamin C content than lemons, sudachi juice is not only extremely appetizing but will be a very healthful addition to your diet too!

These premier culinary ingredients are small in size - measuring only 3-4cm in diameter! - round in shape. Harvested when dark green, their thin, leathery, textured skin becomes a delightful golden-yellow upon ripening. Although supremely visually attractive, sudachi are primarily renowned for what's beneath their peel: their succulent, orange-yellow flesh. Their tender, seeded flesh emits an intense citrus aroma and is highly regarded for its high juice content.
Like other citrus fruits, sudachi are not usually eaten out of hand. Instead, they are principally used for their juice - the juice's fragrant perfume and delightfully sour, peppery taste, offering distinctly herbal undertones and a much zestier flavour than lime or lemon juice, makes it the perfect flavouring! Similar to yuzu juice, sudachi juice works well in both sweet and savoury recipes, adding a tart, tangy kick to drinks (especially cocktails!) and desserts but also pairing well with meats, fish, sushi, ceviche, salads, and much more! Sudachi juice is famously considered essential when eating matsutake mushrooms and is commonly used to make ponzu sauce, a delicious Japanese dipping sauce. A great source of calcium, iron, and dietary fibre, and with a higher vitamin C content than lemons, sudachi juice is not only extremely appetizing but will be a very healthful addition to your diet too!

Name: Citrus - sweetie fruit
Description:
Calling all fruit lovers with a sweet tooth! We have just the fruit for you.
Sweetie fruit is, as the name suggests, a delightfully sweet citrus fruit that will wow your tastebuds!
These round, seedless citrus fruits are the result of a hybrid between a white grapefruit and an acid-less pomelo. Once fully mature, they have appealing deep green skin, that is thicker than the rind of grapefruits, and a wonderful floral aroma that fills the air. Their mouthwatering pale orange and white flesh is overwhelmingly sweet, containing none of the bitterness usually associated with citrus fruits. Indeed, so loved have these fruits become that they have gained the nickname 'oroblanco', or 'white gold' in English!
To eat, simply peel the soft skin like an orange, separate the fleshy segments, discard the bitter membrane, and enjoy!
As well as being delectable when eaten fresh out of hand, they can also be used in various food and drink recipes. It is most common to use sweetie fruits like other citrus fruits, to add a kick of intense flavour to both sweet and savoury dishes. You can also make candied sweetie fruit peel that lasts for up to 2 years, use them to make refreshing oroblanco sorbet, add them to fruit salads, or even juice them into cocktails - the list is endless! Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some recommended recipes.
Don't let the name fool you - sweetie fruits are in fact very low in calories, and boast a number of nutritional benefits. In particular, they are, like other citrus fruits, excellent sources of vitamin C, and are rich in calcium and potassium.

Sorbet

3/4 cup sugar
3/4 cup water
3 sweetie fruits, cut into halves
1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice

Combine the sugar and water in a small, heavy saucepan. Bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring to dissolve the sugar. Reduce the heat to low and simmer for 5 minutes. Chill in the refrigerator for 15 to 20 minutes, or until the mixture is close to room temperature.

Salad

Combine a fresh and well-washed head of lettuce with some fresh pecans. Add some cherry tomatoes, a finely chopped bunch of spring onions and some thinly sliced ​ peppers, and finally add a few wedges of a sweetie fruit. Mix some juice from the fruit with a dash of olive oil, and sprinkle this over the well-mixed salad. Serve with some pieces of French bread with herb cheese.

Name: Citrus - tachibana orange
Description:
Tachibana oranges are citrus delicacies that all exotic fruit lovers need to try!
Tachibana oranges are native to Japan, where they are highly regarded as speciality fruits. Indeed, they have been revered since ancient times - they are one of the country's oldest citrus fruits! - and used to be one of the most favoured fruits of the Japanese royal family. Aristocratic women even used to perfume themselves with tachibana in lieu of bathing!
They are small to medium in size and round in shape, with pebbled, orange rind that is delicate and easy to peel. Beneath their textured skin is thin, white, spongy pith, attached to tender orange flesh that emits a gloriously zesty and subtly spicy fragrance. The soft, seeded flesh is juicy and boasts a richly sour savour, with very subtle undertones of sweetness.
Like other citrus fruits, these succulent oranges are not typically eaten fresh out of hand due to their sharp savour. Instead, they are primarily cooked to make divine marmalades, syrups, jams, and jellies! Tachibana juice is also perfect for adding an acidic kick to soups, stews, and curries, and making tachibana tea is beginning to become popular in Japan. The oranges are also in great demand among bartenders and distillers - they are regarded as gourmet ingredients because their peels are particularly adept at flavouring cocktails (and mocktails!), gins, and other alcohols, as well as being brilliant garnishes!
As well as being versatile, tachibana oranges have been utilised in traditional medicines for centuries, and are still today valued for their nutritional benefits. In particular, they are good sources of vitamin A, dietary fibre, and potassium.

Name: Citrus - UGLI® fruit
Description:
UGLI®* fruit is a type of tangelo, which is a variety of citrus fruit. They're grown exclusively in Jamaica and come in different sizes varying in diameter from 4 inches to 6 inches and many varieties of colour from green to greenish-yellow, to yellow, and some even orange! They are only harvested and sent to market after they have ripened on the tree, so what is found in the store is always ripe fruit even though the skin may be green. Inside, the flesh is always orange to deep orange.
It was discovered growing wild in Jamaica over 80 years ago. The original tree is believed to have been a hybrid formed from the Seville orange, the grapefruit and the tangerine families.
The fresh flavour of UGLI® fruit is delicious in many recipes, adding a subtle tang to both sweet and savoury combinations. It is exceedingly juicy, and has a flavour that does not need added sugar unless you have a very sweet tooth. The simplest way to serve the fruit, is to cut them in half, loosen the segments, and eat with a spoon - this is a delicious breakfast dish.
UGLI® fruit are remarkably juicy, and squeeze easily for refreshing drinks. A glass of ugli fruit juice makes a refreshing, flavourful change to fresh squeezed orange or grapefruit. The juice is also delicious warmed as a hot toddy with rum, and sweetened with honey or brown sugar.
When buying the UGLI® fruit, do not be misled by their appearance, you will love their sweet and tangy flavour!

It is exceedingly juicy, and has a flavour that does not need added sugar unless you have a very sweet tooth. UGLI® fruit are remarkably juicy, and squeeze easily for refreshing drinks. A glass of ugli fruit juice makes a refreshing, flavourful change to fresh squeezed orange or grapefruit. The juice is also delicious warmed as a hot toddy with rum, and sweetened with honey or brown sugar.

Name: Citrus - vanilla orange
Description:
If you are an orange lover looking for a new variety to try, vanilla oranges are the perfect option, especially as they are grown in Italy using organic growing methods.
Neither a blood orange or a navel orange, vanilla oranges are a distinct variety belonging to the blonde orange family and are characterised by their distinct lack of navel and quintessential sweetness reminiscent of vanilla!
They are a medium sized variety with delicate orange skin and a thin peel. Beneath their smooth skin is a bright orange flesh that is low in both acid and sugar, making them notably less sour than other citruses.
Their sweetness means vanilla oranges are best enjoyed out of hand. However, they are also perfect for incorporating into sweet and savoury recipes. They are particularly good for pressing into juices due to their high juice content and incorporating into desserts due to their intense smell.
As well as being delicious and versatile, vanilla oranges are nutritionally valuable. In particular, they are an excellent source of dietary fibre and vitamin C.

Name: Citrus - orange sweet, washington sanguine
Description:
One of the most highly regarded orange varieties, Washington sanguine oranges from Morocco are an absolute must-try for citrus lovers!
Medium to large in size and round to oval in shape, Washington sanguine oranges do not immediately stand out from the crowd. However, you will be wowed by what's inside! Beneath the pebbled orange rind (that sometimes has some red patches) of these round fruits is tender, reddish-orange flesh that emits a wonderfully fragrant aroma and is sure to delight your tastebuds after only one bite. The soft flesh is juicy, refreshing, and boasts a high Brix (sugar) level, meaning that they are bursting with sweetness!
Given their wonderful flavour, few seeds, and easy-to-peel rind, it's unsurprising that Washington sanguine oranges are usually eaten fresh out of hand. However, they are also very well suited to a number of culinary applications. They are considered the best pressing orange by many, so they are perfect for making smooth, invigorating orange juice to be drunk or added to cocktails, syrups and marinades. We'd also recommend using them to create a scrumptious marmalade to add a citrus kick to your toast and incorporating the zest and juice into your favourite baking recipes. Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some recipe inspiration, including a Sicilian whole orange cake (so-called because it uses every part of the orange!)
As well as being mouthwatering, Washington sanguine oranges also provide various nutritional benefits. In particular, they are an excellent source of vitamin C and dietary fibre.

Name: Citrus - yuzu
Description:
Need a new citrus fruit to try? Look no further than yuzu, premier culinary ingredients that will add a kick of flavour to your mealtimes!
These extremely sought-after citrus fruits originated from China and Tibet. It was introduced to Japan and Korea during the Tang Dynasty and it is in these nations that today it is most widely cultivated. In these places, yuzu is highly regarded not only for its culinary uses but also for its skincare benefits. Indeed, in Japan, taking a yuzu bath is an annual tradition!
These Asian delicacies have become globally renowned too, as chefs and bartenders seeking gourmet delicacies are starting to recognise sudachi's potential to enliven food and drink recipes!
Yuzu look somewhat like small - typically measuring 7-12cm in diameter - grapefruits with pebbled yellow skin. Although supremely visually attractive, they are primarily favoured for what's beneath their peel: their succulent, yellow flesh. Their tender, seeded flesh emits a zesty, floral aroma and boasts a high juice content.
Like other citrus, yuzu are rarely eaten fresh out of hand. Instead, they are principally used for their juice - the juice's delightfully tart taste, offering distinct notes of grapefruit and mandarin orange and a much zestier flavour than lime or lemon juice, makes it the perfect seasoning! The juice works well in both sweet and savoury recipes, adding tangy notes to drinks (especially cocktails!) and desserts and pairing well with meats, fish, salads! Yuzu is also an integral ingredient in the citrus-based sauce ponzu, and you can additionally use the fruits to make yuzu vinegar. As well as this, yuzu is often combined with honey to make yuzu hachimitsu, a kind of syrup that is used to make yuzu tea or as an ingredient in alcoholic drinks such as the yuzu sour. In Japanese cuisine, yuzu's fragrant zest is used to garnish both sweet and savoury dishes. As well as being versatile, yuzu are known for their various nutritional benefits. In particular, they are rich in fibre, are an excellent source of vitamin C - they contain 3 times more vitamin C than lemons! - and also provide a good amount of iron and calcium.
Our 100% pure dried yuzu is a healthy treat too! Made simply through the process of dehydration, with no added colours, flavourings, or additives, our intensely fragrant dried yuzu is perfect as an exotic garnish for your cocktails and makes a delicious yuzu tea once infused with hot water. You can also remove the seeds and grind the dried yuzu down into a powder which is ideal for adding a unique kick of citrus flavour to everything from chocolate ganache and grapefruit sorbet to grilled white fish, tabbouleh salads and BBQ prawns!

Name: Coconut - king coconut 'red dwarf'
Description:
King coconuts are a must-try for exotic fruit lovers!
These coconuts native to Sri Lanka have an elongated oval shape and usually measure between 20-30cm in length. However, they stand out from the crowd due to their distinctive colour - they boast bright orange skin that immediately catches the eye!
You will be equally wowed by what's beneath this attractive surface! When you open the coconut, you will be greeted with an abundance of clear water that is supremely sweet and refreshing. Indeed, the renown they earned for their hydrating, flavourful water is the reason why they are known as the 'king' of the coconuts! Highly regarded as the best 'coconuts for drinking', Sri Lanka is now exporting bottled king coconut water to the global market!
Although the sweet liquid is best enjoyed when simply drunk straight from the coconut, you can also combine the water into smoothies and fruit juices!
Used for millennia in traditional Ayurvedic medicine, king coconuts are still today valued for their nutritional benefits. King coconut water is the perfect beverage to drink when exercising, as it quickly replenishes the body's electrolytes. Furthermore, the water is an excellent source of potassium, calcium, amino acids, and B-complex vitamins, and it also provides a good amount of enzymes which aid digestion.

Name: Coffee cherry
Description:
Everyone knows coffee, but what about the berry where the famous coffee bean starts out?
The coffee bean is not a bean, but rather a seed, encased in the bright red coffee cherry. Beginning as a green, unripe berry, the fruit gradually ripens to a beautiful deep red at which point it is harvested for it's famous beans. But what happens to the fruit left behind?
Coffee cherries are grown in the 'coffee belt' in places like Brazil, Ethiopia, Columbia and Vietnam. In a lot of places - and particularly amongst coffee farmers in Latin America - cascara tea is made from the dried coffee skin and pulp as a way to use all of the fruit and maximise harvests.
But did you know that the pulp of a ripe coffee cherry can be eaten? Before coffee beans were extracted and roasted, African tribes mashed the coffee cherries with animal fat to create a quick energy source. Though, the taste may be suprising to those expecting something similar to brewed coffee! Under their smooth and glossy skin is a fresh and juicy pulp often compared to a watermelon or apricot. They have a lovely sweet taste with a little bit of tartness, like a tropical fruit.
As well as being versatile, coffee cherries boast many nutritional benefits. They are rich in calcium, magnesium and iron and many class cascara tea - made from the skins of the sweet coffee cherry - as a superfood due to its inflammatory and anti-oxidant properties! Please note that each batch includes a mix of green, orange and red coffee cherries.

Name: Coffee leaves - dried
Description:
Looking for a new herbal drink to enjoy? Our coffee leaves are just the thing for you!
Coffee leaves are picked from coffee plants, lush, leafy plants plants native to areas of Africa and Asia. Pickers make sure to select only the most pristine young leaves - this is crucial, as it is the youngest leaves that offer the best flavour.
Once the leaves have been cleaned, oxidised, and dried, they are ready to use! The most popular way of enjoying coffee leaves is to make coffee leaf tea.
Coffee leaf tea has been enjoyed for centuries across the world, from India to Jamaica. In Ethiopia, for instance, it was traditional practice to steep the leaves in boiling water for at least 30 minutes, as it was believed that the longer the leaves were boiled for, the sweeter the resulting brew would be. Whilst in Ethiopia it was common practice to add a dash of sugar or salt to the beverage, other cultures added bamboo and sometimes an egg may be stirred in!
For first time drinkers, however, we'd recommend simply breaking up 2-3 coffee leaves into small pieces, steeping them in boiling water for a few minutes, and then consuming! Other popular additions to the drink include sugar, milk, and ginger.
Despite its name, coffee leaf tea is technically not tea - all 'true' teas are derived from the Camellia sinensis tea plant - and it doesn't taste like coffee! Instead, as you sip the silky smooth drink, you will be wowed by its combination of rich, earthy notes and sweet undertones, including hints of vanilla and honey.
As well as being delicious, coffee leaf tea has been regarded as a herbal remedy for hundreds of years, and is still today lauded as supremely nutritious. In particular, it's packed full of antioxidants, boasts anti-inflammatory properties, and has a lower amount of caffeine than both tea and coffee.

Name: Cucamelons
Description:
With nicknames such as 'mouse melons' and 'mini watermelons', it is no secret that cucamelons are much smaller than the typical melon. Yet, what these healthful little Latin American fruits lack in size - being bitesize means they are perfect for snacking! - they more than make up for in flavour.
As one of their given names hints at, in appearance they resemble tiny green watermelons, and cucamelons have a similarly delightful tropical aroma, however in other respects they are comparable to cucumbers (hence the 'cuc' part of their name). For example, like cucumbers, they have crunchy, translucent flesh that is full of seeds, and cucamelons have a similar flavour, although the delicate, fresh sweetness is complemented by a delicious citrus kick and faint sour notes - this has led people to say that eating a cucamelon is like eating cucumber drizzled in lime juice.
Although often eaten whole out of hand, the combination of sweet and sour flavours makes cucamelons ideal for savoury as well as sweet recipes: we particularly recommend pickling them to really bring out their crispness; adding slices cucamelon to salads and stir-fries to bring some juicy crunch, and making the most of cucamelons' natural lime taste to use them to make tangy cocktails (look at our 'Further information' tab for recipes)!
As well as being refreshing and flavoursome, cucamelons also have nutritional benefits. They are rich in antioxidants and are an excellent source of fibre, vitamins A and C, and potassium, so they are all around the perfect healthy and ideal way to add some flavour to your mealtimes!

Cupuacu, originating from South America, is a tropical rainforest tree related to cacao. It is regarded as one of the ultimate super fruits due to its richness of antioxidants and other powerful nutrients!

Its flavour is similarly sublime, reminiscent of a wonderful mixture of pear, banana, passion fruit, and melon! With such a mouthwatering taste, it's not surprising that the fruit is a popular ingredient in desserts, juices and sweets.
Our 100% pure cupuacu frozen pulp is just as delicious as the fruit itself! And with no added colours, preservatives, or flavourings added, you can feel confident knowing it is nutritionally beneficial.
There are many ways you can enjoy our cupuacu frozen pulp: consume it neat; mix it with water or milk and a touch of sweetener to create a refreshing, rejuvenating drink; stir it into smoothies to give them a note of tropical earthiness; combine with desserts such as ice cream to add a unique flavour to your sweet treats, or use it to make up to 0.5L of thirst-quenching juice. Whatever you choose, the result will be an appetizing and healthy delight!

Name: Custard apple - atemoya
Description: One of the most unusual exotic fruits that we sell, atemoya is an absolute must-try! Atemoya are large in size and are usually either round or heart-shaped. These heavy fruits - they can weigh up to 5 pounds! - have thick green skin that immediately catches the eye due to their distinctive protruding points. They almost resemble a pinecone in appearance! Being a cross between a sugar apple and a cherimoya, it's not surprising that these unique fruits boast a delicious flavour! Indeed, atemoya is regarded as the finest variety of custard apple, and for good reason! Whilst the flesh closest to the skin is slightly grainy, with a pear-like texture, most of the flesh boasts a divine creamy smoothness, reminiscent of firm custard! The tender white flesh dazzles the tastebuds with its sublimely sweet savour that combines notes of custard and apples. Although the flesh is best enjoyed when simply scooped out of the shell with a spoon, you can also the flesh to add some tropical flavour to fruit salads, smoothies, cereal, and yoghurt. Additionally, they are perfect for creating your own ice cream: simply blend the pulp with fruit juice and cream and freeze the mixture until it's set! Check out the 'Further information' tab below for recipe inspiration, including simple recipes for atemoya salsa and atemoya sorbet! As well as being unbelievably delectable, custard apples are also nutritionally valuable. In particular, they are an excellent source of vitamin C - one atemoya provides half of an adult's daily vitamin C requirements! - and are rich in dietary fibre, potassium, and magnesium.

Name: Custard apple - ramphal
Description:
Our ramphal from Sri Lanka is an absolute must-try for all exotic fruit lovers!
Ramphal is an overlooked member of the custard apple family. Also known as 'wild sweetsop' and 'bullock's heart', these intriguing fruits immediately catch the eye with their reddish-orange skin and their almost heart-shaped stature. Beneath the smooth, delicate skin of these medium-sized fruits is creamy white flesh that is sure to delight your tastebuds with its heavenly flavour: the soft (and sometimes slightly granular) flesh astounds with its rich, fruity sweetness!
These glorious fruits are best enjoyed when eaten fresh out of hand, particularly because their unbelievably delicious flesh has fewer seeds than that of other custard apple varieties! However, these flavoursome fruits are also very versatile, working well in both sweet and savoury recipes. They are especially perfect for making dipping sauces, sweet preserves such as jams and jellies, and pickles, and we'd also recommend using them to add some tropical flavour to your smoothies as well as your desserts, from sorbets and mousses to cakes! Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some recipe inspirations, including a ramphal ice cream smoothie!
As well as being imbued with a spectacular flavour, ramphal also possesses many nutritional benefits. In particular, it is an excellent source of vitamin C and provides good amounts of vitamin A, dietary fibre, and potassium.

Name: Damson, frozen
Description:
Damsons are a must-try for fruit lovers!

Description:
Love dried fruit? Amir dates are just the thing for you!
Amir dates, also known as 'Amir Hajj' dates, are renowned throughout the world for their high-quality appearance, texture, and flavour. Indeed, they are reputed to be the best dates in Iran, and across the Middle East they have earned the nickname 'the visitor's date', due to them being considered a delicacy worthy of presenting to guests as a gift (or to be carefully picked and boxed for the export market).

Their sublime flesh is so soft and smooth that it almost resembles caramel, and the flavour is nothing short of mouthwatering. Divinely delicate and rich, they will wow your tastebuds with their notes of cinnamon, cardamom, and nutmeg, and a delightful sweetness that is somewhere between the taste offered by Maktoom and Barhi dates.
Although best enjoyed when simply eaten out of hand as a delicious snack, Amir dates are also ideal for a range of culinary applications. Given their soft nature, they are perfect for pureeing, but we'd especially recommend taking advantage of their immense sweetness by using them as a natural sweetener by chopping and sprinkling date pieces into smoothies, cereals, and baked goods recipes. Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some recipe inspiration!
As well as being extremely delectable and versatile, Amir dates also boast many nutritional benefits. In particular, they are an excellent source of dietary fibre, and they contain good amounts of iron, potassium, and numerous antioxidants.

Name: Dates - medjool (Egypt)
Description:
Our 100% pure, organic Medjool dates from Egypt are a must-try!
The Medjool date is believed to be one of the worlds oldest cultivated fruits, with cultivation dating (pardon the pun) as far back as 4000 BC! They have been extremely popular in the Middle East and North Africa for thousands of years - the Ancient Egyptians are known to have used them to make an early form of wine!
Medjool dates are plump and oval in shape and slightly larger in size than other date varieties. They have wrinkled, glossy - their natural sugar crystals give rise to a distinctive shimmer - dark brown skin, underneath which is chewy, juicy, amber-coloured flesh that wows the tastebuds with its sweetness and undertones of caramel, honey, and cinnamon. Within the meaty flesh is a single elongated pit, which you need to remove before consumption.
Thanks to their succulence, softness - they have a softer texture than other dates - intense natural sweetness, and richly aromatic flavour, there are very few date varieties that can compare to the Medjool. Indeed, they are often called the Cadillac of Dates and the "King of Dates" due to their superior taste, size, and consistency!
Our Egyptian dates are some of the best quality Medjool dates you can buy. They are class 1 medium-sized fruits, 100% pure, and containing nothing but fruity goodness
Dates are perfect for snacking as well as a range of culinary uses! Although most commonly eaten fresh out of hand, they are also an ideal natural sweetener and sugar alternative. They are often chopped into pasta or rice dishes, and their sweetness makes them perfect for complementing savoury notes in vegetable and meat dishes, like lamb, pork, or poultry. You can blend dates into smoothies, press them into a syrup, or use them in baked goods like cakes, pies, and bread. We would particularly recommend making maamoul, scrumptious Middle Eastern cookies filled with date pudding that melt in the mouth! Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some of our favourite recipes!

Name: Dates - medjool, organic (USA)
Description:
Our 100% pure, organic Medjool dates from California are a must-try!
The Medjool date is believed to be one of the worlds oldest cultivated fruits, with cultivation dating (pardon the pun) as far back as 4000 BC! They have been extremely popular in the Middle East and North Africa for thousands of years - the Ancient Egyptians are known to have used them to make an early form of wine!
Medjool dates are plump and oval in shape and slightly larger in size than other date varieties. They have wrinkled, glossy - their natural sugar crystals give rise to a distinctive shimmer - dark brown skin, underneath which is chewy, juicy, amber-coloured flesh that wows the tastebuds with its sweetness and undertones of caramel, honey, and cinnamon. Within the meaty flesh is a single elongated pit, which you need to remove before consumption.
Thanks to their succulence, softness - they have a softer texture than other dates - intense natural sweetness, and richly aromatic flavour, there are very few date varieties that can compare to the Medjool. Indeed, they are often called the Cadillac of Dates and the "King of Dates" due to their superior taste, size, and consistency!
Our Californian dates are some of the best quality Medjool dates you can buy. Dates first began to be cultivated in the USA in the 1920s. Our dates are grown in California's Coachella Valley, an ideal environment for Medjool dates to develop the delicate texture and rich flavours they are renowned for given the sunny, warm climate and limited rainfall. They are 100% pure, and are unique in being totally organic.
Dates are perfect for snacking as well as a range of culinary uses! Although most commonly eaten fresh out of hand, they are also an ideal natural sweetener and sugar alternative. They are often chopped into pasta or rice dishes, and their sweetness makes them perfect for complementing savoury notes in vegetable and meat dishes, like lamb, pork, or poultry. You can blend dates into smoothies, press them into a syrup, or use them in baked goods like cakes, pies, and bread. We would particularly recommend making maamoul, scrumptious Middle Eastern cookies filled with date pudding that melt in the mouth! Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some of our favourite recipes!
As well as being divinely delectable, Medjool dates boast many nutritional benefits. In particular, they are an excellent source of fibre, calcium, and vitamin B, and contain more potassium than bananas!

Name: Dates - red
Description:
Fresh red dates are native to Egypt however the most extensive commerical cultivation now takes place in India and Pakistan. They are harvested in bunches on long yellow stems. They have a deep red to burgundy skin and are edible during all three stages of ripeness - khalal, rutab and tamr.
These speciality dates are usually larger than the more commonly found fresh barhi date and have a more fruity but slightly less sweet flavour.
If left at room temperature, they will eventually turn a brownish colour as they ripen, becoming very sweet, soft and chewy with a thin crisp outer skin.

Name: Durian
Description:
Regarded by many people in Southeast Asia as the "king of fruits", durian is distinctive for its strong odour, and formidable thorn-covered husk. The fruit can grow as large as 30 centimetres long and weighs up to 5kg.
The flavour is unique - compared to custard, almond, onion and vanilla!
Its shape ranges from oblong to round, the colour of its husk green to brown, and its flesh white to red.
Some people regard the durian as having a pleasantly sweet fragrance; others find the aroma overpowering with an unpleasant odour. The smell evokes reactions from deep appreciation to intense disgust but the supremely delectable flesh makes it worth the interesting aroma!
Durio zibethinus is the only species available in the international market: all other species are sold only in their local regions. There are hundreds of durian cultivars; many consumers express preferences for specific cultivars, which fetch higher prices in the market.
The durian, native to Southeast Asia, has been known to the Western world for about 600 years. The nineteenth-century British naturalist Alfred Russel Wallace described its flesh as "a rich custard highly flavoured with almonds". The flesh can be consumed at various stages of ripeness, and it is used to flavour a wide variety of savoury and sweet dishes in Southeast Asian cuisines. The seeds can also be eaten once cooked.

Name: Durian - D88, frozen pulp
Description:
With over 600 varieties of durian in the world, it can be hard to know where to start. If you're struggling to choose which variety to try first, we'd recommend the D88 durian!
D88 durians are typically medium to large in size (with a slightly longer stem than other durian varieties) and round to oval in shape. They have the spiky green shell and the rich fragrance for which durians are renowned. Their thick, golden-yellow flesh (containing small, flat seeds) has a dryer, more fibrous texture than that of other durians. Yet, they also possess a markedly milder flavour, with a delightful sweetness that lessens the fruit's bitter notes, meaning D88 durians are ideal for those trying the fruit for the first time.
Our 100% pure D88 pulp boasts the same wonderful bittersweet flavour (with an almost alcoholic aftertaste!) and can be enjoyed in many different forms. As well as consuming it neat (once defrosted), you can mix the pulp with water or milk and a touch of sweetener to create an extra refreshing, rejuvenating drink or alternatively stir it into smoothies to give them a note of tropical goodness! We'd also recommend combining the pulp with desserts such as ice cream to add a unique flavour to your sweet treats. Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some recipe inspiration - whatever you choose, the result is sure to delight your tastebuds!
As well as being flavoursome and versatile, our D88 durian pulp boasts a number of nutritional benefits. It is an excellent source of dietary fibre and vitamin C, and with no colours, preservatives, or flavourings added, you can be confident in knowing that what you're consuming is supremely healthy!

Name: Durian - D88, frozen pulp

As well as being flavoursome and versatile, our D88 durian pulp boasts a number of nutritional benefits. Name: Durian - musang king
Description:
Durian fanatics usually regard musang king as one of the best durian varieties. It's known for the buttery, thick and creamy bright yellow flesh and rich flavour, with some bitterness to balance the sweetness.
The Malaysian durian musang king was originally known as 'raja kunyit'. This translates to 'turmeric king' which alludes to the colur of the deep-yellow flesh.
Musang king first established its reputation in the 80s when Tan Lai Fook from Raub, Pahang, Malaysia discovered a raja kunyit durian tree in Gua Musang, Kelantan. After bringing a branch of the tree back to Raub, this new breed started to attract other durian cultivators in the area.
The resulting durian cultivar was named after Gua Musang where it originated. In Chinese this durian is literally named "Cat Mountain King". This is either a phonetic rendering of musang or reference to the Malay meaning, the cat-like Asian palm civet.
The husk is dusky green-brown and usually features a distinctive star shape at the bottom.

Name: 'Fat pork' fruit
Description:
We bet even our most knowledgeable exotic fruit connoisseurs have never heard of 'fat pork' fruit!

This uniquely named specimen is the fruit of the chrysobalanus icaco tree, also known as the cocoplum or paradise plum tree, which is native to parts of Africa, the Americas, and the Caribbean. In Guyana, they are also known as 'fat poke'.

These very small fruits please the eye with their plump, round shape and their dazzling deep pink skin. Beneath this aesthetically pleasing, thin, smooth skin is divinely juicy white flesh that is spongy and has a largely neutral flavour with subtle notes of both tanginess and sweetness. Within the flesh is a central white seed - bite into it and it should split into two halves with a white interior that makes it resemble the interior of a coconut! This inner white coating can be eaten.

Although they are most commonly eaten fresh out of hand, since their soft, succulent flesh and bite-size nature means they make the perfect refreshing snack, they are also ideal for use in a number of recipes. We'd particularly recommend using them to make fruity jams and jellies, roasting the seeds for a uniquely appetizing morsel, and grounding the kernels of the seeds into a powder known as “gbafilo” or “itsekiri”, a favourable addition to West African soups. Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some further inspiration!

As well as being delectable and culinarily versatile, fat pork fruit boasts a range of nutritional benefits. In particular, they are an excellent source of vitamin A and also provide a good amount of vitamins C and K.

Name: Gac fruit
Description:
One of the most eye-catching fruits that we sell, gac fruit is an absolute must-try for lovers of unusual fruits!

Although gac fruit is native to various regions in Southeast Asia, it has found particularly popularity in Vietnam. In fact, not only is the name 'gac' derived from the Vietnamese word for 'round', but in Vietnam, gac fruit is nicknamed the 'heavenly fruit' due to both its upward climbing nature (the vines can grow up to 6 metres tall!) and impressive nutritional benefits.

Gac fruits are small to medium in size and round to oblong in shape. Their skin, which ripens from green to yellow and finally to dark orange, has a leathery texture and is covered in hundreds of small spikes. Immediately beneath the distinctive skin is a layer of creamy orange flesh, enveloping a central core. Within this core are multiple seeds, encased in sticky red membranes - these soft, melt-in-the-mouth membranes are the edible parts of the fruit. 

These fruits are unique in that they can only be harvested when they are ripe. Therefore, although they have a hard texture when picked, they quickly turn soft. This is why we have choose to freeze some of our gac fruits: frozen fruits will last much longer than their fresh counterparts!

As the flesh has only a mild vegetal flavour (with notes of carrot, avocado, and tomato), gac fruit is usually cooked or juiced rather than consumed raw. We'd particularly recommend cooking the flesh as this maximises the flavour. The most common dish it's used for is sticky rice, particularly Xôi Gc in Vietnam.

Tab Content:Preparation:
Fresh: wash the exterior before preparation. Slice in half and scoop out the flesh and seeds. The seeds are not eaten.

Frozen: the gac fruit is ready to eat once defrosted. Slice in half and scoop out the flesh and seeds. The seeds are not eaten.
Tab Content:Usage:
Gac fruit is used to make juice and to add flavour to savoury recipes.

The immature green fruit is used as a vegetable in India. The spiny skin is removed and the fruits are sliced and cooked, sometimes combined with potato or bottle gourd.

In Sri Lanka, gac is used in curry, and in Thailand, gac is served with ice cream!
Tab Content:Storage:
Fresh: leave to ripen at room temperature. Once soft, keep in the refrigerator and use within a few days 

Frozen: keep in the refrigerator and use within 3 days or immediately refreeze upon arrival.

Name: Garlic - smoked garlic
Description:
Looking for a new way to add a kick of flavour to your mealtimes? Smoked garlic is just the thing for you!
Smoked garlic is the result of the partial cooking of black garlic cloves: slowly cold smoked to perfection, the result is rich, sweet, tangy garlic that stuns with its smokey flavour and aroma.
Our string of smoked garlic (weighing approximately 1kg, with 10-15 bulbs on a string) will wow your tastebuds with its combination of both sweet and savoury notes. Indeed, smoked garlic's umami flavour makes it the perfect addition to a number of dishes! To maximise the intense kick of garlic flavour, we recommend cutting the bulbs in half (keep the peel on to retain the smokey flavour!), drizzling them with oil, and roasting them in the oven to create a sublime side dish of roasted vegetables - this will bring some earthiness and depth to your favourite meals. Smoked garlic works particularly well with roast chicken: simply put a clove (or half of one) inside the chicken along with a sprig of thyme to enjoy the best Sunday lunch ever! Smoked garlic also excels in salad dressings, marinades, and numerous other sauces. Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some recipes!
The cool temperatures of cold smoking mean that it lasts longer than hot smoked garlic too!
As well as having culinary versatility, smoked garlic also boasts many nutritional benefits. In particular, it is rich in many antioxidants and is believed to reduce the body's 'bad' cholesterol and boost immunity.

Description:
African ginger, also known as wild ginger and Natal ginger, has a particularly potent taste that makes it perfect for adding a real kick of flavour to your diet!
Our African ginger comes in medium to large-sized hands and travels to the UK by air from Uganda, which means it's fresher than the Chinese ginger often found in supermarkets. The freshness of the ginger is immediately noticeable - it's much juicier and more aromatic than sea-freight gingers!
Ginger can be used fresh, dried, powdered, or as an oil or juice. Most commonly used as a flavouring for both sweet and savoury dishes, we recommend using our African ginger to make a scrumptious lime and ginger drizzle cake and a ginger chicken curry - check out the 'Further information' tab below for the recipes!
A staple part of traditional African medicine, ginger boasts many nutritional benefits. For instance, ginger contains healthful, anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, and it is believed that consuming ginger aids digestion.
For ginger which is not only more flavoursome but also healthier, this is your ideal choice!

African ginger, also known as wild ginger and Natal ginger, has a particularly potent taste that makes it perfect for adding a real kick of flavour to your diet!
Our African ginger comes in medium to large-sized hands and travels to the UK by air from Uganda, which means it's fresher than the Chinese ginger often found in supermarkets. The freshness of the ginger is immediately noticeable - it's much juicier and more aromatic than sea-freight gingers!
Ginger can be used fresh, dried, powdered, or as an oil or juice. Most commonly used as a flavouring for both sweet and savoury dishes, we recommend using our African ginger to make a scrumptious lime and ginger drizzle cake and a ginger chicken curry - check out the 'Further information' tab below for the recipes!
A staple part of traditional African medicine, ginger boasts many nutritional benefits. For instance, ginger contains healthful, anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, and it is believed that consuming ginger aids digestion.
For ginger which is not only more flavoursome but also healthier, this is your ideal choice!

Name: Golden apple (june plum)
Description:
Mature golden apple are roughly the size of an egg.
Whilst green, they have crunchy flesh which is a little sour. Once they've ripened and turned yellow, the juicy golden flesh has a pineapple-mango aroma and flavour. They're sweet, with a hint of acidity.
It's common for the skin of golden apples to be rough and blemished.
In many parts of the world, the green fruit are used in raw salads like som tam in Thailand and rojak in Malaysia and also eaten as a snack, after being dipped into fish sauce, salt or shrimp paste.
Golden apple juice, which can be made from green or yellow fruits, is popular in the Caribbean and Southeast Asia. It's mixed with water, and sugar or salt to taste. Sometimes dried sour or salted plums are added to the juice.
The leaves of the golden apple tree are used as seasoning and in salads.
Golden apple from the Caribbean are larger and will usually ripen to a sweet flavour and golden yellow colour. They can be eaten fresh out of hand or used to make sweeter juice.
The golden apple from Asia are smaller, harvested when very young and unripe. They can be used for pickling, adding to salads and to make sour juice but they won't usually ripen.
CategoryManagement: Home > Shop Online
MetaDescription: Golden apple are a must-try! Whether eaten ripe and juicy or unripe and crisp, you will be wowed by these delicious fruits. Buy now for UK delivery in days!

Tab Content:Also Known As: Ambarella, jobo, june plum, jocote de corona, hog plum, ambaló, mango ciruelo, caja, pommecythere, umbra and amra.
Tab Content:Origin: Dominican Republic, St Lucia, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka or Grenada.
Tab Content:Preparation:
Always wash first.

If consuming when green, either bite into the fruit like an apple or cut small pieces of the golden apple away from the central seed.

If consuming when yellow and ripe, eat whole like an apple, discarding the central seed.

When juicing, either add the fruits to your juicer whole (if you're using a high powered juicer) or cut into smaller pieces.
Tab Content:Usage: The fruit is either eaten fresh, made into juice or used in cooking.
Tab Content:Storage:
Kept in the refrigerator, they will last for a week or two.

To ripen, leave at room temperature and consume once they turn yellow and soften.

Name: Gungo peas, frozen
Description:
A small, round legume grown in a pod similar to a pea or bean. They have a delicious nutty flavor and can be used as an alternative to the lima bean. They are grown in warmer climates such as the Caribbean.They are eaten as a fresh green pea, picked when the pod is green or allowed to mature into a dried bean with a brown pod, and processed for ease of use and storage.
Gungo Peas can be served in the same manner as green peas, combining them with other vegetables such as carrots and cauliflower, however they're more commonly cooked with rice and coconut milk. They require a cooking time slightly longer than garden peas and when eaten are not quite as sweet, due to their lower sugar content, interestingly they have a higher starch and protein value.
This hearty pea is consumed on a large scale in South Asia and is a major source of protein for the population of the Indian subcontinent.
