Name: Guinep
Description:
Guinep are small tropical fruits from the Caribbean and Central/Southern America which are around 2-3cm in diameter. They have a short season of a few months when the bunches of fruits are harvested to be mainly eaten locally, but some are also exported to western markets.
This fruit goes by the nickname 'lemon sorbet fruit' because of the sweet flavoured pulp which somewhat resembes lemon.
Our guinep may arrive on the stem with leaves attached, we find this helps to keep the fruit fresh. We ensure that this is taken into account when weighing out an order.
As guinep are quite seasonal and only available for a few months each year we buy extra stock when they are in peak season and freeze them so we can offer this wonderful fruit all year round - or until stocks last!
The guinep are frozen both whole and peeled. They're ready to eat after defrosting.
You can mix peeled guinep with water and maybe a hint of sugar to make delicious guinep juice - yum!
Our frozen guinep are offered in 300g vacuum packs (peeled) and 500g vacuum packs (whole fruits). Please note the vacuum packing process may sometimes cause the green peel of some fruits to split. This will not affect the flesh inside.
CategoryManagement: Home > Shop Online > Sweet Fruits:Home > Shop Online
MetaTitle: One of our best selling Caribbean fruits. Guineps are bursting with sweet yellow flesh which you ease off the seed by rolling around in your mouth
MetaDescription: Looking for sweet guinep? Sourced from the Caribbean, guinep are nicknamed 'lemon sorbet fruit'  because of the sweet lemon flavour. Also known as mamoncillo.
Related Products: Soursop,Jocote, yellow and green,Banana - burro,Citrus - key limes, seeded
Tab Content:Also Known As: Mamoncillo, ackee, chenette, quenepa, lemon sorbet fruit.
Tab Content:Preparation: Ready to eat upon arrival. With your teeth or fingers break the green skin, to reveal the yellow fruit inside. Roll around in your mouth for a minute or two, to remove the firmly affixed flesh from the central seed.
Tab Content:Usage: The fruit is best eaten fresh out of hand but can also be used to make juice by mixing with water. The seeds can be retained and roasted - once cooked they taste similar to macadamia nuts.
Tab Content:Storage:
Fresh guinep should be kept in refrigeration.

-

Frozen guinep should be refrozen immediately upon arrival or kept in the refrigerator for 3 days.

Name: Hala fruit
Description:
Hala fruit is a little-known gem.
Cultivated in various regions around the world, primarily Southeast Asia, the Pacific Islands, Hawaii, and Australia, this large fruit - it can grow up to 30cm long! - dazzles people first and foremost with their truly unique appearance. Made up of a central white stone surrounded by multiple (from dozens to hundreds) green-tipped red segments, called 'keys', that resemble pieces of quartz, hala fruits look almost otherworldly - indeed, many people say they look like exploding planets!
The delightful floral aroma is matched by a similarly brilliant taste. Beneath the inedible skin of the keys is a thick pulp that has a sweet, delicate, tropical flavour, with some comparing it to mango and pineapple, noting undertones of banana, whilst others say the taste is comparable to sugarcane; the very fibrous green tips of the keys are edible too, and even the central seed can be eaten, although it is usually roasted first. As well as eating it raw, hala fruits are also commonly boiled, baked, and dried to make a paste that closely resembles dates in both appearance and flavour; the flesh can be boiled with sugar and made into a delicious jam, and refreshing juice can be extracted from the fruit.
Hala fruits are a great source of dietary fibre, and contain high amounts of beneficial vitamins, minerals, and antioxidants.

Tab Content:Preparation:
The fruit is inside the red segments. To eat, pull out a segment - once the fruit is ripe you should be able to twist the segments off, but you may have to prize the first few segments out with a sharp utensil - and start chewing from the inner end to squeeze out the sweet pulp contained inside. The green outer edges of the keys are edible too but are very fibrous.

The central seed can be eaten - it is usually roasted before eating.
Tab Content:Usage:
The pulp of the hala fruit can be eaten raw but it can also be boiled, baked, or used in a variety of food and drinks recipes. The green tips can be eaten but are very fibrous, whilst the central seed/stone is delicious when roasted.

The skin of the hala fruit is inedible.

Description:
Hawthorn fruits are a must-try!
These fruits are small berries which grow on trees and shrubs belonging to the Crataegus genus. The skin of these minuscule, rounded berries ranges from yellow to dark red, and their flesh boasts a unique flavour combination: they have both sweet and sour notes, with intense tangy undertones.
Due to their astringency, hawthorn berries are not typically eaten raw, but are instead cooked and made into jams, chutneys, preserves, or syrups, or popularly turned into juices, teas, or even wine. Did you know that hawthorn berries are also a common ingredient in tomato ketchup recipes? Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some recipe inspiration, including delicious hawthorn jelly and refreshing hawthorn iced tea!
As well as boasting culinary versatility, hawthorn fruit has been used as a herbal remedy for centuries, and still today it is recognised that it possesses a number of nutritional benefits. In particular, the berries are packed full of antioxidants and have considerable anti-inflammatory effects.

Name: Ice cream bean
Description:
Ice cream beans are one of the most unique items that we sell!
These fruits originating from Latin America consist of cylindrical pods that vary considerably in size, measuring anywhere from 50 to 100cm in length. These curved pods have leathery, semi-thick green skin that becomes yellowish-brown when the fruits are fully ripe. Beneath this textured skin is fluffy white flesh encasing numerous seeds. The flesh is simply delightful: in texture, it is pulpy, spongy, and delicate - almost resembling candyfloss, and to the touch it is reminiscent of cotton wool! - and its taste is similarly enchanting, combining notes of vanilla, cream, and cinnamon!
This intensely sweet flesh is best enjoyed when simply scooped out of the pods. Indeed, in Latin America, the moist flesh is consumed raw as a refreshing sweet snack to quench people's thirst! However, the pulp also has a variety of culinary applications: they are perfect for adding gentle sweetness to salads, smoothies, and cocktails (and mocktails)! The flesh is used in its raw form as it is not able to withstand the heat from cooking.
As well as being delicious, ice cream beans boast numerous nutritional benefits. In particular, they are rich in calcium, dietary fibre, and vitamin C. The pods/outer skins of ice cream beans are inedible. The seeds of the fruit are edible only when cooked; do not eat them raw.

Name: Jackfruit J33 variety - frozen
Description:
Our frozen jackfruit pulp is a must-try for exotic fruit lovers!
Jackfruit is the ultimate exotic fruit with a spectacular flavour that brings together many of our tropical favourites, boasting notes of pineapple, mango and banana. Not only does it taste great, but it has a luscious aroma too - the smell of a perfectly ripe jackfruit is almost intoxicating!
The natural flavour of this fruit is so highly celebrated that the flavour of the world's best-selling chewing gum, Wrigley's juicy fruit gum, is based on jackfruit. This is why jackfruit is nicknamed by some as bubblegum fruit - the best jackfruit can smell and taste just as good as confectionery!
Made of 100% pure jackfruit, specifically the J33 (also known as 'takem') variety, this frozen pulp treats you to the same glorious flavour and fragrance of the fresh fruits themselves. Indeed, J33 is one of the most sought-after varieties of jackfruit in the world due to its renowned sweetness, so you know you're in for a treat for the senses! This sweet and soft snack has a notable bite, and the texture can be compared to perfectly cooked 'al dente' pasta!

Name: Jalapeño green, orange and purple - fresh and frozen
Description:
Jalapeños are perfect for adding a kick of heat to your mealtimes!
Originally hailing from Mexico - they got the name jalapeño from Xalapa, the capital of the Mexican state of Veracruz - but now cultivated around the world, jalapeños are members of the nightshade family, alongside potatoes and tomatoes, but they are more commonly known as the chilli peppers that are used to flavour salsa and salad dressing.
Green when harvested, jalapeños turn red as they ripen, although they are usually used in an unripened state. Yet green and red jalapeños are not all the varieties you can try - eye-catching orange and purple jalapeños are a must-try! Crunchy in texture, jalapeños have a fresh flavour that is similar to that of a green bell pepper, and are renowned for their spiciness. The heat varies from pepper to pepper - purple jalapeños are milder and sweeter than green peppers; orange peppers are the sweetest and juiciest - but they are mild enough to be eaten whole.
Jalapeños can be enjoyed in many different ways: you can dice or mince them to spread the heat throughout a salad dressing or salsa; add slices of jalapeño to nachos and tacos if you fancy an intensely tangy bite, or fill them with cheese, cover with breadcrumbs, and deep-fry them to recreate a popular American snack! You can also dry and smoke jalapeños to turn them into chipotles, and they are additionally ideal for pickling if you want to try a new, delicious condiment to serve alongside your favourite meals. We recommend making spicy jalapeño poppers, a delectable appetizer perfect for a dinner party, and a refreshing, super healthy Mexican corn salad! Check out the 'Further information' tab below for the recipes.
For those who enjoy a more moderate flavour, we suggest removing the jalapeño's seeds and ribs, but remember to wash your hands straight after doing so as their oils might cause discomfort if they come into contact with your eyes, nose, and sensitive areas of skin.
As well as being very flavoursome, jalapeños are also nutritionally valuable, being a good source of dietary fibre and boasting a high content of various vitamins (namely vitamins A and B6) and minerals. Purple jalapeños in particular are renowned for their high vitamin C content.

Name: Jocote, red
Description:
Jocote fruit, pronounced ho-CO-tay, and also known by many other names, grow on deciduous trees in warm tropical climates. They grow on thick irregular branches in clusters, or alone. Unusually, the fruits begin to develop following tiny red flowers before the leaves appear.
The small tantalising fruits which are often unevenly shaped, have a sweet plum-like flavour and soft juicy golden yellow flesh which melts in the mouth. The shiny and waxy red skin is edible however the large central seed is to be discarded.
Young jocote fruits usually ripen from green-yellow to a purple or red colour although some variants of the species will ripen to a yellow color. We also sell yellow jocote, click here to find out more.
Jocote fruit are rich in vitamin C and carbohydrates. They are a source of calcium, phosphorus, iron and a small amount of fibre. They contain carotene, B-complex vitamins, and several important amino acids. Jocotes are high in antioxidants, which help rid the body of free radicals.

Name: Jocote, yellow and green
Description:
A new arrival from St Lucia, our jocote is a must-try for exotic fruit lovers!
Also known as 'Spanish plums', jocotes are small green fruits that ripen to an attractive golden-yellow colour. Beneath their thin, glossy, edible skin is a thin layer of flesh surrounding an inedible central seed, which is large for the size of the fruit itself. The flesh boasts a wonderful flavour: leave the fruits to fully ripen and the flesh will delight your tastebuds with its combination of sweet and subtly sour notes, evoking flavours reminiscent of mango, cashew apple, and plum!
Although, for the best flavour, we'd recommend eating the fully ripe jocote fresh out of hand like a plum - eat the flesh but discard the stone - they are also delectable, yet considerably more bitter, when unripe. Add a dash of salt or pickle the unripe jocotes in vinegar to maximise their brilliant savour! The pulp of the ripe fruits is perfect for combining in smoothies and yoghurts, and you can additionally boil the whole fruits in water and sugar to create an amazing jocote syrup or 'honey' which is typically eaten alone or with ice cream!
Our frozen jocotes are just as delicious as the fresh fruits and contain nothing but pure fruit. We'd recommend using these soft jocotes to make wonderfully sweet and refreshing jocote juice, a favourite drink in El Salvador!
As well as being delicious, jocotes are nutritionally valuable, being utilised for centuries in Latin American medicine! In particular, they are an excellent source of vitamin C and provide a good amount of calcium and iron. Please note, you will receive either yellow or green jocote. Yellow jocote are ready to eat, whilst green jocote can be ripened at home. If you specifically require green jocote, you must contact us before ordering otherwise we cannot guarantee that you will receive it.

Fresh: leave at room temperature to ripen. Keep refrigerated once ripe.

Name: Kiwano
Description:
Kiwano has horn-like spines, hence the name "horned melon". Ripe kiwano has orange skin and lime green, jelly-like flesh with a refreshingly fruity taste, and texture similar to a passionfruit or pomegranate. The flavour is intriguingly compared to a unique combination of cucumber, banana and lemon/lime!
Kiwano is a traditional food plant in Africa. Along with the Gemsbok cucumber, and Tsamma (Citron melon) it is one of the few sources of water during the dry season in the Kalahari Desert. In northern Zimbabwe it is called gaka or gakachika, and is primarily used as a snack or salad, and rarely for decoration. It can be eaten at any stage of ripening, but when overripened, will burst forcefully to release seeds.
Some people also eat the peel, which is very rich in vitamin C and dietary fibre.
Health benefits include high in vitamin A, beta carotene and magnesium.

Name: Kola nut
Description:
Love Coca-Cola? Then we have just the thing for you: kola nuts.
Kola nuts are small brown nuts (roughly the same size as chestnuts) found inside the star-shaped fruits that grow on kola trees, a species of tree native to West Africa.
Each nut is packed with caffeine, so when they are eaten fresh they have a somewhat bitter taste. However, dried kola nuts have a much milder flavour and boast a delightful aroma comparable to nutmeg.
Kola nuts are prized in West Africa for their stimulant effects: one nut contains more caffeine than two cups of coffee, so it's not surprising that it is common for people to chew the nuts to get their daily caffeine kick! So well known did the powerful effects of kola nuts become that in the 19th century kola extract was used in a variety of purportedly energy boosting medicines, and by the 20th-century the inventors of Coca-Cola added the extract to their recipe - indeed, the 'cola' in the brand's name is derived from 'kola'!
Although kola nut extract is apparently no longer in Coca-Cola, it is still used in many popular energy drinks, so you have probably experienced the kola nut without realising it!

Name: Lemongrass
Description:
Looking for a new way to add some subtle citrus flavour to your mealtimes? Lemongrass is just the thing for you!
Although it is not very well-known in the UK, lemongrass - a tall, perennial grass native to Sri Lanka and India - is extremely popular throughout Asia, so much so that the herb is regarded as one of the staples of South Asian (particularly Thai) cuisine.
This popularity is unsurprising given the wonderful flavour of lemongrass. As its name suggests, lemongrass has not only an aroma reminiscent of lemon, but its citrus flavour is similar to lemons too (with glorious undertones of ginger). In fact, lemongrass actually possesses the same oils as lemons and is often used as a substitute for tangy lemon flavouring!
Its fresh, floral, and almost minty aroma, combined with its zesty taste, means lemongrass works well in both sweet and savoury dishes, complimenting everything from your favourite baked goods to steaks! They are also ideal for making drinks, with lemongrass becoming a common choice among distillers - the herb is appearing in spirits, beers, sports drinks, and herbal teas.
We'd particularly recommend using the versatile herb to infuse some vibrant lemon flavour into your curries and soups, and making sublime sauces and marinades. Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some of our favourite recipes, including iced tea, shrimp and lemongrass skewers, and a vanilla and lemongrass creme brulee that will wow your dinner party guests!
As well as being delicious, lemongrass boasts many nutritional benefits. Used for centuries in Ayurvedic (Indian) medicine, lemongrass is still valued today for its richness of vitamins and minerals, notably vitamins A and C, folate, and niacin.

Description:
The longan is a prized fruit from Southern Asia because of its health benefits. It is also believed that the longan has very positive effects on the beauty of the skin and that it has aphrodisiac abilities.

Name: Long kong
Description:
The long kong fruit looks much like small potatoes and grow in clusters similar to grapes.
It is covered by very thin, yellow hair giving a slightly fuzzy aspect.
The skin thickness varies with the varieties, from 2 millimetres to approximately 6 millimetres.
Long Kong fruit contain 1 to 3 seeds, flat, and bitter tasting; the seeds are covered with a thick, clear-white aril that tastes sweet and sour.
The taste has been likened to a combination of pomelo and grape, and is considered excellent by most.
The sweet juicy flesh contains sucrose, fructose, and glucose.
The greatest producers of Long Kong are Malaysia, Thailand, the Philippines and Indonesia. The production is mostly for internal consumption, although some is exported to Singapore and Hong Kong.

Name: Lulo
Description:
Lulo are a must-try for all exotic fruit lovers!
Small in size and round in shape, in appearance, lulo somewhat resemble small oranges. Indeed, lulo are also known as 'naranjilla', the Spanish term for 'little orange'. Their thick orange skin is delicate (these fruits are easily bruised), smooth, and leathery to the touch.
Yet, whilst on the outside lulo look like oranges, on the inside, they bear a resemblance to tomatoes. The green, jelly-like flesh is separated into 4 sections and has small, pale yellow seeds. The flesh has a rich aroma, with distinctly sour notes and a flavour that delights the tastebuds: it has a notably citrus taste, sometimes described as a spectacular combination of rhubarb, pineapple, kiwi and lime!
The fruits are best enjoyed when eaten fresh out of hand: simply cut the lulo in half, add some salt, squeeze out the pulp and discard the rinds, then devour! However, their sweet-sour taste means they are also ideal for a range of culinary applications. They are commonly used to make refreshing juice and delectable jams, jellies, and sauces. You can use lulo pulp as a filling in baked goods and to make delicious lulo ice cream, sherbet, or sorbet, each of which is perfect for anyone with a sweet tooth! The pulp even works well in savoury meat stews! Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some recipe inspiration, including a quick recipe for the brilliant Colombian drink 'lulada', which is made from the fruit's green juice.
As well as being supremely delectable, lulo boasts numerous nutritional benefits. In particular, they are a good source of dietary fibre and vitamins C, A, and K.
Our frozen lulo pulp is the flesh of ripe lulo fruits frozen in a container or vacuum bag. Made of 100% pure fruit, the pulp offers much of the same brilliant citrus flavour and, once fully defrosted, can be used in many of the same ways as fresh lulo. One of the most popular uses of frozen lulo pulp is to simply mix it with water or milk to make healthy, refreshing juice - our 500g sachets make up to 1.5L of juice!

Name: Madd fruits in syrup
Description:
Looking for an unusual way to add some tropical flavour to your diet? Our madd fruit in jars is just the thing for you!
Madd fruit grows on vines in the African savannahs and takes over a year to become ready to harvest. They are picked after the first rains of the season, in April and May. The orange to brown-coloured fruit has a hard, spherical shell that contains seeds which are coated with a soft and juicy yellow pulp. The flavour is simultaneously tart and sweet.
In Africa, madd fruit is easy to find in street markets, where it's sold topped with sugar and/or salt and pepper. It can also be eaten neat but most people prefer to season the pulp. Mixed with water and sugar, the pulp makes a delicious juice. It's not advisable to swallow the seeds but the inside of the shell is covered with pulp that can be consumed.
Madd fruit is rich in vitamin C and also contains vitamin B6, calcium, phosphorus and magnesium.
In the region of Casamance in Senegal, bunches of roots from the madd plant are sometimes strung outside homes to protect the inhabitants from evil spirits.
This product is made by Zena Exotic Fruits, which is a family-owned, eco-friendly company based in Dakar, Senegal in West Africa. Zena supports non-profit organisations that help young children's education in Senegal. By purchasing Zena products, you are supporting Africa.

Name: Madd fruits in syrup
Description:
Looking for an unusual way to add some tropical flavour to your diet? Our madd fruit in jars is just the thing for you!
Madd fruit grows on vines in the African savannahs and takes over a year to become ready to harvest. They are picked after the first rains of the season, in April and May. The orange to brown-coloured fruit has a hard, spherical shell that contains seeds which are coated with a soft and juicy yellow pulp. The flavour is simultaneously tart and sweet.
In Africa, madd fruit is easy to find in street markets, where it's sold topped with sugar and/or salt and pepper. It can also be eaten neat but most people prefer to season the pulp. Mixed with water and sugar, the pulp makes a delicious juice. It's not advisable to swallow the seeds but the inside of the shell is covered with pulp that can be consumed.
Madd fruit is rich in vitamin C and also contains vitamin B6, calcium, phosphorus and magnesium.
In the region of Casamance in Senegal, bunches of roots from the madd plant are sometimes strung outside homes to protect the inhabitants from evil spirits.

Name: Mamey apple (mammea americana)
Description:
In certain Latin American countries, mammea americana is referred to as "yellow mamey" (Spanish: mamey amarillo), in order to distinguish it from the unrelated but similar looking pouteria sapota, whose fruit is usually called "red mamey" (Spanish: mamey colorado or mamey rojo).
Mamey is round or slightly irregular, with a brown or grey-brown rind that is a few milimetres thick.
Mamey usually range from 10-15cm in diameter.
When unripe, the fruit is hard and heavy, but its flesh slightly softens when fully ripe. The flesh is orange to yellow, not fibrous, and can have various textures (crispy or juicy, firm or tender). The flavour of the flesh can be most closely compared to apricot.
Small fruits contain a single seed, while larger ones might have up to four.

Name: Mamey sapote (pouteria sapota)
Description:
Mamey sapote fruit, technically a berry, has flesh ranging in colour from pink to orange to red. The brown skin has a texture like the fuzz on a peach but firmer. The texture is creamy and soft.
The delicious and complex flavour has been compared to a combination of sweet potato, pumpkin, honey, burnt sugar, caramel, peach, apricot, cherry, and almond. A mamey sapote is ripe when the flesh is a vibrant salmon colour. The flesh should be soft to very-soft.
It's an excellent source of vitamin B6 and vitamin C, and is a good source of riboflavin, niacin, vitamin E, manganese, potassium & dietary fibre. Research has identified several new carotenoids from the ripe mamey sapote.

Name: Mango - amrapali
Description:
Looking for a new mango variety to try? Amrapali mangoes are just the thing for you!
These mangoes from India are a hybrid between the ever-popular 'Dasheri' and 'Neelum' varieties. They are small to medium in size and have glossy, smooth skin that often stays green even when the fruits are fully ripe. Beneath the aesthetically appealing skin is dazzling golden-orange pulp that is sure to wow your tastebuds: with a unique earthy sweetness and a glorious succulence, these mouthwatering, aromatic mangoes are a must-try!
With a divine floral flavour and aroma that is only found in mangoes from this part of South Asia, amrapali mangoes are regarded by many as not only one of the best mangoes to eat fresh out of hand, but also as a superior culinary ingredient. As well as enjoying these fruits as a refreshing treat (particularly perfect for summertime snacking!), its subtle sweetness makes it the perfect mango to use in a range of recipes, from jams and chutneys to smoothies, cocktails, and curries! Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some of our favourite mango-based recipes.
Like the other mangoes we sell, amrapali mangoes boast a range of nutritional benefits. In particular, they are an excellent source of dietary fibre, have a high content of vitamins A and C, and also include a good amount of magnesium and potassium.
CategoryManagement: Home > Shop Online > Sweet Fruits:Home > Shop Online
MetaDescription: Amrapali mangoes are a must-try. They have a glorious floral aroma and a divine earthy sweetness that will wow your tastebuds. Buy now for UK delivery in days!
Related Products: Mango - graham mango,Mango - himsagar,Mango - honey,Mango - kartha kolamban
Tab Content:Preparation:
Ready to eat once the mango yields to gentle pressure. 

Wash the mango first.

Quite simply, one can peel back the skin and eat the mango flesh directly from the central seed.

Alternatively, cut long ways along each side of the seed to separate the mango into 3 pieces. With a spoon, scoop the flesh from the two outer pieces. The flesh surrounding the seed shouldn't be wasted! Scrape off with a spoon or eat the mango flesh directly from the central seed. 

You may also use the 'hedgehog' method to prepare honey mangoes - score longways and crossways on the outer pieces and turn inside out to reveal many cubes of mango which can be easily removed from the skin.
Tab Content:Usage: Best enjoyed straight out of hand when perfectly ripe, but can also be used to make drinks and desserts.
Tab Content:Storage:
Ripen at room temperature.

Once the mango yields to gentle pressure it's ripe and should be refrigerated to prevent spoiling.

Description:
One of the finest Pakistani mangoes, banana mangoes are an absolute must-try for all exotic fruit lovers!
Banana mangoes earned their name due to their distinctively long and thin shape that resembles a banana more than a typical mango (although some people have compared their shape to the 'Nam Doc Mai', the most popular variety of mango in Thailand). When they are ripe, their smooth, glossy, green skin becomes an eye-catching yellowish-orange. Beneath their appealing skin is dazzling golden-orange flesh that will instantly fill the room with its intense tropical aroma, and will delight your tastebuds with its heavenly flavour: the firm flesh is sublimely succulent and wonderfully sweet. Indeed, they are so adored that they have acquired the nickname 'golden mango'!
Although unbelievably delicious when eaten fresh out of hand - the fact that their silky smooth flesh contains only a very flat stone means you have even more fruit to enjoy! - these flavoursome mangoes are also extremely versatile, perfect for use in a number of sweet and savoury recipes. Alongside being ideal for making dipping sauces, sweet preserves, and pickles, they are also well-suited for combining in fruit and green salads, and for adding some exotic flavour to desserts, from sorbets and mousses to tarts and pies! Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some more recipe inspiration!
As well as being versatile and imbued with a spectacular flavour, banana mangoes also possess many nutritional benefits. In particular, they are an excellent source of dietary fibre, are rich in calcium, and contain good amounts of potassium.

Name: Mango - bari-4
Description:
Are you a mango lover looking for a new variety to try? Our bari-4 mangoes are just the thing for you!
Named after the scientific institution which developed them, the Bangladesh Agricultural Research Institute (BARI), bari-4 mangoes are a late-maturing mango variety that dazzles fruit fanatics everywhere.
Bari-4 mangoes stand out from other mango varieties first and foremost in the fact that they are hybrids: they were made by hybridizing the M-3896 variety (male) from Florida with the local Ashina mango (female).

Name: Mango - black
Description:
Love mangoes but looking for a new variety to try? Our black mangoes are just the thing for you!
Black mangoes (also known as 'blackie mangoes') are a favourite fruit in their native Jamaica, and for good reason!
Although, like other mangoes, black mangoes have a round to oblong shape and a small to medium size, they vary in the colour of their peel. Despite their name, neither their skin nor their flesh is black in colour - they are called black mangoes to distinguish them from mangoes that turn red upon maturing, since the skin of black mangoes instead remains yellowish-green in colour even when fully ripe.
Beneath their smooth, delicate, aesthetically appealing skin is eye-catching, tender orange pulp that emits a spectacular floral fragrance and is sure to wow your tastebuds with its divine sweetness and mouthwatering succulence. As well as being supremely aromatic, refreshing, and delectable, black mangoes are almost entirely fibreless, meaning that they are an easier - and infinitely less messy! - fruit to enjoy.
Although they are best enjoyed when simply eaten fresh out of hand, black mangoes are also a superior culinary ingredient. Whilst their sweetness makes them perfect for dessert recipes, they are very versatile and therefore can be used in a range of savoury applications too! We'd particularly recommend using them to make delicious jams and chutneys, blending them into smoothies, capitalising on their rich tropical savour to liven up your cocktails (and mocktails!), and stirring some into curries to balance out their spiciness. Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some of our favourite mango-based recipes, including an amazing mango mousse!
As well as being brilliantly appetizing, black mangoes boast a range of nutritional benefits too. In particular, they are an excellent source of dietary fibre, have a high content of vitamins A and C, and include a good amount of magnesium and potassium.

Name: Mango - dasheri
Description:
Mangoes from India and Pakistan are regarded by many as the best mangoes in the world - our dasheri (also known as dusheri) mangoes from India are no exception! Indeed, dasheri mangoes are not only one of the oldest varieties of Indian mango (discovered in the 18th century), but they are also one of the most highly prized!
Dasheri mangoes are small to medium in size, and are typically elongated in shape. They have smooth, leathery skin that ripens from light green to yellow, culminating in a glorious golden hue when fully mature. Beneath this aesthetically appealing skin, you will find tender, bright orange pulp that is sure to wow your tastebuds: divinely sweet, mouthwateringly succulent, and as gloriously aromatic in taste as they are in fragrance, one bite of these fruits and you will be hooked! Name: Mango - edward
Description:
Widely regarded as one of the finest-tasting mango varieties in the world, Edward mangoes are an absolute must-try for exotic fruit lovers!
Whilst we source our Edward mangoes from Peru, they were originally developed in the USA in the 1920s. Given that they are a hybrid of the Haden and Carabao mango cultivars, two of the most popular mango varieties in the world, it's not surprising that these medium-sized, round to oval-shaped mangoes excel in eating quality!
Edward mangoes have smooth, delicate skin that boasts an eye-catching reddish-orange blush. Beneath their attractive skin is golden-orange flesh that emits a glorious tropical aroma and a savour that will wow your tastebuds: sublimely sweet (with very subtle acidic undertones), wonderfully succulent, and supremely refreshing, one bite of these amazing fruits will be enough to hook you! The creamy, melt-in-the-mouth flesh is also completely fibreless, meaning they are an easier - and infinitely less messy! - mango variety to devour.
Although their spectacular flavour and great flesh-to-seed ratio mean they are best enjoyed when simply eaten fresh out of hand as a mouthwatering snack, Edward mangoes are also well-suited for use in a number of sweet and savoury recipes. Whether sizzled into jams and chutneys, blended into smoothies, used to add a tropical twist to cocktails, or even paired with fish and meat, these fruits will be the perfect addition to whatever you choose! Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some of our favourite mango-based recipes, including a fluffy mango mousse!
Edward mangoes have the same nutritional benefits as the other mangoes we sell: they are an excellent source of dietary fibre, have a high content of vitamins A and C, and also include a good amount of magnesium and potassium.

Name: Mango - fazli
Description:
Although primarily cultivated in Bangladesh and India, fazli mangoes are adored by fruit fanatics everywhere.
Fazli mangoes stand out first and foremost in their size: they are one of the largest and heaviest mango varieties, often weighing up to 1500g! They are also distinct from other mangoes in that they mature later in the season, which is good news for mango lovers as you can still get your mango fix when most varieties are no longer being cultivated!
However, their tender but firm, orange-yellow flesh has that characteristically sweet mango flavour: as if their delightful tropical aroma isn't satisfying enough, one bite into its refreshingly juicy, almost completely fibreless flesh (which makes them an easier - and less messy! - mango variety to eat) and you will instantly be hungry for more! Indeed, fazli mangoes are very popular across Southeast Asia due to the delicious condiments, jams, and pickles they make. Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some recipe inspiration, including a scrumptious mango and lime eton mess!
As well as boasting a divine savour, fazli mangoes provide many nutritional benefits. In particular, they are excellent sources of vitamin C and dietary fibre, and also contain enzymes that are beneficial for digestion.

Name: Mango - haden
Description:
One of the most popular and widely cultivated mango varieties, haden mangoes are an absolute must-try for all exotic fruit lovers!
Haden mangoes originate from Florida where they were first grown from a mulgoba mango seed in the early 20th century by Captain John J. Haden, a retired U.S. Army officer living in Coconut Grove near Biscayne Bay. The haden is credited with launching the Florida mango industry and subsequently became the parent of many other mango cultivars that have been developed in Florida!
They are medium to large in size and rounded with a tapered end in shape. When they are ripe, their smooth, glossy, green skin becomes an eye-catching red with a golden-yellow blush. Beneath their appealing skin is dazzling orange flesh that will instantly fill the room with its intense tropical aroma, and will delight your tastebuds with its heavenly flavour: the firm flesh is almost completely fiberless, sublimely succulent, and wonderfully sweet.
Although unbelievably delicious when eaten fresh out of hand - the fact that their velvety smooth flesh is nearly totally fibreless means they are an easier and less messy mango variety to eat! - these flavoursome mangoes are also extremely versatile, perfect for use in a number of sweet and savoury recipes. Alongside being ideal for making dipping sauces, sweet preserves, and pickles, they are also well-suited for combining in fruit and green salads, and for adding some exotic flavour to desserts, from sorbets and mousses to tarts and pies! Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some more recipe inspiration!
As well as being versatile and imbued with a spectacular flavour, haden mangoes also possess many nutritional benefits. In particular, they are an excellent source of dietary fibre, are rich in calcium, and contain good amounts of potassium.

Always wash first.

The most famous mango variety in the Mekong Delta, hoa loc mangoes are an absolute must-try for mango lovers!
Vietnamese hoa loc mangoes are named after the Hoa Loc commune (in the Giao Duc district, Dinh Tuong province), the area they were first grown. They are now cultivated commercially on a large scale (over 5000 hectares) in Tien Giang province, with the increased production supported by the Vietnamese government.
These highly-regarded mangoes are plump and slightly elongated in shape and medium to large in size. They have delicate, smooth skin that ripens from green to bright yellow. Beneath their attractive, thin skin is firm, golden-yellow flesh that has a thin seed.
The taste of hoa loc mangoes' flesh is sure to wow you! Divinely sweet, mouthwateringly succulent, and as gloriously aromatic in taste as they are in fragrance, just one small bite of these fruits is enough to hook you for life! Indeed, these mangoes have become renowned in Vietnam for their rich tropical aroma and sweetness. The flesh is also almost entirely fibreless, meaning they are an easier - and infinitely less messy! - mango variety to devour.
Although best enjoyed when simply eaten fresh out of hand, these refreshing mangoes are also perfect ingredients for a range of sweet and savoury recipes. From jams and chutneys to smoothies, cocktails, and curries, you will find a recipe to please all the family! Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some of our other favourite mango-based recipes, including a fluffy mango mousse!
Like the other mangoes we sell, hoa loc mangoes boast a range of nutritional benefits. In particular, they are an excellent source of dietary fibre, have a high content of vitamins A and C, and also include a good amount of magnesium and potassium.

Honey mangoes are medium in size and elongated in shape. When they are ripe, their smooth, glossy, green skin becomes an eye-catching golden-yellow. A unique feature of honey mangoes is the wrinkling on the skin which develops as the mangoes ripen. Beneath their appealing skin is dazzling golden-orange flesh that will instantly fill the room with its intense tropical aroma, and will delight your tastebuds with its heavenly flavour: the soft flesh is almost completely fiberless, sublimely succulent, and wonderfully sweet. Indeed, honey mangoes are so globally renowned that tens of thousands of tons are exported across the world throughout the three-month season they're available!
Although unbelievably delicious when eaten fresh out of hand - the fact that their velvety smooth flesh is nearly totally fibreless means they are an infinitely easier and less messy mango variety to eat! - these flavoursome mangoes are also extremely versatile, perfect for use in a number of sweet and savoury recipes. Alongside being ideal for making dipping sauces, sweet preserves, and pickles, they are also well-suited for combining in fruit and green salads, and for adding some exotic flavour to desserts, from sorbets and mousses to tarts and pies! Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some recipe inspirations, including brilliant mango jam!
As well as being versatile and imbued with a spectacular flavour, honey mangoes also possess many nutritional benefits. In particular, they are an excellent source of dietary fibre, are rich in calcium, and contain good amounts of potassium.
Please note, our honey mangoes turn soft and wrinkly in a matter of days of being harvested. They will arrive to you soft and ready to eat with wrinkly skin.

Looking for a new mango variety to try? Look no further than our keitt mangoes!
First cultivated in Florida, keitt mangoes are now grown in the Caribbean and South America too.
Keitt mangoes are medium to large in size and oblong in shape. They have thin, smooth, glossy skin that has a faint green hue, that sometimes develops a red blush on the sun-exposed shoulder. However, they are also perfect for use in a range of sweet and savoury recipes, from ice cream and smoothies to salsas and curries! They are especially ideal for making chutneys and jams! Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some recommended recipes, including a scrumptious keitt mango sorbet!
As well as being delicious and versatile, keitt mangoes are also nutritionally valuable. In particular, they are rich in vitamin C, dietary fibre, and potassium. Keitt mangoes tend to remain green even when fully ripe - to test if the fruits are ripe, they should be gently squeezed, and if they have a slight give, they are ready for consumption.

Considered the best of the Thai green mango varieties, kiew sawoi mangoes are an absolute must-try for mango lovers!
Kiew sawoi mangoes, also known as 'kiew savoy', are medium in size and oblong in shape. Even when they are ripe, the smooth skin of these slender mangoes remains deep green in colour - indeed, their name translates to 'eat it green'!
Beneath their appealing skin is dazzling greenish-yellow flesh that will instantly fill the room with its intense tropical aroma and is sure to delight your tastebuds with its heavenly flavour: the crisp flesh is sublimely succulent and boasts notes of green apple, oranges, and macadamia nuts. With a wonderful balance of sweetness and acidity, it's not surprising that kiew sawoi mangoes command a high price in Thai markets!
Kiew sawoi mangoes are unbelievably delicious when eaten fresh out of hand - why not follow local Thai tradition and dip them in salt, sugar, and chilli powder to maximise their flavour? These juicy mangoes are also extremely versatile, perfect for use in any number of recipes. They are particularly well-suited to savoury applications: they are ideal for making dipping sauces, sweet preserves, and pickles, combining in green salads, and chopping into salsas! Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some more recipe inspiration!
As well as being versatile and imbued with a spectacular flavour, kiew sawoi mangoes also possess many nutritional benefits. In particular, they are an excellent source of dietary fibre, are rich in calcium, and contain good amounts of potassium.

Name: Mango - langra
Description:
One of the most popular varieties of mango in India, langra mangoes are a must-try for all exotic fruit lovers!
Langra mangoes are medium in size and oval in shape. They are distinct from other mangoes in that their smooth, delicate skin remains green even when they are fully ripe. Beneath their appealing skin is dazzling, tender yellow flesh that will instantly fill the room with its intense tropical aroma, and will delight your tastebuds with its heavenly flavour: the firm flesh is almost completely fiberless, sublimely succulent, and wonderfully sweet, with a slightly acidic aftertaste.
These refreshing, velvety smooth mangoes are best enjoyed when simply eaten fresh out of hand, especially because their nearly totally fibreless flesh (and very thin stone) makes them an easier - and infinitely less messy! - mango variety to eat. However, they are also ideal culinary ingredients, perfect for use in both sweet and savoury recipes. Langra mangoes are especially well-suited to making chutneys, salsas, and smoothies and impart a divine tropical savour to curries and baked goods such as cakes! Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some recommended recipes, including delectable mango sorbet!
As well as being delicious and versatile, langra mangoes are nutritionally beneficial too. In particular, they are excellent sources of vitamin C and dietary fibre and are rich in enzymes that are beneficial for digestion.

Description:
One of the most eye-catching mangoes you can buy, mahachanok mangoes are an absolute must-try for exotic fruit lovers!
Mahachanok mangoes are medium to large in size and elongated in shape. When they're ripe, the smooth green skin of these slender mangoes becomes an eye-catching yellowish-orange with an attractive red blush - this glorious array of colours is why they have the nickname 'rainbow mangoes'!
Beneath their appealing skin is dazzling golden-orange flesh that will instantly fill the room with its intense tropical aroma, and will delight your tastebuds with its heavenly flavour: the buttery flesh is sublimely succulent, wonderfully sweet, and almost completely fiberless. Their central seed is also nearly paper-thin, creating a great flesh-to-seed ratio which equates to more wonderful fruit to devour!
Mahachanok mangoes are best enjoyed when simply eaten fresh out of hand, especially because their juicy, melt-in-the-mouth flesh is nearly totally fibreless, meaning they are an easier - and infinitely less messy! - mango variety to eat. However, these flavoursome mangoes are also extremely versatile, perfect for use in any number of sweet and savoury recipes. Alongside being ideal for making dipping sauces, sweet preserves, and pickles, they are also well-suited for combining in fruit and green salads, and for adding some exotic flavour to desserts, from sorbets and mousses to tarts and pies! Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some more recipe inspiration!
As well as being versatile and imbued with a spectacular flavour, mahachanok mangoes possess many nutritional benefits. In particular, they are an excellent source of dietary fibre, are rich in vitamins C, B1, and B2, and contain good amounts of calcium.

Tab Content:Preparation:
Ready to eat once the mango yields to gentle pressure. 

Wash the mango first.

Quite simply, one can peel back the skin and eat the mango flesh directly from the central seed.

Alternatively, cut long ways along each side of the seed to separate the mango into 3 pieces. With a spoon, scoop the flesh from the two outer pieces. The flesh surrounding the seed shouldn't be wasted! Scrape off with a spoon or eat the mango flesh directly from the central seed. 

You may also use the 'hedgehog' method to prepare honey mangoes - score longways and crossways on the outer pieces and turn inside out to reveal many cubes of mango which can be easily removed from the skin.
Tab Content:Usage: Best enjoyed when simply eaten fresh out of hand - before eating the whole mango, make sure to wash the sap off the skin. The mangoes also freeze really well so you can slice them and bag them, or puree them and store them in ice cube trays in the freezer.
Tab Content:Storage:
Ripen at room temperature.

Once the mango yields to gentle pressure it's ripe and should be refrigerated to prevent spoiling.

 Never store mangoes in a plastic bag in the fridge as they need to breathe.

Name: Mango - mankurad
Description:
Mankurad mangoes are the most popular mangoes in their native Goa - they are lauded as even tastier than 'the king of mangoes', the alphonso mango!
In Goa, these small to medium, oval-shaped fruits are usually the first mangoes to hit the market: their renowned status - there were two mango festivals devoted just to mankurad mangoes in 2018 and 2019! - means they command a high price compared to other offerings on the market stalls.
Their attractive appearance is one reason why they're so beloved. They have smooth, golden-yellow skin that develops a dazzling red blush during ripening. They are famous too for their aroma: it is said that if you store a mankurad mango in your kitchen, soon your whole house would be filled with its distinctive floral scent! However, the brilliant flavour of the deep orange flesh is the main draw of these spectacular fruits. The soft, immensely succulent flesh boasts a wonderful balance of sweet and sour notes and a rich tropical flavour. As well as being juicier than other mango varieties, their pulpy flesh is less fibrous and their seed is much smaller and thinner, which makes them an easier mango to eat!
Although best enjoyed fresh out of hand, mankurad mangoes are very versatile and are therefore well-suited to a number of culinary applications. They are ideal for adding a natural sweetness to your food and drink creation: they are especially perfect for creating smoothies and cocktails (or mocktails), and also make spectacular salsas, sorbets, and fruit salads! Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some of our favourite recipes, including an amazing mango panna cotta!
As well as being mouthwateringly delectable, mankurad mangoes boast a number of nutritional benefits. In particular, they are an excellent source of potassium and magnesium.

In Goa, these small to medium, oval-shaped fruits are usually the first mangoes to hit the market: their renowned status - there were two mango festivals devoted just to mankurad mangoes in 2018 and 2019! - means they command a high price compared to other offerings on the market stalls.
Their attractive appearance is one reason why they're so beloved. They have smooth, golden-yellow skin that develops a dazzling red blush during ripening. They are famous too for their aroma: it is said that if you store a mankurad mango in your kitchen, soon your whole house would be filled with its distinctive floral scent! However, the brilliant flavour of the deep orange flesh is the main draw of these spectacular fruits. The soft, immensely succulent flesh boasts a wonderful balance of sweet and sour notes and a rich tropical flavour. As well as being juicier than other mango varieties, their pulpy flesh is less fibrous and their seed is much smaller and thinner, which makes them an easier mango to eat!
Although best enjoyed fresh out of hand, mankurad mangoes are very versatile and are therefore well-suited to a number of culinary applications. They are ideal for adding a natural sweetness to your food and drink creation: they are especially perfect for creating smoothies and cocktails (or mocktails), and also make spectacular salsas, sorbets, and fruit salads! Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some of our favourite recipes, including an amazing mango panna cotta!
As well as being mouthwateringly delectable, mankurad mangoes boast a number of nutritional benefits. In particular, they are an excellent source of potassium and magnesium.

Ingredients:

  • 2 ripe Neelam Mangoes, peeled and chopped
  • 1 cup plain yoghurt
  • 1 cup chilled milk
  • 2 tablespoons sugar (adjust to taste)
  • A pinch of cardamom powder (optional)
  • Ice cubes

Method:

  1. In a blender, combine the chopped mangoes, yoghurt, milk, sugar, and cardamom powder (if using).
  2. Blend until smooth and creamy.
  3. Add a few ice cubes and blend again until frothy.
  4. Pour into glasses, garnish with a slice of mango, and serve chilled.

Name: Mango - rajapuri
Description:
Rajapuri mangoes are a must-try for mango lovers!
These mangoes from India are one of the largest mango varieties in the world. They are elongated in shape, and have thin, smooth skin that dazzles the eyes with its vibrant green hue. Rajapuri mangoes have the divine floral aroma that is characteristic of Indian mangoes, and their flavour is similarly superb. Beneath the red-blushed skin of our ripe rajapuri mangoes is soft, tender flesh which is sublimely succulent - it truly melts in the mouth! - and which delights the tastebuds with a delectably sweet and tropical flavour, with distinctly tangy undertones. By contrast, the raw rajapuri mangoes, which are harvested early, whilst they are still firm and completely green, are crunchy in texture and have a sour taste. They are thus used to add some fruity crispness to salads and utilised to make splendid chutneys and marmalades, rather than eaten straight out of hand.
The ripe mangoes are best enjoyed fresh out of hand, but are also perfect for use in any number of food and drink recipes. Indeed, they are like other mangoes in being well-suited to both sweet and savoury culinary applications! Why not respect their Indian roots by pureeing and mixing the mangoes with milk or cream and then using it as a delicious dipping sauce? We'd recommend using them to make desserts such as sorbets, healthy smoothies or lively cocktails, or utilising them to add some fruity notes to your curries! Check out the 'Further information' tab below for recipe inspiration.
As well as being flavoursome and versatile, rajapuri mangoes boast a range of nutritional benefits. In particular, they are an excellent source of dietary fibre, have a high content of vitamins A and C, and also provide a good amount of magnesium and potassium.

Tab Content:Preparation:
Ready to eat once the mango yields to gentle pressure. 

Wash the mango first.

Quite simply, one can peel back the skin and eat the mango flesh directly from the central seed.

Alternatively, cut long ways along each side of the seed to separate the mango into 3 pieces. With a spoon, scoop the flesh from the two outer pieces. The flesh surrounding the seed shouldn't be wasted! Scrape off with a spoon or eat the mango flesh directly from the central seed. 

You may also use the 'hedgehog' method to prepare honey mangoes - score longways and crossways on the outer pieces and turn inside out to reveal many cubes of mango which can be easily removed from the skin.

Shelly mangoes have the same nutritional benefits as the other mangoes we sell: they are an excellent source of dietary fibre, have a high content of vitamins A and C, and also include a good amount of magnesium and potassium.

Susu mangoes are best enjoyed when simply eaten fresh out of hand. However, these flavoursome mangoes are also extremely versatile, perfect for use in any number of sweet and savoury recipes. Alongside being ideal for making dipping sauces, sweet preserves, and pickles, they are also well-suited for combining in fruit and green salads, and for adding some exotic flavour to desserts, from sorbets and mousses to tarts and pies! Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some more recipe inspiration.
As well as being versatile and imbued with a spectacular flavour, susu mangoes also possess many nutritional benefits. In particular, they are an excellent source of dietary fibre, are rich in calcium, and contain good amounts of potassium.

Name: Melon - charentais
Description:
Charentais melons are a must-try for melon lovers!
Native to the south of France (specifically the fields surrounding the town of Cavaillon) but cultivated around the globe, charentais melons are small in size and round to oval in shape. They have eye-catching skin: the thin, wrinkled rind ranges in colour from grey-green to pale green, and displays distinctive dark green stripes.
They have a divine aroma, emitting a fragrance that stuns with its honeyed, fruity, and floral notes reminiscent of ambrosia. Their flavour is similarly sublime. Beneath the wonderful exterior is light orange flesh and a central cavity packed with oblong ivory seeds, attached to small white fibres. The flesh is supremely succulent and sweet, although the mild acidity of charentais melons means this sweetness is balanced out, with a notable floral aftertaste. Indeed, their heavenly flavour has made them so renowned in France that they are annually celebrated in the world-famous 'Feria du Melon a Cavaillon', the Melon Fair of Cavaillon, and charentais melons have earned more sufficient regarded to be hailed a speciality variety.
To best enjoy these brilliant fruits, simply remove the rind and seeds, and devour the flesh! However, charentais melons are also ideal for a range of culinary applications - their combination of fresh sweetness and faint sour notes makes them well-suited to savoury as well as sweet recipes. For example, it is popular to mix them into salads; wrap slices of melon in prosciutto; sprinkle thin pieces with salt and lime juice for an appetizing snack; serve them with fish or poultry, and use them to make sorbets. Why not respect their French roots by slicing or scooping the melons into bite-sized pieces and serving with a sweet wine or port? We'd also suggest pickling them so they can be enjoyed all year round! Check out our 'Further information' tab for some of our favourite recipes.
Alongside being refreshing and full of flavour, charentais melons also boast many nutritional benefits. They are rich in vitamin C and dietary fibre, are a good source of vitamins A and B, and provide potassium, zinc, and calcium.
For a snack-sized option, try our baby charentais melons which weigh between 420g and 620g.

Name: Melon - orange watermelon
Description:
Love melons but growing tired of standard supermarket varieties? Our orange watermelons from Murcia (Spain) are just the thing for you!
Orange watermelons are thought to originate from Africa, where they have been cultivated for millennia - paintings dating to ancient Egyptian times show watermelons were highly regarded as a key water source! In fact, it's believed that yellow and orange watermelons were by far the most common varieties of the fruit in existence, with the red flesh melons being a rare mutation.
Given how red watermelons have spiked in popularity, orange watermelons are today a speciality item, only available from select fruit retailers. As such, our website is one of the few places you can buy this amazing fruit in the UK!
These melons are typically small to medium in size, on average weighing around 1.5kg to 2kg per fruit. They will feel heavy for their size - this indicates ripeness. Like other melons, orange watermelons are round or oblong in shape, however they do not display the typical distinct striping which we are used to seeing on the outer rind of watermelons. Instead, there is fine, deep green mottling dispersed sporadically over the lighter green backdrop. You may notice a yellow spot on your watermelon which is the underside, known as the belly. Once ready to harvest the spot turns from white to yellow.
The flesh is bright orange - perfect to bring a splash of colour to salads and desserts! If in season, why not add a yellow watermelon to your basket too - you could easily create a rainbow on your plates with just a few of our tropical fruits! The texture and flavour of the flesh are just as astounding as its appearance: the flesh has a divine crispness and will delight your tastebuds with its supreme juiciness, delicate sweetness, and glorious tropical notes.
Their subtle sweetness makes these fruits ideal for both sweet and savoury recipes. We'd especially recommend using them to make a spicy watermelon soup to bring a kick of heat to your mealtimes, some refreshing watermelon sorbet that will cool you down in the summer heat, and a scrumptious halloumi, watermelon, and mint salad! Check out the 'Further information' tab below for these recipes!
We receive both seeded and seedless orange watermelons from our suppliers across the season, aiming to source the seeded varieties as much as possible.
As well as boasting a mouthwatering taste, orange watermelons provide a range of nutritional benefits. In particular, they are a good source of vitamins A and C, and are rich in potassium, magnesium, and dietary fibre.

Name: Melon - sakata
Description:
Sakata melons from Japan are a must-try for all exotic fruit lovers!
The small size, floral aroma, and delicious taste of these melons mean they are an excellent snack-sized fruit, perfect for eating on the go!
The smooth skin of sakata melons turns an appealing yellow-green when fully ripened, and, unlike most melons, is not only edible but is also thin and as soft as the inner flesh. Beneath this delicate skin is dense, ivory-coloured flesh that will delight your tastebuds with its delectable flavour: crisp, divinely sweet, and juicy (although also slightly grainy, with a texture somewhat comparable to that of a pear), one bite of these wonderful fruits and you'll be hooked!
Whilst they're best enjoyed eaten ripe and out of hand, they can also be used for pickling when underripe. Moreover, they are ideal for use in any number of recipes, from combining in fruit or green salads to blending into soups or smoothies and simmering into jams! In Japan, these melons are also sometimes used to flavour bread and desserts. Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some recipe inspiration, including scrumptious melon and crunchy bran pots, an unbeatable breakfast for all the family!
As well as being refreshing and versatile, sakata melons boast many nutritional benefits. In particular, they are rich in potassium and vitamins A and C, and provide good amounts of dietary fibre.

Sakata melon salad

Ingredients

  • 4 sakata melons
  • 1-2 tbsp. of fresh lemon grass, minced
  • 1 tsp. of fresh ginger, grated
  • 2 tbsp. of lime juice
  • 2 tbsp. of honey
  • 1/2 tsp. of sesame oil
  • 1 tbsp. of cilantro, chopped
  • 1 tbsp. of mint, chopped
  • 1 tsp. of jalapeno pepper, minced

Instructions

  1. Cut the melons in half, scoop out the seeds, peel off the outer yellow rind, and cut into 1-inch pieces.
  2. Place melon pieces in a non-reactive bowl (glass or stainless steel) and add the remaining “dressing” ingredients.
  3. Toss and allow to marinate in this dressing for one to two hours in the refrigerator.
  4. Serve over lettuce of your choice.

The small size, floral aroma, and delicious taste of these melons mean they are an excellent snack-sized fruit, perfect for eating on the go!
The smooth skin of sakata melons turns an appealing yellow-green when fully ripened, and, unlike most melons, is not only edible but is also thin and as soft as the inner flesh. Beneath this delicate skin is dense, ivory-coloured flesh that will delight your tastebuds with its delectable flavour: crisp, divinely sweet, and juicy (although also slightly grainy, with a texture somewhat comparable to that of a pear), one bite of these wonderful fruits and you'll be hooked!
Whilst they're best enjoyed eaten ripe and out of hand, they can also be used for pickling when underripe. Moreover, they are ideal for use in any number of recipes, from combining in fruit or green salads to blending into soups or smoothies and simmering into jams! In Japan, these melons are also sometimes used to flavour bread and desserts. Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some recipe inspiration, including scrumptious melon and crunchy bran pots, an unbeatable breakfast for all the family!
As well as being refreshing and versatile, sakata melons boast many nutritional benefits. In particular, they are rich in potassium and vitamins A and C, and provide good amounts of dietary fibre.

Name: Melon - sugar oro
Description:
A new melon variety for us in 2024, we know our Italian sugar oro melons will quickly become a customer favourite!
Sugar oro melons (also known as 'sugar gold') are medium to large in size and are round to oval in shape. They have textured, greenish-brown skin that's divided by dark green stripes, giving them an attractive appearance. They somewhat resemble French charentais melons, although the skin of charentais melons is usually slightly paler.
Beneath the wonderful exterior is bright orange flesh and a central cavity packed with oblong ivory seeds, attached to orange fibres. The flesh is tender, succulent, and finely grained, and boasts a wonderfully sweet and refreshing flavour.
To best enjoy these brilliant fruits, simply remove the rind and seeds, and devour the juicy flesh! However, sugar oro melons are also ideal for a range of culinary applications. For example, it is popular to mix them into salads; wrap slices of melon in prosciutto; sprinkle thin pieces with salt and lime juice for an appetizing snack; serve them with fish or poultry, and use them to make sorbets. Check out our 'Further information' tab for some of our favourite recipes!
Alongside being refreshing and full of flavour, sugar oro melons also boast many nutritional benefits. They are rich in vitamin C and dietary fibre, are a good source of vitamins A and B, and provide potassium, zinc, and calcium.

Name: Monk fruit
Description:
Monk fruit is harvested in the form of a round, green fruit, which becomes brown on drying. It is rarely used in its fresh form, as it is hard to store.
Thus, the fruits are usually dried before further use and are sold in this fashion in Chinese herbal shops. The fruits are slowly dried in ovens, preserving them and removing most of the unwanted aromas.
The dried fruits are used in the preparation of teas, soups, and as a sweetener for products that would usually have sugar or honey added to them
Monk fruit, whose extract is nearly 300 times sweeter than sugar, has been used in China as a low-calorie sweetener for cooling drinks and in traditional Chinese medicine. We also have a broken shell option, this is just where the shell has split.

Description:

Name: Moringa leaves, fresh
Description:
Moringa leaves have been used in traditional medicine for thousands of years and are still today renowned for their nutritional benefits!
Moringa plants are native to India but are today found in markets around the world. Their smooth, green leaves are very small in size - averaging 1-2cm in length - and round to oval in shape. The leaves have a fresh, bitter flavour that wows the tastebuds with its horseradish-like heat!
With moringa trees being nicknamed 'miracle trees' due to the plant's impressive nutrient content, it's unsurprising that the leaves are so highly prized as superfoods! As well as being eaten fresh, they are also ideal for cooked applications such as boiling. They are often incorporated into curries, stews, salads, and chutneys and are also commonly used as a garnish. However, they are most popularly utilised to make soothing herbal tea. In the Philippines, for instance, moringa leaves are boiled with lemongrass to make a soothing tea believed to possess healing properties. Moringa leaf tea has a taste somewhat similar to green tea, although moringa tea is notably more peppery. Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some more recipe inspiration, including a delectable moringa omelette!
Among the wide array of moringa leaves' health benefits, they are excellent sources of calcium, protein, vitamins C, B6, A, potassium, and amino acids.

Name: Noni (also known as vomit fruit!)
Description:
Noni is a tropical plant native to Polynesia. Not only does it look unusual, it also has a particualy unique flavour and aroma! These small rough-skinned fruits are very pale to honey-yellow in colour when ripe.
Most commonly compared to strong cheese, noni is more often consumed for its health benefits rather than its flavour.
Fresh ripe noni is certainly a fruit that any fruit lover would enjoy trying once but in countries where it grows, it has a regular place in the diet for many. It is eaten raw, with cheese and salt, which is believed to complement its savoury taste. It's sometimes also cooked and eaten with curry, and in Thailand, noni is added to some types of som-tam, a popular salad made with green papaya. Its leaves are used in Thai cuisine too.
Noni drink can be made by either blending the fruits with water or fermenting them. The fermented drink is usually consumed in small doses on a daily basis as a nutritional supplement.
Noni fruits are particularly difficult for us to source as there are few commerical farms, on which the majority of the harvest is used for drink production. Also, noni can ripen and become soft very quickly, making them a challenging fruit to successfully export. We have limited availability of this fruit so if you're eager to try, we would advise purchasing as soon as you see it in stock, as it's likely they wont last long!

Tab Content:Preparation:
Wash first. Once soft, the noni is ready to eat. It can simply be eaten out of hand. The seeds are safe to eat but some people choose to discard them.

To make a traditional noni drink, place the ripe noni fruits in a sealed sterilised jar and leave them to ferment in the sun for a few months. For a quicker and less adventurous noni drink, blend the fruits with water then strain and add natural sweetener if you wish.
Tab Content:Usage: Noni can be eaten fresh out of hand, cooked or made into juice and powder. In some countries, it's also used in cosmetic products.
Tab Content:Storage:
Fresh: leave to ripen at room temperature. Refrigerate once ripe. Ripe noni fruit can be frozen for at least 6 months.

Frozen: refrigerate immediately upon delivery and consume in a few days.

Name: Peppers - padron
Description:
Padron peppers are perfect for adding a kick of heat to your mealtimes!
These peppers are cultivated primarily in Spain, Mexico, and California. Indeed, they're so popular in Spain that since 1979 the town of Herbon has held an annual festival in their honour, with the Festa do Pemento de Padron attracting tens of thousands of visitors every year!
Small in size (usually only measuring 2-7cm in length!) and curved or straight in shape, they have shiny, waxy, wrinkled skin that ripens from a deep green to a bright red when fully mature. Beneath this visually appealing skin is crispy, crunchy flesh that envelopes a central hollow space filled with cream-coloured seeds.
Padron peppers have a wonderful fresh aroma and a delicious flavour. They have a vegetal flavour and are ideal for those looking for a way to spice up their diet, wowing your tastebuds with their mild to high level of heat - they range from 500-2,500 SHU on the Scoville scale, with some peppers being significantly spicier than others depending on growing conditions. To enjoy the most complex flavour they can offer, we recommend waiting until they are fully mature, as they will develop a taste that is both sweeter and more intensely spicy!
These peppers can be enjoyed in many different ways: fresh, fried, roasted, grilled, sautéed... the list is endless! Why not follow Spanish tradition by using these bite-sized 'Pimientos de Padron' (as they are known in Spain) in tapas dishes? Simply sear the peppers in a pan with olive oil until the skin blisters, add a sprinkle of salt and a splash of lemon juice, and they are ready to be devoured! They are also the perfect additions to salads, pasta, and soup, and make brilliant pizza toppings. We'd also recommend battering and frying them to make amazing tempura, cooking them into frittatas, and utilising them in rice-based dishes such as paella. Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some of our favourite recipes!
As well as bursting with flavour, padron peppers also boast a range of nutritional benefits. In particular, they are exemplary sources of vitamins C, B6, and K, and contain high levels of dietary fibre, which aids digestion. They also contain potassium and magnesium.

Name: Pandan leaf
Description:
Our intensely aromatic pandan leaves are an ingredient you should be using in your cooking!
Sourced from Sri Lanka and Thailand, locals in these countries tend to use these fragrant green leaves during the cooking process, as a tool and an ingredient. Although they are not eaten, pandan leaves are convenient tools to carry and wrap food during cooking, as they are large, flexible, and waterproof. They also boast an intense aroma and freshness that enhances the flavour of meals, whether you are steaming vegetables, grilling meat, or baking fish.
We'd particularly recommend wrapping chicken in pandan leaves to recreate a popular starter served in Thai restaurants around the world: the leaves keep the chicken enveloped inside tender and juicy whilst frying, and impart it with a delightful freshness and aromatic quality. Check out the 'Further information' tab below for a recipe for these bite-sized delights, along with a recipe for an amazing pandan leaf and coconut panna cotta, the ultimate dessert!
It is also common to mash pandan leaves with a little water, and then stir the juice from this mixture into your dish whilst cooking - this juice is particularly good at perfuming curries and rice.
Pandan leaves are used as plates too, and can even be BBQ mats. Simply place a piece of pandan leaf on your BBQ, put your food on it, and cook! The leaf will turn bright green and then brown, and will infuse your food with a distinctive savour. Our fresh pandan leaves are also ideal for decoration, adding a visually striking feature to any room, so they are the perfect quirky gift for fruit fanatics!

Name: Passionfruit - curuba
Description:
A member of the passionfruit family, the curuba looks somewhat like a straight, small banana with rounded ends, hence the nickname 'banana passion fruit'. It's yellow to green once ripe and has an orange pulp (with several black seeds) which is often enjoyed with a little sugar.
The curuba is used to flavour meringues, cakes, fruit sauces and gelatin desserts such as 'esponjada de curuba'. Another popular treat in Colombia is curuba ice cream. Because of curubas high pectin content, it is also used to make fruit preserves. It can be used in fruit salads, crepes, yoghurt; in fact, anywhere that passionfruit is used! Our frozen curuba pulp is also ideal for making refreshing juice, the ideal thirst-quencher! Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some recipe inspiration, including a brilliant passionfruit and mango roulade!
Like passionfruit, curuba is a good source of dietary fibre, gained primarily from the seeds. The fruit is also high in phosphorous, niacin, calcium, iron and sodium. Curuba is high in vitamin C and contains vitamin A too.

Name: Papaya - green papaya
Description:
Green papaya is unripe papaya that is usually shredded to make spicy salads, particularly in South-East Asia.
It's commonly used by vegans and vegetarians to create raw salads but meat and seafood can also be added.
Immature green papaya has crisp white flesh with very little flavour. It is prized mostly for its crunch and used primarily as a base for salads, most notably in the Thai classic som tam, where it serves as a bland backdrop for the powerful flavours of chile, lime, garlic, and fish sauce. Tasters characterise green papaya as clean-tasting and like cucumber or jícama.

Name: Pear - fragrant
Description:
Chinese fragrant pears are a must-try for everyone who loves pears!
Fragrant pears have been cultivated in China for over a thousand years, but were only introduced to the wider world in the 2000s. They are a hybrid of two pear varieties - 'Pyrus armeniacifolia', a local Chinese species and the more well-known Asian species 'Pyrus communis'.
At first glance, fragrant pears do not seem significantly different from other pear varieties: they are small in size, round and plump in shape, and have smooth, waxy, and thin skin that is yellow in colour, with brown lenticles and a distinctive red blush.
Yet, as their name indicates, they stand out in aroma. They emit an intense, floral fragrance that fills the room and is sure to wow you! Their flavour is equally as wonderful. Beneath their tender, attractive skin is cream to white-coloured flesh (encasing a few black/brown seeds in the centre) that will delight your tastebuds. Once the fruits are fully ripe, their firm flesh is crisp, succulent, and divinely sweet.
Due to their bite-size stature and wonderfully juicy and crunchy flesh, Chinese fragrant pears have become one of the most favoured pear varieties for eating fresh out of hand. However, they are also ideal for use in a variety of sweet and savoury recipes. For example, you could serve them slightly chilled and pair them with cheese; bake them into tarts and pies, or use them to make revitalizing juice! Additionally, it is popular to poach fragrant pears. Check out the 'Further information' tab below for more recipe inspiration, including caramel pear cookies!
As well as being delectable and versatile, fragrant pears also boast many nutritional benefits. In particular, they are rich in vitamin C and provide a good amount of dietary fibre.

As well as being supremely delectable, comice pears are also nutritionally valuable. In particular, they are an excellent source of dietary fibre and are rich in vitamin C.

Name: Pear - deveci 'honey pear'
Description:
One of the most renowned pear varieties, deveci pears are an absolute must-try for fruit lovers!
Deveci pears hail from Turkey - combining the texture of an Asian pear with the aromatic nature of a European pear, it's not surprising that they are the country's most exported pear variety!
Although they are squat in shape (with no discernible neck), these small to medium pears are heavy for their size due to their high water content - deveci pears have been known to reach an astounding 2kg in weight! They have yellowish-green skin that is thin, semi-smooth, and covered with small brown dots, which are indicative of the fruits high sugar content.
Beneath the appealing skin is firm white flesh that emits a glorious floral aroma and is sure to wow your tastebuds: the almost translucent flesh boasts a divinely crisp and crunchy texture and delights eaters with its sublime sweetness and succulence. Indeed, these pears bursting with juice are so well-known for their sugary savour (with almost no acidity) that they've earned the nickname 'honey pear'!
These wonderfully refreshing pears are best enjoyed when simply eaten fresh out of hand as a healthy snack. However, deveci pears are extremely versatile so are perfect for using in any number of recipes! Used fresh, they can combined in fruit salads or made into coleslaw, paired with meats and cheeses on charcuterie boards, blended into smoothies, or pressed into juices. They are commonly cooked too: like other pears, they are delicious when poached and can be simmered with butter and sugar to create sweet caramelized slices. Check out the 'Further information' tab below for some more recipe inspiration!
As well as being divinely delectable, deveci pears are nutritionally valuable. In particular, they are provide a good amount of vitamin C and dietary fibre.
